News.title: Fury as UN reveals migrants are being granted asylum in Britain even when they may NOT be entitled to it
News.content:
MIGRANTS are being granted asylum even when they may not be entitled to it, UN investigators have warned.

A probe by the organisation’s Refugee Agency found serious flaws in Home Office interviews used to decide who is allowed to stay in the UK.



Officials warned rushed questioning meant asylum was at risk of being wrongly granted to people who do not qualify — while genuine refugees could be rejected.

UN officials examined 60 interviews and cases and found the full basis of an applicant’s claim was still unclear after questioning in nearly a third of interviews studied.



They uncovered a “failure to probe material facts”, too many closed questions and interpreters summarising migrants’ answers instead of translating them fully.

They warned this created a “real risk” of genuine refugees being rejected while others were granted asylum despite not qualifying.

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: “The UN — hardly a hostile witness — has told the Home Office that it is granting asylum to people who are not entitled to it.

“Last year alone 58,000 people were granted asylum or leave to remain, a ten per cent increase on the year before, and the highest number of initial decisions since records began.”

Meanwhile, a Government whistleblower has claimed just one in 100 asylum claims are genuine and many “use the same script”.

The Home Office insider, who has assessed thousands of applications, said he and his colleagues have encountered hundreds of Iraqi Kurds purporting to be in a relationship with the daughter of Kurdistan’s prime minister.



The number is so high that it has allegedly become a “running joke” among officials.

He also told The Times that hundreds of Pakistanis claim to fear for their lives because they are in a gay relationship with the same man.

Multiple claims feature photos of “topless guys in a club with their arms around each other trying to prove they’re gay”.

News.title: Andy Burnham braced for Donald Trump clash as he prepares to hit Israel with sanctions
News.content:
ANDY Burnham is bracing for a fresh row with Donald Trump as he prepares to unveil Israeli sanctions as soon as today.

The PM is expected to impose a punishment package on Benjamin Netanyahu’s government over illegal West Bank settlements.



Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is expected to make the announcement today as Labour seeks to win back pro-Gaza voters it has lost in recent years.

But it risks a backlash from the Americans who are understood to be furious with Britain’s hardening approach against Israel.



Washington’s ambassador to Israel recently blasted Labour for being consumed with “Jew hate”.

Mike Huckabee said: “The Brits have lost it.



“The Jew hate of their government knows no boundaries and knows no facts.”

A Number 10 spokesperson completely rejected the claim.

They said: “We’re committed to protecting Jewish communities in the UK, and continue to engage with community leaders and groups.

“The government is investing almost £318 million over three years to protect Jewish communities, crack down on antisemitic extremism and hostile state activity, and tackle antisemitism in schools, universities, and local communities.”



Mr Trump and Mr Burnham spoke last night about the Israel-Gaza war.

A Downing Street spokesman said: “On the Middle East, the Prime Minister set out the UK’s commitment to working towards peace and security in the region, stressing the importance of the Two-State Solution, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and ensuring that Iran never acquires a nuclear weapon.”

News.title: Brit hols hotspot dubbed ‘Devil’s Island’ as 88 of Italy’s most dangerous mafia bosses and terrorists moved to new jail
News.content:
DOZENS of Italy’s most notorious criminals have been moved to a jail in a Brit holiday hotspot which has now been dubbed “Devil’s Island”.

The group of 88 infamous mafia bosses and feared terrorists has been sent to a new high security wing at Uta prison.



The criminals are among 746 inmates who are forced to follow Italy‘s strictest solitary confinement rules known as 41-bis.

Prisoners held under these terms are forbidden from talking to each other – limiting their ability to run gang operations from behind bars.



The crooks were transferred to the island via two ATR 42 jets owned by Italian police.

Only eight or nine were allowed to board each flight at a time and cops separated them to prevent communication.

Sardinia’s governor Alessandra Todde complained about the move which she said posed a risk to the island’s safety.

The latest decision has nearly doubled the number of 41-bis prisoners in the island to 183 – about a quarter of the national total.



Todde said: “The government has moved in a unilateral and arrogant way, treating Sardinia like the Cayenne of Italy.”

The Cayenne prison – also nicknamed “Devil’s Island” – was run by France off the coast of French Guiana before being closed in 1953.

Earlier this year, hundreds of protesters swarmed the streets of Cagliari, the Sardinian capital, to demonstrate against the looming arrivals.



Todde warned the island’s jails are already understaffed – a factor which was magnified by the escape of a Puglia mafia boss from one of their jails in 2023.

Prisoners are being sent to Uta jail as part of a plan to concentrate inmates serving life sentences into a smaller number of jails, one prisoner officer told The Times.

He said the law favoured them being sent to islands to keep them isolated.

The officer said: “We can’t send them to Sicily because many of them come from there in the first place.”

Italy‘s junior justice minister Alberto Balboni called Todde, who represents the opposition party, a hypocrite.



She said: “The new wing of Uta jail for these prisoners was ordered by a minister in a previous government who belonged to the [opposition] Five Star party.”

Balboni argued claims that families of mafia prisoners would move to Sardinia to be closer to their relatives were baseless.

She added: “They do not do this since you can only visit prisoners once a month for a few minutes.”

In the 1990s, Sardinia started to host more and more mob prisoners following a crackdown on Cosa Nostra, the Sicilian mafia.

Many criminals were jailed on the small island of Asinara – nicknamed the Alcatraz of Italy – off Sardinia’s coast.



This included Raffaele Cutolo, a crime boss from Naples, and Salvatore “Toto” Riina, the head of Cosa Nostra.

Toto was linked to 150 killings and orchestrated the murder of anti-mafia officials Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino in 1992.

Asinara only saw one prisoner escape from its facilities during its 112 years of service before it closed in 1997.

The 41-bis system is designed to entice prisoners to give up mafia secrets in return for better living conditions.

Some human rights groups have criticised the standard of living.



Inmates are locked in nine-square-metre cells for 23 hours per day – only being allowed 60 minutes outside for exercise in a tiny yard.

Conversations are closely monitored by prison guards who are familiar with codes used by mafia heads.

Officers also have to make sure bosses who mix don’t kill each other.

The prison source added: “You don’t want mafiosi from the same organisations together but if they are from opposing clans they might try to kill each other.”

News.title: Laughing gas canisters found in car involved in crash in which two cyclists were killed
News.content:
CANISTERS of hippy crack have been found in a car involved in a crash that killed two cyclists.

The Ford Focus allegedly hit a group of riders from behind, leaving a man in his 60s and a woman in her 50s dead.



The driver allegedly ran from the scene but was arrested half an hour later with his brother.

The pair, aged 20 and 21, were arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving.



A woman, 19, is suspected of assisting an offender.

All three were still in custody last night after the crash in Cobham, Kent, on Sunday.

Hippy crack, otherwise known as nitrous oxide or laughing gas, is illegal for recreational use.

A source said: “Police found a few laughing gas cannisters in the car and the suspicion is they were for recreational use.

“They are investigating whether the driver was under the influence of nitrous oxide at the time of the crash.”

Kent Police Serious Collision Investigation Unit (SCIU) is appealing to anyone who witnessed the incident, or saw the car or cyclists prior to the collision, to contact them.

News.title: Labour’s migration approach reeks of complacency – is it any wonder there is such widespread public fury?
News.content:
Justified fury

IS it any wonder that there is such widespread public fury at Britain’s broken borders?

It suits ministers to dismiss the protests in Portsmouth this weekend as “thuggery”, pointing to the participation of some masked yobs. But the anger of decent, law-abiding folk IS rising.



Voters are in disbelief at reports that the Home Office presides over a system in which 99 PER CENT of the evidence put forward by asylum-seekers is FAKE and often read from identikit scripts.

They are sick of judges in immigration courts granting the right to remain to violent foreign criminals.



Above all, there is outrage that among eight boats carrying 625 migrants on Sunday was a mega dinghy ESCORTED 80 miles to our shores by five French rescue boats and two helicopters.

What is the point of Britain paying £1billion to crack down on people- smugglers in Calais if the French authorities undermine those efforts as soon as the gangs change tactics?



Whatever Andy Burnham may claim, Labour’s approach so far reeks of complacency.

Reeves 2.0

DOES John Healey really think Labour can carry on taxing the country to death and still get economic growth?

Andy Burnham has promised voters the biggest change in 40 years.

But the Chancellor’s first speech yesterday delivered more of the same gruel served up for two years by his predecessor Rachel Reeves.



Moaning about Britain paying the “Truss penalty” is an increasingly tired act, especially as the cost of Government borrowing is HIGHER under Labour.

Burnham and Healey look set to make the same fundamental mistake as Reeves and Keir Starmer: borrowing more while doing nothing to cut welfare.

Yesterday, Jaguar Land Rover confirmed 4,000 job losses and hedge fund tycoon Chris Rokos — who paid £330MILLION in tax last year — quit Britain for good.

Healey’s pledge to make “Great Britain, Growth Britain” won’t ever be more than a meaningless slogan while Labour taxes everything in sight.

Censor alarm

WE cannot afford to live in a country where the Government decides what kind of news is good for the public.



Plans to give the Government influence over which news sources citizens have fed to them by online algorithms have led to the US issuing an extraordinary official warning that Britain would be “facilitating” censorship.

In a world of dangerous disinformation spewing on social media, a healthy free Press is more important than ever.

Ministers forget this at their peril.

News.title: Man, 52, who raped & abused child for four years is jailed after victim says she suffers ‘flashbacks almost every night’
News.content:
DISTURBING ABUSE Man, 52, who raped & abused child for four years is jailed after victim says she suffers ‘flashbacks almost every night’

A MAN who raped and abused a young girl has been jailed for 27 years, after the victim was left “afraid of leaving the house”.

Krzysztof Biros, 52, gave the girl “nightmares and flashbacks” over the sickening four year ordeal.

The predator, of no fixed abode in Bristol, tried to convince the victim she wouldn’t be believed as he continued to attack her.

It is believed Biros also drove a white van during the period of his offending, leaving the victim panicking every time she saw one on the road.





Krzysztof Biros, of no fixed abode in Bristol, was sentenced for eight counts of rape against a child on Thursday 27 August.

His offending first came to light when the victim confided in her parents that she had been raped by Biros.

The man was arrested on April 7, 2024, to prevent further offending before he was charged on April 22, 2025, before he went on trial in August this year.

The judge described the case as “disturbing and harrowing” as Biros changed his pleas to guilty half way through the trial.



He has also been given a Sexual Harm Prevention Order and indefinite restraining order to protect the victim and witnesses.

This also prevents him from having contact with children should he be released.

A victim impact statement read out in court on behalf of the victim’s step-mother said: “She often said she felt guilty about what had happened and felt like a bad person, and I always reassure her that she has nothing to feel guilty about.

“She is often crying when she talks about these experiences, and I give her a big hug when she has finished.



“She would have nightmares and flashbacks almost every night, and would often be afraid of leaving the house over fears of meeting Biros.

DC Joe White said: “The defendant did not admit his guilt until half way through the trial, which put the victim and their family through unnecessary added stress and anxiety.

“He told the victim they would not be believed because they were a child, which delayed them reporting the offences for a number of years.

“This conviction shows that we will take children’s reports seriously and carry out a robust and thorough investigation.

“The strength of the investigation and evidence gathered has resulted in the defendant pleading guilty during the trial and the Judge’s sentence reflects the seriousness of his offending.”

News.title: Haunting details from fiery crash of Amazon cargo plane that killed five as officials describe ‘utter devastation’
News.content:
HAUNTING new details have emerged in the fiery Amazon cargo plane crash at a major airport that left five people dead and five others injured.

The harrowing incident occurred on Sunday when the massive Boeing aircraft overran the runway at Miami International Airport and plowed into several vehicles, including a work van that was carrying a cleaning crew.



“I would describe it in one word as devastating, utter devastation,” Jennifer Homendy, the chairwoman of the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), said during a press conference on Monday.

“You can see on the paved surface tire marks that continues through the grass, there’s debris everywhere.



Homendy said the Econoline van, which was carrying seven people, was completely destroyed.

“The vehicle SUV, you can see airbags, surrounding airbags. You can see components from vehicles, both passenger vehicles and the aircraft itself,” she added.



“Hard to see. I’m sure it must’ve been very difficult for the responders as well.”

Despite the investigation being in the recovery phase, Homendy said NTSB officials are looking at the history of the flight, the crews’ experiences and training, radar data, and aircraft performance.

The chairwoman said the flight data recorder and the cockpit voice recorder were both recovered and are being evaluated.

The cargo plane was about 1,300 feet above the runway when it shot over the airstrip, striking airport equipment, and a cleaning work van that was inside the airport perimeter.



The aircraft then proceeded to rip through the perimeter fence, plowed through a Toyota Corolla traveling on a nearby road, and continued onto a grassy field.

The plane finally stopped near an area where a row of parked Tesla robotaxis.

Dramatic footage showed thick black smoke billowing into the sky as first responders rushed to extinguish the flames and rescue survivors.

Video obtained by NBC affiliate WTVJ captured the moment the pilot jumped out of the cargo plane immediately after the crash.

“It was shocking to witness all of that; then, unexpectedly, we saw the pilot jump out of the cockpit door and run for his life as the plane rapidly burst into flames,” Olvin Henriquez, who drove past the crash site, told the outlet.



“My family and I quickly turned the car around, fearing the plane might explode violently.”

Homendy revealed the Amazon flight crew survived the crash.

They have since been released from the hospital, according to the outlet.



The victims have not been identified.

Harrowing emergency audio showed the pulse-pounding seconds firefighters scrambled to tackle the raging blaze and rescue survivors trapped under rubble.

“The plane is on fire,” first responders are heard saying over radio traffic, according to audio obtained by the Miami Herald.

“The plane is one fire. Put your game faces on guys.”

Firefighters raced to get hoses close enough to the aircraft to douse the heavy flames and smoke pouring from the wreckage.



But the operation was made even more dangerous because the plane’s left engine was reportedly still running.

The live engine prevented firefighters from safely entering the aircraft to search for anyone trapped inside.

Radio traffic reportedly captured crews saying the pilots had told them they could not shut it down because they would need to energize the aircraft.

Firefighters were then forced to flood the engine with water in an attempt to disable it.

At the same time, other rescuers were battling to free seriously injured people from vehicles struck by the cargo plane.



One victim was trapped underneath a vehicle and had to be freed by specialist rescue crews.

Miami-Dade Fire Rescue Chief Raied Jadallah described the operation as a “very complex situation,” with crews also battling an active fuel leak.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Around 200 firefighters and 60 units were involved in the mammoth emergency response, with crews arriving within just 30 seconds of receiving the call.

The NTSB is investigating the cause of the crash.

News.title: I’ve had enough of illegal migrants taking the mickey – anyone caught making a false asylum claim should be sent packing
News.content:
IMAGINE, say, if evidence emerged that 99 per cent of claims for some kind of business tax relief were found to be fraudulent.

The Chancellor would abolish the relief in a moment, and HMRC would carry out mass prosecutions.



Where, then, is the outrage from the Government following the revelations of a Home Office whistleblower, who exposed widespread fraud in the asylum system?

Speaking on the condition of anonymity to The Times yesterday, he claimed: “At best, one per cent of asylum seekers are genuine.



“There’s almost no aspect of the asylum system that isn’t either a massive fraud or just really dysfunctional.”

He then cited the case of “hundreds” of Kurds whose claim to asylum was based on them being in danger of persecution because they had been in a relationship with the daughter of the Kurdish PM.



Either she is the most prolific femme fatale in history or the asylum seekers are lying — and don’t even have the imagination to come up with an original story.

The whistleblower also claimed that large numbers of Pakistani asylum seekers claim to be in a gay relationship with the same man, while Bangladeshi applicants claim to be members of a dissident group but can’t recall even basic details about it when pressed by officials.



These apparent cases of fraud slip through the net, the fed-up insider says, because the officials ruling on them are incentivised to give them the nod.

The decision to grant asylum can be dealt with in minutes, yet a refusal means vastly more bureaucracy.

Apologies if I have missed something, but all I have heard from the Government so far is condemnation of the anti-migration protesters who turned up at Dover and Portsmouth over the weekend.



Chief Secretary to the Treasury, Emma Reynolds, described them as “thuggish and intimidating”.

It is true that no protesters, whether they are anti-migration ones or Just Stop Oil ones, should be blocking roads and stopping people going about their lawful business. Anyone who does this deserves to be arrested and charged with public order offences.

Nevertheless, the Government can’t escape its failures over migration by trying to deflect attention.



The reason the protesters travelled to Portsmouth is because a boatload of 140 illegal migrants turned up, after travelling from near the French port of Cherbourg.

And it isn’t just illegal migrants who are taking us for a ride, but French border authorities, too.

In April, our own government agreed to pay the French £662million over three years to stop the boats, supposedly using drones and riot police.

Yet French officials claimed they had to let the boat sail because it would have been too dangerous to try to stop it once it was in the water.

Andy Burnham’s government keeps trying to claim credit for a fall in the numbers of migrants arriving in small boats over the past year — much of which simply reverses the spike in arrivals during the Government’s first year in office.



Ministers don’t like to admit one of the main causes of the drop: A fall in illegal migrants arriving on Europe’s southern shores thanks to the tough policies of Giorgia Meloni’s Italian government.

She has done deals with African countries to stop boats leaving and sent asylum seekers for processing in Albania,

If there are fewer asylum seekers arriving in southern Europe, there are fewer to travel northwards.

However, with Spain becoming a soft touch under its socialist government, we can’t assume the numbers won’t rise again. We need to be cracking down ourselves.

Action rarely gets taken on false asylum claims because we have a powerful pro-asylum lobby which tries to make out that everyone who gets on a boat to cross the Channel is “desperate”.



They also like to claim that migrants will be an asset to our economy.

Well, accepting large numbers of fraudsters into the country is not going to benefit the economy.

It isn’t just the Home Office whistleblower who is telling us what is going on.

In April, a BBC investigation revealed an industry of crooked lawyers who are charging asylum seekers thousands of pounds, in some cases, to help them pretend to be gay.

One man was told that once he had successfully convinced authorities that he was gay, his wife could get into the country, too — by claiming to be a lesbian.



Then there are the multiple cases of fake Christians who have managed to convince a dopey vicar that they have converted from Islam — like the failed Liverpool Women’s Hospital bomber Emad Al Swealmeen, who turned out to be attending mosque at the same time as going to Liverpool Cathedral.

His case was too much even for our pliant migration officers, and yet still they failed to remove him from the country before he blew himself up.

Sorry, but I have had enough of illegal migrants taking the mickey.

Besides defrauding the UK taxpayer of billions — the asylum system cost £5billion last year, although some estimates put it at £8billion — the liars and opportunists are making it harder for people who are genuinely fleeing for their lives.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Anyone caught making an asylum claim on false information should be sent packing, whatever dangers they claim to be facing at home.



It is time we called out asylum fraud for what it is — and treated it accordingly.

News.title: 'Right-wing thugs branding RNLI 'traitors' is sickening - hero crews have saved countless lives'
News.content:
'Right-wing thugs branding RNLI 'traitors' is sickening - hero crews have saved countless lives'

' The government was right yesterday to condemn “thuggish and intimidating” ­behaviour from protesters in Portsmouth on Sunday after similar scenes in Dover. Anti-migrant rhetoric and online hate tidal wave has empowered hooligans'

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Right-wing thugs branding heroes who rescued migrants off Portsmouth as “traitors” is sickening. Crews at the Royal National Lifeboat ­Institute assist anyone in trouble on the water. They have saved countless lives at sea and deserve our gratitude – not abuse.

‌



The government was right yesterday to condemn “thuggish and intimidating” ­behaviour from protesters in Portsmouth on Sunday after similar scenes in Dover. Hundreds of angry hooligans have been empowered after years of anti-migrant ­rhetoric and a tidal wave of online hatred.

‌



None of us should welcome the sight of men, women and children crossing the Channel on dangerous dinghies. But nor should we fall for the idea that there’s an easy fix. Smuggling gangs know that since Brexit, the UK has no returns agreement with the EU and a limited agreement with France.

‌



Despite this, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood can point to some successes. This summer had the fewest arrivals since 2020. And in spite of the masked thugs, we are and always will be a compassionate country.

Tricky choices

John Healey was right to tell an ­“optimistic story” about Britain in his first speech as Chancellor. The feelgood factor was notably lacking during Keir Starmer’s first months in office.

Article continues below

But the new Chancellor is also right to be under no illusion the country faces a tricky Budget. And we are clear the burden must fall on those with the broadest shoulders. The government has given families some breathing space but there must be bolder action in October’s high-stakes Budget.

Space cadet

Donald Trump’s proposal of a Star Wars-style uniform for his Space Force appears to have missed the point. What looked like an AI-generated image of the costumes appears to have cast Trump’s US as the sinister villains...

News.title: Turkey wildfire: Residents evacuated as flames spread towards homes in Antalya
News.content:
Turkey wildfire: Residents evacuated as flames spread towards homes in Antalya

Evacuations are underway around the Turkish tourist destination, Antalya, with hundreds of firefighters tackling wildfire which is spreading quickly through neighbourhoods

View 3 Images Evacuations are underway in Antalya, Turkey, with hundreds of firefighters tackling the blaze. (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

People have been evacuated as a wildfire rips through a tourist hotspot in Turkey, with flames spreading towards homes.

‌



The blaze is tearing through Antalya’s Aksu district after breaking out at around 6pm local time, with strong winds helping it spread into residential areas.

‌



One house has been completely destroyed, with smoke spreading from the Karaöz neighbourhood, according to Turkish outlet Cumhuriyet. The cause of the fire is unknown.

‌



Around 45 fire engines along with 275 firefighters are now trying to bring the forest fire under control along with the help of nine helicopters and three planes.

View 3 Images (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Many residents have been evacuated while the road running from Karaoz into the centre of Antalya has been closed to traffic due to flames.

‌



A statement from the Regional Forestry Directorate said: "Our teams are intervening from the air and the ground in the spot fires caused by flammable materials spreading due to the energy of the main fire."

Locals have also been trying to stop the progress of the wildfire by building barricades to protect their homes.

One resident Muhammet Özdemir told the media outlet Cumhuriyet: "They told me there was a fire near my house. Both the right and left sides are burning. It came right up to my house. There's nothing left, not even a tree."

‌



View 3 Images Evacuations are underway in Antalya, Turkey, with hundreds of firefighters tackling the blaze. (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Ahmet Karakış, an elected official for the Aksu district, confirmed that people had been evacuated with a house burnt down and fortunately there have not been any reported casualties.

He said: “We evacuated many houses in the neighbourhood immediately after the fire started. So far, one house has burned down completely. Thank God there are no casualties. We are working with all our might to extinguish the fire.”

Article continues below

The fire has spread in different directions due to the wind and has now reached the borders of the Döşemealtı, Kızıllı, and Ilıca districts with further evacuations taking place including at an animal shelter.

Police have told people to leave their homes as a precaution and water cannons are being deployed in the surrounding districts to stop the advancing wildfire while people have are not being allowed exit into the zone.

It comes after a summer where wildfires have ripped through large areas of Europe, including the UK, on an unprecedented scale due to extreme temperatures.

News.title: Far-right Portsmouth protesters target RNLI heroes sparking backlash as police hunt masked thugs
News.content:
'Thuggish' protestors faced an angry backlash today after they branded lifeboat heroes 'traitors' for rescuing a boat carrying asylum seekers in the Channel.

A far right group confronted the Royal National Lifeboat Institute crews on Sunday night in Portsmouth. The crews, who were based on the Isle of Wight, helped a 'mega dinghy' carrying around 120 people which was stranded in the Channel.

It came into UK waters from Cherbourg, near the ferry crossing for Portsmouth, rather than using the usual route from Calais into Dover, Kent. They were saved by lifeboat rescuers who returned to find a group of men in a boat shouting: “How do you feel bringing illegal migrants into this country?”

View 9 Images RNLI volunteers were targeted by far-right protesters in Portsmouth after helping rescue stranded migrants (Image: Barry Williams/PA Wire)

‌



A volunteer in a yellow life jacket told them: “I don’t know; I haven’t brought any in.” The protestors replied: "Look at these guys absolute traitors to this country. Look at the state of you.” Other footage posted also showed people shouting abuse at an RNLI crew on their boat. There were again calls of 'traitors' and 'Yellow jackets, yellowbellies'. A nother protestor described the lifesaving crews as 'scum'.

The RNLI defended their role, saying: "We are a voluntary lifesaving rescue service, tasked in the UK by HM Coastguard to assist anyone who is in trouble on the water. We will rescue those in danger without judgement or preference, as the RNLI has been doing for more than 200 years."

View 9 Images The RNLI has responded saying they will rescue people 'without judgement or preference' as the service has done for more than 200 years

Police have launched a hunt for the masked thugs who injured officers and damaged vehicles during the anti-migrant protests in Portsmouth. They are investigating potential assaults and criminal damage after black-clad activists attempted to block migrants being driven away overnight on Sunday.

‌



A small number of officers were injured and some vehicles damaged during the protest against the small boat crossings in Portsmouth. The man behind the balaclava protest in Dover on Saturday and the protest in Portsmouth on Sunday is said to be Danny Thomas, known as Danny Tommo. He became a close associate of the anti-migrant and anti-Muslim activist known as Tommy Robinson, real name Stephen Yaxley-Lennon. The government has condemned "intimidating and thuggish behaviour" in both protests.

View 9 Images Patriot Platform founder Daniel Thomas, known as Danny Tommo speaking to Reform UK home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf in Portsmouth (Image: Pol Allingham/PA Wire)

People whose lives were saved by the lifeboat volunteers have since praised their actions and defended the RNLI. Marian Boyd, a Conservative councillor who is the mayor of North East Lincolnshire, is fund raising for the charity this year after her life was saved during a yacht race.

She told the Mirror: "From personal experience I was in a yachting race and caught in a storm when the RNLI came out to rescue us. So they are special to me because I was so anxious out there in the mouth of the Humber. It was freezing cold, and I have never been so glad to get back on dry land. We are up in North East Lincs, so the water is very deep and quite a few ships have gone down in the past.

‌



"At sea in a dinghy is very dangerous, you would not want to be out there in a under those circumstances. RNLI rescuers are unpaid. They get calls at all times of the day and night. I do not like the fact that there are so many boats coming over but I would not leave them out there to die."

View 9 Images Life boat jackets left at the scene in Portsmouth (Image: Jonathan Buckmasterr)

She added: "There was a baby on board the other week, and my husband was saying, 'Why on earth would you bring a baby in on a boat like that?' But you cannot blame the RNLI. I remember when we went out, years ago now, it was a fine day with no storm forecast, it blew up without warning. That can happen at any time."

Writing on social media, one RNLI critic stated: “Do not donate to the RNLI. This scum organisation actively aids our traitorous Government in the invasion of this country.” But Andrew Douglas, 54, a boat tour operator who has worked for more than 30 years off the North East coast in Northumberland, described attacks on the RNLI as 'crazy'.

‌



He said: "You do not want people dying. It is their job and that is what they are there to do, the job that they do is fantastic. When it comes to somebody dying, you cannot just leave them. If they went into the sea with such low water temperatures, they would not last two minutes.

View 9 Images RNLI rescuers returned from helping the stranded migrants to find a group of men shouting abuse

"If there is a man drowning, you cannot ignore him because he is an immigrant. To slag off the RNLI for saving lives, it is not British. You cannot have something like that. I think it says something about modern life. Common sense and decency have gone out the window. When you are at sea all the time, you have the RNLI as a safety net. They make a massive difference and save so many lives."

Amanda Martin, Portsmouth North MP, praised the RNLI and emergency services. She added: "They deserve our thanks, support and respect, not threats and abuse. Everyone has the right to protest peacefully and make their views heard. But there is a very clear line between peaceful protest and disorder. RNLI crews are volunteers. They put their lives at risk to help people in danger. They are not political; they see someone in trouble at sea and help them, whatever their background. That is an important principle that must not be lost."

‌



In a Commons statement on the protests in Dover and Portsmouth, Policing minister Sarah Jones told MPs: “Peaceful protest is a fundamental part of our democracy and it must be defended. But so too is the right of other citizens to go about their lives without undue interference, and there can be no excuse for threatening behaviour or serious disruption.

View 9 Images Policing minister Sarah Jones made a statement in the Commons warning protesters who 'cross the line' into illegality will 'face the full force of the law' (Image: House of Commons/UK Parliament/PA Wire)

"Let me therefore make clear to the House and to the country that disorder of any kind will never be tolerated. And those who cross the line from peaceful protest into illegality will face the full force of the law. This government condemnds the intimidating and thuggish behaviour shown by some of the protesters this weekend."

She added that police in Kent and Hampshire have the Government’s “full backing” in taking “any necessary step to uphold public safety and maintain the peace”. Hampshire Police said that violence and criminal damage have no part in peaceful protest. “There is an investigation to identify offenders responsible for any assaults to officers, criminal damage to vehicles or other criminal offences has been launched,” they added.

‌



A National Police Chiefs’ Council spokesperson said: “Policing is committed to upholding and facilitating the right to lawful and peaceful protest, however we will not tolerate these rights being used to commit crime, particularly where that involves causing damage, disorder or serious disruption. Nationally, we have been supporting Kent Police and Hampshire & Isle of White Constabulary over the last few days in their response to recent events in their force areas.

View 9 Images Kent Police and the Hampshire & Isle of White Constabulary have been supported by the National Police Chiefs' Council (Image: Joe Sene/PA Wire)

“Mutual aid is routinely used to mobilise officers across the country to ensure public safety, which was utilised over the weekend. Policing continues to work with partners and the Home Office to develop its tools and tactics in response to serious disorder and has made significant improvements in recent years so policing can quickly and effectively deploy officers and teams around the country if needed.”

The stand-off came after crowds of masked, black-clad men blocked road access to the Port of Dover on Saturday, in scenes which have been condemned by politicians. Questions have been raised over whether police were adequately prepared. Nick Lowles, chief executive of Hope Not Hate, said there appeared to have been a failure of intelligence.

‌



He added: “To have 300, 400 people with balaclavas marching down the streets, stopping traffic. It’s not just good enough. We need to call these people out for their politics and for the type of Britain that they want to see. This is creating a climate of fear among migrants and immigrants, fear among people of colour. I think the government needs to be far more robust in standing up against this.”

The group behind the protests, Patriot Platform, was founded by far-right campaigner Daniel Thomas in July, and he has used social media to recruit supporters. The demonstration in Dover, Kent, brought traffic on routes to the UK’s busiest international ferry and passenger port to a halt, delaying some ferry services and blocking major roads.

View 9 Images Police in Portsmouth today in the aftermath of the protest at the rescue of immigrants on a boat from France (Image: Jonathan Buckmasterr)

Kevin Moore, a former Det Chief Supt with Sussex Police, said: "People have got a right to protest but they should not be assaulting police officers or using fear of violence. There's legislation that says if you're going to have a demonstration you have to let the police know in advance."

‌



A grandfather said he had to deflate his own dinghy to stop protesters taking it on Sunday night. Barry John-Williams, 69, said the protesters were “idiots” and some had offered him money to use his boat. He added: “They were offering to pay me money to take the boat and I said: ‘Look it’s staying there,’ and that’s why I deflated it. What they were going to do with it, I don’t know."

“One of the idiots, I heard him say they thought the migrants might have come in this boat,” he added, referring to his own small 2.7 metre-long dinghy. The dinghy was met by RNLI lifeboats from the Isle of Wight when it reached UK waters, having set off from the Cherbourg area.

It is thought to have made one of the longest journeys of any small boat, and landings as far west as Hampshire are rare. Officials believe it was a one-off rather than new tactics. A Home Office spokesperson said: “We condemn the intimidating and thuggish behaviour we saw in Portsmouth last night. The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy, but it must never cross a line into disorder."

View 9 Images The protests have been branded 'thuggish' and 'intimidating' (Image: Jonathan Buckmasterr)

‌



" This Government is doing the hard and necessary work of bearing down on small boats crossings, with the lowest number of June to August arrivals since 2020," the spokesperson added. Joe Robertson, Tory MP for the Isle of Wight East, writing to the Home Secretary, added: “I would like to take this opportunity to thank the brave lifeboat volunteers from Bembridge who were at sea for over 12 hours dealing with this very challenging situation.

"The RNLI is a charity established to save lives at sea and respond to boats in danger. It is not the job of the lifeboat to police UK waters. Anyone entering the UK without legal right to be here should be deported without delay by the Home Office, but when it comes to saving lives, every life matters no matter where you are from.”

It is not the first time RNLI rescuers have been targeted. In 2021, RNLI volunteers shared experiences of 'vile abuse' on the beach as they returned with people, including young children, in desperate need of medical attention, such as having beer cans thrown at them and people shouting “fuck off back to France”.

Richard Quigley, along with fellow Labour MPs from the Solent region, Satvir Kaur, Amanda Martin, Stephen Morgan, and Darren Paffey thanked rescuers, adding: "This Labour Government is cracking down on the evil, criminal smuggler gangs. Summer small boat crossings have fallen to a six-year low, and we are ending the use of asylum hotels for good. But we’re not complacent. We still have an enormous job ahead of us – but it’s one this government is going to tackle head on."

‌



The RNLI defended their crews, saying: "They handed the casualties to relevant authorities on reaching shore. Due to the large number of members of the public on scene, some of whom had entered the water, several of the lifeboats stayed afloat for some time as a precaution. Everyone at the RNLI remains focused on our core purpose of saving lives at sea."

News.title: London-bound Virgin Atlantic flight with 270 passengers forced into emergency landing
News.content:
London-bound Virgin Atlantic flight with 270 passengers forced into emergency landing

Virgin Atlantic flight VS317 from Bengaluru to London Heathrow was forced to turn back shortly after takeoff and make an emergency landing after the crew found a technical issue

View Image The Virgin Atlantic 787 Dreamliner was forced to turn back (file photo) (Image: PA)

A plane heading for London carrying 270 passengers was forced to make an emergency landing shortly after takeoff.

‌



The Virgin Atlantic aircraft took off from Kempegowda International Airport (KIAB) in Bengaluru (also called Bangalore) in the southern Indian state of Karnataka at around 8.20am on September 6.

‌



The aircraft had not been in the skies for long before the flight crew noticed a technical issue and the plane was forced to abort its journey and return to land.

‌



The crew circled the aircraft for more than half an hour before returning to KIAB where passengers were made to disembark the flight.

A Virgin Atlantic spokesperson said: "The VS317 flight from Bengaluru to London Heathrow returned to Bengaluru shortly after departure due to a technical issue.

Article continues below

“The aircraft landed safely as a precaution and the flight was subsequently cancelled. The safety and security of our customers and crew is always our top priority. We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused to our customers.

“Our teams are supporting those affected and are working hard to rebook them onto alternative services as quickly as possible."

News.title: Michelle Keegan shares rare picture of daughter Palma as she turns 18 months
News.content:
Michelle Keegan shares rare picture of daughter Palma as she turns 18 months

Michelle Keegan has shared a rare glimpse into motherhood to celebrate her daughter, Palma, turning 18 months old.

View 5 Images Michelle Keegan and Mark Wright welcomed their first child together last year (Image: Getty Images for Atlantis The Royal)

Michelle Keegan has shared a rare glimpse into motherhood after revealing her daughter, Palma, had hit a major milestone. The Blame actress gave birth to her first child with husband Mark Wright last March, introducing their little one to the world shortly after.

‌



Since then the couple, both 39, have taken steps to keep her out of the spotlight but the soap favourite couldn’t help but celebrate that she had turned 18 months old.

‌



Taking to Instagram, the mum-of-one posted a sweet snap of the tot faced away from the camera, while wearing a tiny denim dress in front of two wooden plaques, which were personalised with her name and ‘18 months’.

‌



Alongside the upload, which was posted on her story, Michelle simply wrote: “How did that happen?”

View 5 Images Michelle revealed her daughter had hit a major milestone

She welcomed baby Palma with Mark in March 2025, just months after revealing her pregnancy with fans. They captioned the joint post announcing her arrival: "Together we have a new love to share... Our little girl."

‌



The couple first started dating in 2012 and quickly became inseparable, walking down the aisle three years later.

Michelle became a household name thanks to her stint as barmaid Tina McIntyre on Coronation Street - a role she remained in for six years. Since then, she has claimed parts in BBC drama Our Girl and Netflix hit, Fool Me Once.

She is next set to grace our screens in The Blame on ITV, starring opposite Douglas Booth, Joe Armstrong and Nigel Boyle. The six-part series will premiere on September 20 and follows a local town being rocked by a tragic death.

‌



5 View 5 Images She recently spoke about returning to work after giving birth (Image: WireImage) 5 View 5 Images Michelle posted the very rare snap on Instagram

The official synopsis reads: "What starts as a tragic death in the quiet town of Wakestead, spirals into a tangled web of lies, institutional cover-ups, and moral compromise as DI Crane (Michelle) and DI Radley (Douglas) dig deeper.”

‌



Earlier this year, Michelle spoke candidly about getting back to work after Palma’s birth, and how it felt to return to a set after such a huge change.

She told Graham Norton at the ITV Showcase: "Coming back to work after having a baby is quite daunting. The production [crew] were so supportive and I was so looked after and it was like working with family."

While Michelle and co are gearing up for The Blame, it has been claimed that she quit another drama just weeks before it was due to start filming.

‌



According to reports, she was due to appear as a working class barrister in a new series penned by Sherlock creator Steve Thompson, with cameras set to roll from November.

View 5 Images Michelle and Mark have been married for over a decade

However, she is thought to have stepped back to prioritise Palma, with former Doctor Who actress Jodie Whittaker reportedly taking her place instead.

‌



An insider told the Sun: "Michelle was really keen to take on the meaty role, but the heavy filming schedule would take her away from daughter Palma for too long.

“The hours were quite intense and the project was starting straight after her Netflix drama The Woods and she just couldn’t commit.

"She is dedicated to her acting career, but like all working mums has to prioritise being there for her family, juggling work, parenting and being present for Palma."

News.title: Body exhumed in police probe into ‘unexplained’ death of woman in Telford
News.content:
Body exhumed in police probe into ‘unexplained’ death of woman in Telford

Police are investigating the death of a woman in Telford which is now being treated as "unexplained" after a man had been arrested on suspicion of murder

View 3 Images Police at Fenns Meadow Green Burial Ground, where a woman’s body was exhumed. (Image: Iconic Media Group / SWNS)

A body has been exhumed in an investigation into the "unexplained" death of a woman in Telford.

‌



Officers from West Mercia Police went to Fenns Meadow Green Burial Ground near Whitchurch, Shropshire, early this morning (September 7) to recover the body of the woman, who died in 2022.

‌



Images from the scene showed police in hazmat suits and forensic officers working behind a cordon, with blue tents also set up.

‌



The investigation was launched after the force was contacted by Essex Police with information about the death of the woman earlier this year.

A 62-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder in May and has been bailed amid enquiries.

View 3 Images A body has been exhumed amid an investigation (Image: Iconic Media Group / SWNS)

‌



Police said enquiries are continuing and the woman's death is now being treated as "unexplained".

Detective Chief Inspector Lee Holehouse, from the Major Investigations Unit, said police were unable to release further details while the investigation remained ongoing.

He explained: "On Wednesday 6 May 2026, we were contacted by Essex Police after information was given to them regarding the death of a 57-year-old woman in Telford in 2022.

‌



View 3 Images An officer in a hazmat suit at the scene during the exhumation (Image: Iconic Media Group / SWNS)

"An investigation was then launched by West Mercia Police, and a 62-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder. He has since been released on police bail as enquiries continue.

"As part of the ongoing investigation, which is now being treated as an unexplained death, this morning (Monday 7 September) officers have completed the exhumation of a grave at Fenns Meadow Green Burial Ground near Whitchurch, Shropshire.

Article continues below

"The activity at the cemetery is unrelated to the burial ground, but we would like to thank Fenns Meadow Green for their cooperation and assistance while we carried out this complex operation.

"Due to the ongoing investigation we are unable to release further details at this time but will do so when we are able to."

News.title: Brits face ‘major risk’ heat alerts in Spain as tourists told ‘be prepared’
News.content:
Brits face ‘major risk’ heat alerts in Spain as tourists told ‘be prepared’

Spain's weather agency as issued several amber and yellow weather warnings across the country with temperatures hitting as high as 40C in some holiday hotspots

View 2 Images Brits have been warned to expect temperatures in the high 30C range (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Holidaymakers have been warned of extreme temperatures across Spain with the mercury reaching 40C in coming days.

‌



Weather warnings are in place across Spain for extreme heat following weeks of scorching summer temperatures across Europe and the UK.

‌



Spain's weather agency AEMET (State Meteorological Agency) has issued several amber and yellow weather warnings across the country, the Liverpool Echo reports.

‌



An orange warning poses a more serious risk, referred to as an "important hazard". AEMET says an orange, or amber, alert signifies a "major risk", with people advised to "be prepared", take precautions and follow the latest weather information.

Popular tourist areas including Gran Canaria, Andalucía and Cataluña have been placed under an orange warning. Meanwhile yellow warnings are in place for Aragon, the Balearic Islands, Castile and León, Castile-La Mancha, Extremadura, Madrid, Murcia, Navarre and Valencia.

View 2 Images The warnings cover a wide swathe of Spain (Image: aemet)

‌



The yellow warnings are "low risk", but temperatures could reach 36C which is hotter than average for September in Spain.

The warnings remain in place throughout Monday (September 7), with temperatures looking to remain high throughout the week.

Spain is a popular holiday destination for millions of British tourists every year. Many people will still be jetting off to resorts across Spain over the next few weeks to make the most of the final summer sunshine.

‌



In the BBC's forecast for Seville this week, temperatures will remain in the high 30s. There will be a high of 39C on Tuesday (September 8) before a slight decrease to 35C on Wednesday (September 9).

Ibiza is cooler, with a high of 31C on Tuesday (September 8) and 29C on Wednesday (September 9).

While large parts of Europe continue to experience extreme heat, temperatures have dropped in the UK compared to the blistering sunshine we experienced over the summer.

‌



In its outlook for the UK this week, the Met Office said: "Drier and brighter on Wednesday with spells of sunshine. Another band of rain then moves in for Thursday, before drier and brighter weather returns on Friday. Temperatures likely around average."

Temperatures remain around 17C and 18C this week, with drizzly spells and sunny interludes.

September is officially underway, which marks the start of autumn for many. The beginning of a new season often brings about some unsettled conditions.

Article continues below

Some signs that autumn has arrived include the changing colour of the leaves, a fall in temperatures and the arrival of cooler mornings.

According to the Met Office, meteorological autumn always begins on September, 1 and ends on November 30.

However, astronomical autumn begins with the autumn equinox, which usually falls on September 22 or 23 each year.

News.title: Majority of voters worried about impact of climate crisis on hospital patient safety
News.content:
Majority of voters worried about impact of climate crisis on hospital patient safety

EXCLUSIVE: More in Common data showed high levels of concern, with 75% worried about the impact that high temperatures will have on the NHS's ability to treat patients

View 2 Images The extreme dry weather produced kindling for wildfires across the UK (Image: PA Wire)

The public want Andy Burnham to take strong action on climate change to protect kids and hospital patients, new polling has revealed.

‌



After a summer that saw a record five heatwaves and wildfires spread across the country, More in Common data showed high levels of concern, with 75% worried about the impact that high temperatures will have on the NHS's ability to treat patients, and 63% concerned about schools' ability to teach pupils.

‌



Seven in ten of those polled said the UK should roll out solar-powered air conditioning in schools and hospitals, with 37% saying the government and taxpayers should foot the bill, with 22% saying it should be paid for by multinational oil and gas corporations.

‌



Three in four would support installing solar-powered air conditioning in schools and hospitals, while around two in three (69%) would support a new legal maximum indoor working temperature of 30 Celsius.

Brits warned to stock up on days of supplies as UN issues 'supersize' El Nino warning READ MORE :

View 2 Images Andy Burnham was urged to stand up to oil giants (Image: Wiktor Szymanowicz/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

There was also support for councils being required to open free, cool public spaces with air conditioning during heatwaves, backed by 65%.

‌



The survey was commissioned by climate change non-profit Global Witness, who are now calling for fossil fuel companies to pay more tax to fund climate adaptation and mitigation.

Global Witness senior campaigner Flossie Boyd said: “Our schools and hospitals should be keeping people safe, but this summer many of us lost sleep worrying about our loved ones in baking hot classrooms and wards. MRI scanners cut out in the heat, teachers reported classrooms hitting 40 degrees and kids fell sick in sweltering school buildings.

“It’s scandalous that as people’s lives were put at risk this summer, the oil giants turbo-charging extreme heat were raking in sky-high profits, pushing for more dirty drilling and lower taxes.

‌



“If Burnham wants to stand up for families and working people, he should stand up to oil giants, tax them fairly and use the proceeds to fund the climate preparedness Britain desperately needs – like solar-powered AC to protect the most vulnerable.”

BMA council chair Dr Tom Dolphin said: “Health services have seen more patients coming through their doors because of the heat, and this demand, coupled with the outdated state of NHS buildings has made working throughout the heatwaves unbearable for large groups of staff, making their ability to provide safe and high quality care incredibly difficult.”

“While traditionally summer was a time when the NHS services and staff could rebuild and rest, we’re now facing year-round pressures with no let-up – something extreme temperatures are only making worse.

Article continues below

“The NHS urgently needs funding to make healthcare buildings both greener and fit-for-purpose so that they can cope with the rapidly changing climate while not contributing to it.”

News.title: Minister condemns disorder at Portsmouth anti-migrant protest after police officers hurt
News.content:
Council leader Steve Pitt said the decision had caused "needless disruption".

Around 200 people, some wearing masks, confronted police in riot gear after they descended on the Eastney Landing ferry port area, where the migrants were landed.

Police protected a number of coaches parked on a road leading away from Eastney Marina as protesters blocked traffic. A dispersal order was put in place, meaning anyone failing to comply with police could be arrested.

In a statement, Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said a handful of officers were treated at the scene for injuries, none of which were serious.

It said: "Violence and criminal damage have no part in peaceful protest.

"No arrests have been made at this time, however an investigation to identify offenders responsible for any assaults to officers, criminal damage to vehicles or other criminal offences has been launched."

Spencer Wragg, chair of Hampshire Police Federation, said: "I've seen footage of officers being pushed off their motorbikes, I've seen pictures of police vehicles damaged. It appears that the police last night became the target for some of the protest."

Daniel Thomas, known as Danny Tommo - an associate of far-right activist Tommy Robinson - was livestreaming from the scene - where he called for his supporters to "get down to Eastney" and stop the migrants being transported.

The coaches carrying the migrants were able to leave in the early hours of Monday and the Border Force confirmed "individuals from the boat have been transported outside of Hampshire for processing".

News.title: King makes clear Harry and Meghan remain non-working royals
News.content:
The King's letter has been sent to Prince Harry's team, government departments, military officials and Lord Lieutenants, according to Palace sources.

Lord Lieutenants, who are the monarch's local representatives, and government staff are often involved in royal visits and engagements.

This letter makes clear that any engagements carried out by the Sussexes will be in a private capacity and they will not be representing the Royal Family.

It seems to be something of a shot across the bows, making clear that any Prince Harry and Meghan visits should not be treated as royal engagements.

This comes ahead of what are likely to be public appearances by the Sussexes this autumn, as they settle in the UK and support their charities.

The couple have kept a low profile, but the first picture of Prince Harry since coming back to the UK appears to have been posted on the social media account of Tower Bridge Studios in London.

The message from the King emphasises that the position agreed in 2020 when the Sussexes left the UK - the so-called Sandringham Agreement - is still in place.

This ruled out any "half-in and half-out" status, so Harry and Meghan could not pursue their own commercial interests while continuing to be working royals.

"It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of the Sovereign, and are no longer working members of the Royal Family," the letter says.

The letter sent on behalf of the King makes it clear that this remains the case.

"The charitable work of the Duke and Duchess is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity," it adds.

The King's message says that any questions from organisations about the reception to be given to the Sussexes, "particularly where recourse to public funds may be required, should be directed to Buckingham Palace".

Prince Harry and Meghan faced an acrimonious departure from the UK in 2020, which they chronicled in their Netflix documentary.

They established their financial independence in California, including Prince Harry writing a best-selling memoir Spare and Meghan creating an online food range, As Ever.

This summer the couple made a surprise return to the UK, where their children will be going to school.

It's expected that Prince Harry will be supporting his charities, including the Invictus Games, which are due to be held in Birmingham next year.

There have been reports that Meghan is considering a return to acting.

Disputes about Prince Harry and Meghan's security in the UK remain unresolved and the letter spells out: "Any operational security issues should continue to be directed to the relevant police authorities."

Prince Harry has complained about a lack of adequate police protection in the UK, but the Palace says that has to be addressed by the Royal and VIP Executive Committee - known as Ravec - which decides security for royals and public figures.

Palace sources have suggested it was better to make the Lord Chamberlain's letter public, in a spirit of transparency, rather than risk it emerging in leaks.

Prince Harry and Meghan's representatives have been contacted for a response.

News.title: Faisal Islam: Chancellor's attempts to boost vibes may limit tax rises
News.content:
The chancellor may have thought about shifting the venue of his first major speech this morning.

It was an absolute and total coincidence that he chose to make it in the Coventry Manufacturing and Technology Centre (MTC), just a few minutes' drive from the city's totemic HQ of Jaguar Land Rover (JLR).

In the event, no one was pulling punches. The 4,000 office-based job losses at JLR were confirmed as John Healey answered questions a few miles away.

Healey chose to lean into it as an example of the global turbulence against which the UK needs more resilience.

The difference between this chancellor and his predecessor was he also feels that stressing fiscal discipline should instil confidence in consumers, businesses and investors, and not sap it away amid rolling fears of tax hikes.

So the prime minister and his chancellor have been engaged in a conscious attempt to boost the economic vibes - "a new story", as he called it.

In his speech, and in a BBC interview afterwards, this was clear. There are some positive underlying signs from consumer, business and recruiter confidence measures that indicate this message has been heard, although the hot weather and World Cup have also been factors.

The Downing Street duo are trying to maintain this precious commodity of confidence and the promotion of economic animal spirits that have been suppressed by years of political and economic chaos.

"Borrowing costs are too high," Healey acknowledged at the start of his speech. The global rise in bond yields is like a boa constrictor squeezing the Budget maths, slowly and relentlessly, occasionally loosening its grip, but never actually slithering away entirely.

It raises some reasonable questions therefore about how to balance reining in borrowing with protecting mildly better confidence?

The speech did not seem to me to prepare the ground - a "pitch roll" - for significant tax rises, as I heard at the equivalent Budget "scene setters" for the past two years.

"Am I right?" I asked the chancellor on this point. A pause as he sought precisely the right word formulation. "I won't comment. I can't comment. No chancellor can ahead of a Budget I will take and announce on October 28th".

OK, what about the advice from one of the PM's favourite economists Lord O'Neill that the rise in borrowing rates is a golden opportunity to scrap the triple lock?

This lock guarantees the state pension rising each year in line with either inflation, wage increases or 2.5% - whichever is the highest - but some have argued it is unaffordable.

"The prime minister has said, like I have, that we must bring down welfare costs, but we are also responding to the extreme pressure that is there in wider markets," Healey said.

Neither answer was a denial, but nor were they any type of confirmation. Like a stubborn batsman, the chancellor is going to stay at the crease, giving little away, in his case, about next month's Budget.

News.title: Jaguar Land Rover to cut 4,000 jobs over next two years
News.content:
Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) is to cut 4,000 jobs as the carmaker struggles with Chinese competition, US tariffs, and the transition to electric vehicles.

The cuts will happen over the next two years and will mostly affect the head office, which is based in the UK.

JLR's long-term issues were made worse after a cyber-attack last year caused the firm, which employs 43,000 people globally, to shut down production for more than a month.

Chief executive PB Balaji said the firm was "committed to supporting everyone with care, fairness and respect" through the redundancy process.

"The automotive industry faces significant challenges, with technological change amidst intense competition and ongoing geo-political uncertainty," he added.

JLR is hoping to achieve the cuts through voluntary redundancy, with a window open until 4 October, but said it would make compulsory redundancies with less generous terms if necessary. Affected staff will receive an email in the coming days.

The redundancies are being made in an attempt to save Â£1.7bn over the next two years.

JLR is "as strategically important as it gets for the UK economy", according to David Bailey, business and economics professor at Birmingham University.

He said many UK jobs were dependent on its supply chain and the economy as a whole took a hit when the firm closed down production because of last year's cyberattack.

"It's the centre of our automotive industry," he added.

Yet, the car maker has been losing sales to rivals from China, a country which JLR initially saw as a market for growth rather than a source of competition.

In addition, US President Donald Trump's tariffs have hurt the company, which unlike many of its rivals does not have a factory in the US.

In its results for the year to the end of March, JLR said US tariffs and the cyberattack were the main reasons why its sales had slumped by a fifth to Â£22.9bn from Â£29bn in the previous two years.

Ian Robertson, former director at BMW, told the BBC's Today programme that JLR should have copied its rivals and started manufacturing in the US.

"The biggest operation for BMW in the world is in Spartanburg, South Carolina. Mercedes have their plant further south in Tuscaloosa. JLR didn't take that decision early enough in my view," he said.

He also said JLR had been "somewhat late to the party" in terms of electric vehicles.

Jaguar launched the I-PACE, a fully-electric SUV, in 2018. But the electric Range Rover announced last week will be its first electric vehicle launch since then.

Robertson added that Brexit had hurt the firm, despite its factory in Slovakia giving it "some flexibility".

News.title: Self-described 'genocidal racist monster' jailed after BBC investigation
News.content:
"That bubble subsequently popped and he now has to take responsibility for those actions."

Sentencing Webster to two years, Judge Anthony Potter said he had been given numerous opportunities to show remorse and change his behaviour.

"Talk is very very cheap," he told Webster. "It has allowed you to escalate your offending and propagate the most harmful views.

"I cannot accept that there is a realistic prospect of rehabilitation in the community. I'd be failing in my public duty if I didn't send you to custody."

Frank Ferguson, the Chief Crown Prosecutor for the CPS, said inciting racial hatred was a "very serious offence" which went "beyond any debate about freedom of speech."

"Expressing a wish for people to be killedâ¦ Jewish people, Muslim people, black people, south-asian people, immigrants and LGBTQ+ community as wellâ¦ and encouraging other people to express similar views.

"It's not just about what he might do, it's what he might be encouraging others to do by his words," he said.

Det Ch Supt Alison Hurst, Head of Counter Terrorism Policing for the West Midlands, said Webster had been investigated previously for racially aggravated offences and thanked BBC Wales for bringing him to their attention again.

"Parts of the evidence from that documentary has been presented to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), which has led to the prosecution and sentencing," she said.

Webster was given a two-year sentence, where he'll serve half in prison and a year on licence.

If you or someone you know has been affected by the issues raised in this story, information about available help and support can be found via BBC Action Line.

News.title: New videos of man at centre of 9/11 lawsuit reveal links to extremists and Saudi state
News.content:
The man at the heart of a $1 trillion (Â£733bn) lawsuit brought by 9/11 families had extensive links to Saudi government officials and went paintballing with one of al-Qaeda's future leaders, video obtained by the BBC reveals.

The footage, which the FBI had within days of the 2001 attacks, stands in stark contrast to Omar al-Bayoumi's 25 years of denials that he was an extremist and a Saudi spy.

Bayoumi, who claimed to be a student when he was in the United States, is seen in one clip embracing Anwar al-Awlaki, who would go on to lead al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula. In another, Bayoumi and Awlaki are paintballing near San Diego with an official from Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Islamic Affairs.

The videos form part of the 9/11 families' lawsuit against Saudi Arabia and have never been shown publicly before.

The lawsuit argues Saudi Arabia was complicit in the attacks and that Bayoumi aided two of the 19 hijackers who flew planes into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon - with another crashing in Pennsylvania.

Bayoumi was arrested in the UK by the Metropolitan Police days after the attacks and the videos were found among his possessions, along with other crucial evidence.

This included a diagram of a plane with a flight descent equation written alongside.

Multiple FBI agents received copies of the diagram, but it was never shared with the British interrogators, even though it had been couriered to the police station where Bayoumi was being held in custody.

The diagram was also kept from some FBI agents investigating Bayoumi, as well as from the 9/11 Commission - the independent inquiry into the largest mass murder in US history, in which nearly 3,000 people were killed. Bayoumi was never prosecuted.

He and the Saudi government did not respond to the BBC's requests for comment, but both have always denied any involvement in, or prior knowledge of, the attacks. The FBI declined to comment.

After a judge ruled the lawsuit could go ahead in 2018, thousands of documents, as well as videos and photographs, have been released to the court and also declassified through an executive order made by former President Joe Biden.

BBC Panorama and Radio 4 have examined these documents, and spoken to dozens of special agents and investigators, to trace the evidence the FBI gathered about Bayoumi and Saudi Arabia's alleged involvement in 9/11 - and to understand why it was never fully pursued over 25 years.
