Thank you for your feedback.

Talking points

Borussia Dortmund have maximum points, thanks to a remarkable comeback at Hoffenheim. Remarkable, because they should have been three or four down rather than just 2-0, before Serhou Guirassy and Fábio Silva brought them level and Ethan Nwaneri, on his debut, engineered an unlikely winning own goal by Albian Hajdari. Credit too to the newly-adventurous Niko Kovac for sending on the Arsenal loanee for the injured centre-back Filippo Mané and Silva for midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas.

View image in fullscreen Ethan Nwaneri celebrates his part in Albian Hajdari’s own goal. Photograph: Heiko Becker/Reuters

BVB are only third, though. Augsburg lead the pack after coming back from a half-time deficit to eventually demolish a woeful Eintracht Frankfurt in Sunday’s late game, and Freiburg sit second after their single-goal win at Paderborn. Meanwhile Elversberg wowed this week too, recovering from 3-1 down at Borussia Mönchengladbach to win via Maurice Krattenmacher’s stoppage-time winner (his second goal) to make them the fourth team with two wins from two.

Cheers also for Jarell Quansah, impressing as a rampaging right-back in Leverkusen’s 4-0 hammering of Union Berlin, their first points of the season, and Niclas Füllkrug scoring (already) header of the season in Werder Bremen’s surprise 3-1 win over Leipzig.

Sports.title: Aubameyang rolls back years as revamped ‘Super Dépor’ return to La Liga in style | Billy Munday
Sports.content:
Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang was already the best player on the pitch when he ran through to score Deportivo A Coruña’s winner on Saturday night. It was certainly not Ilias Akhomach, the Villarreal substitute whose pass on halfway had inadvertently played Aubameyang through, nor Sergi Cardona, the intended target of that pass. After 89 minutes and two assists, the 37-year-old Aubameyang raced the length of the half to slot past Luiz Júnior to make it 3-2.

It had been a similar case the week before, when Aubameyang’s pace left the Valencia defenders behind before he dinked the ball over the goalkeeper. The week before that, he calmly rounded Málaga’s Alfonso Herrero before opening the scoring. The week before that, the former Barcelona striker marked his return to La Liga against Elche with a superb touch and finish from Lorenzo Amatucci’s diagonal pass. Scoring in each of his first four games for Deportivo is a club record, eclipsing Bebeto’s fast start of three in a row from 1992.

Like Aubameyang, Deportivo appear reborn. “Super Dépor” were Spain’s most popular team around the turn of the century, with Bebeto having helped them win the Copa del Rey in 1995. Djalminha, Roy Makaay and the rest inspired them to a first league title in 2000, followed by another Copa del Rey in 2002 and a run to the Champions League semi-finals in 2004. After the money dried up, they were relegated from the top flight in 2011, 2013 and again in 2018, only returning this summer after eight years away.

The former Arsenal striker Lucas Pérez returned for a fourth stint to help Dépor climb out of the third tier two years ago. Aubameyang now has his sights on the club record of scoring in seven consecutive league matches, held by Pérez and Bebeto from different eras. It was another former Arsenal forward in Nicolas Pépé who broke the deadlock for Villarreal at the Estadio de la Cerámica on Saturday, with their new head coach, Iñigo Pérez, still searching for his first victory since leaving Rayo Vallecano.

At the start of the week, Pérez was preparing to face a very different Deportivo squad. By the weekend, it included the deadline-day arrivals of José María Giménez from Atlético Madrid and Marc Casadó from Barcelona. Deportivo’s equaliser at Villarreal came when Giménez stepped out from centre-back and slid the ball into the box for Aubameyang to chase. He clipped it into the middle with the outside of his boot, Luismi Cruz finishing first-time.

The signings of Giménez and Casadó – both on loan, both two-time La Liga winners – are a coup for Deportivo, even after an ambitious window where they spent €26m (£22.3m) on new players – only Barcelona, Real Madrid, Atlético and Real Betis have spent more.

View image in fullscreen Marc Casadó (right) – a loan arrival at Deportivo – tries to curtail Tajon Buchanan’s progress. Photograph: Mateo Villalba/Getty Images

Investment and debt-clearing at the club have gone hand in hand since the Galician bank Abanca became the majority shareholder in 2020, when Dépor were relegated to the third tier during the Covid pandemic. Abanca now owns 99.99% of the club, but the fans still have a voice. Supporters voted this summer to change the team’s name from Deportivo de “La Coruña” to the Galician version “A Coruña”.

The investment in all areas of the club has paid off. When given a guided tour of the training ground alongside Giménez, Casadó was impressed with the facilities. “It’s better than Barça,” he said, deadpan, on camera. “Seriously.”

Adama Traoré has arrived too, after a chat with his former Barcelona teammate Aubameyang, on a free. Antonio Hidalgo, who guided Deportivo back to La Liga in his first season in charge, deployed debutant Traoré as a wing-back off the bench on Saturday. When Gerard Moreno crossed for Tajon Buchanan at the back post, Traoré scrambled to get back into position but comically looped a header over his own goalkeeper to gift Villarreal the lead again on 76 minutes.

The influx of new players has brought with it concerns about the crop that got Dépor promoted in the first place. But where many thought Aubameyang might replace the bustling striker Bil Nsongo, the pair – 16 years apart in age – are now forming a fearsome partnership. Deportivo scouted Nsongo when he was playing for Canon Youandé in his native Cameroon but decided not to extend his contract after his first year with the B team. He was insistent though, having made A Coruña his home, and won the club over. “He was very interested in staying here,” said Deportivo’s academy director, Ismael Arilla.

Deportivo’s second equaliser came from another striker: Zakaria Eddahchouri, whose 18 months in A Coruña have been marked by his significant contribution to promotion and the time he fell over the top of the waterfront while taking a selfie last year. Firefighters had to rescue the Dutchman from the rocks below and he spent the night in hospital with minor injuries. After 12 goals in the second tier last season, his first in the top flight was drilled past Júnior at the near post after Aubameyang found him with a well-weighted pass.

View image in fullscreen Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has scored in each of Deportivo’s first four games this season – a club record. Photograph: Maria Jose Segovia/DeFodi Images/Shutterstock

There is no overstating the importance of Aubameyang since his €1.5m arrival from Marseille – in goals, ambition and willingness to mentor younger players. “He has a special talent but you should see him train, how involved he is, how it rubs off on his teammates,” said Hidalgo at full-time after the veteran’s late winner. But it’s also the little things: “His smile is infectious.” The front flip celebrations are a sight, too.

The “brutal” victory, as Hidalgo put it, against opponents who begin their Champions League campaign on Tuesday, moves Deportivo into the top five and keeps them unbeaten, but the former Sabadell, Sevilla B and Huesca coach is not getting ahead of himself. “The table that tells you where you’re at is the one on the final day of the season – now it’s just for looking at.”

Quick Guide La Liga results Show La Liga results Real Betis 1-0 Real Madrid, Athletic 3-0 Atlético Madrid, Rayo Vallecano 3-2 Racing Santander, Villarreal 2-3 Deportivo La Coruña, Valencia 0-5 Barcelona, Alavés 5-2 Osasuna, Málaga 0-0 Levante, Espanyol 1-1 Sevilla Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Talking points

José Mourinho congratulated Real Betis for “playing for a draw and then winning the lottery” after his first defeat back as Real Madrid coach. Troy Parrott, given his professional debut by Mourinho at Tottenham, scored his first Betis goal in Friday’s 1-0 win at La Cartuja. Mourinho slumped in his chair as VAR spotted an offside in Carlos Espí’s acrobatic equaliser before Kylian Mbappé had a stoppage-time penalty saved by Álvaro Valles, leaving Barcelona to extend their lead over Madrid to three points with a 5-0 rout of Valencia on Sunday. Luck of the Irish?

Sandwiched between Barça and Madrid are Alavés, who have won three of their first four games. The former Real Madrid striker Mariano Díaz, who spent over a year as a free agent before signing in 2025, scored his third goal in four games during a 5-2 victory against Osasuna on Sunday. He was upstaged by Lucas Boyé, whose hat-trick included an absolute belter from 35 yards out. “I didn’t even think about it,” the Argentinian striker said.

View image in fullscreen Lucas Boyé (left) wheels away after scoring Alavés’ third goal – his second of a hat-trick in a 5-2 win over Osasuna. Photograph: Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images

One Argentina striker who is having considerably less fun is Julián Álvarez. Atlético were 2-0 down at Athletic Bilbao on Saturday by the time he entered the field to whistles from the travelling supporters. Nico Williams and Robert Navarro scored two in three minutes after the restart and Oihan Sancet added a late third. Diego Simeone opted not to comment on Álvarez not doing his post-match warm-down with the other substitutes.

Sports.title: Danny Murphy: Liverpool duo are Andoni Iraola’s biggest problem, they aren’t good enough and this is where they’re really poor
Sports.content:
Danny Murphy: Liverpool duo are Andoni Iraola’s biggest problem, they aren’t good enough and this is where they’re really poor

Danny Murphy believes Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez are the two biggest problems in Andoni Iraola's Liverpool team.

The Reds splashed out around £80million on the duo in the summer of 2025, but the transfers are yet to work out.



4 Murphy believes Iraola's full-backs are Liverpool's weak links Credit: Getty

A lot of stick has come the way of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz due to their price tags.

However, it is the full-back duo who Murphy is more concerned about.

When asked about Isak and Wirtz, Murphy said on Kick Off: "The bigger problem for Liverpool because at times at Anfield, they are going to dominate the ball so much that the press isn't going to be that important.

"The bigger problem is that the full-backs aren't good enough at Liverpool. They are not good enough.



"They are not going to get better, it is not in them.

"They are 100mph. They are working hard but their level of crossing and choice of final pass is really poor.

"It looks worse for the Liverpool fans when you have been so used to seeing two of the best we've ever seen in Andy Robertson and Trent Alexander-Arnold, in terms of assists, quality and picking the final pass.



"They have brought in two full-backs, who aren't as good. I think they are okay defensively, not brilliant, but they are okay.

"And going forward, the best teams have really good full-backs on the ball because teams clog up the middle of the pitch, so the space is wide.



"Your full-backs get so much of the ball, and Frimpong and Kerkez just don't have that quality that you need to open up teams."

4 Frimpong started Liverpool's first two Premier League games, but began on the bench for their most recent outing Credit: Getty

4 Kerkez worked under Iraola at Bournemouth, but has made a shaky start to the season Credit: Getty

Frimpong's issues

During his time in Germany with Bayer Leverkusen, Frimpong scored 30 goals and provided 44 assists in 190 games.



He became one of the best prospects on the market when it came to wing-backs, with the Dutchman a key part of the Xabi Alonso team that went a whole domestic campaign unbeaten to claim two trophies.

However, he was largely played as just a wing-back throughout his time with Leverkusen, and Liverpool don't use wing-backs.

On Friday, he was dropped for Ronald Araujo, and after the match, Andoni Iraola said: “With Ronald, the thinking was about Fatawu swinging crosses into the box and Ipswich puts a lot of balls in.

“Those crosses and second balls, and also set pieces, I felt that Ronald could help us. He was very important.



“We will need Jeremie Frimpong when we need to be more offensive and others we will need Ronald. We will take that decision according to the game.”

4 Iraola might have a decision to make regarding his full-backs Credit: AFP

Gabby Agbonlahor believes that Dominik Szoboszlai should play at right-back over Frimpong.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, he said: "If you've got [Ryan] Gravenberch on the bench last week against Forest - Gravenberch comes in with [Alexis] McAllister in that midfield and [Florian] Wirtz.



"And it just makes sense, because Frimpong does not have the quality and he's never going to have the quality.

"He’s a wing-back, not a full-back."

Kerkez's struggles

Hungary international Kerkez made his name at Bournemouth as a flying left-back, who epitomised Iraola's intense and aggressive football.

An outstanding 2024/25 season earned his move to Anfield.

Under Arne Slot, the Dutchman appeared reluctant to initially let him off the leash, and so many players struggled for Liverpool last year.

Iraola is now the Liverpool head coach and has started Kerkez in all three Premier League games so far.



But even he has struggled still to replicate that form from his time on the south coast.

Speaking after the win over Ipswich, he said: “[Milos] Kerkez had a difficult game against [Abdul] Fatawu but he was very aggressive and I liked his game."

There is still quite a while until the January transfer window, so plenty of time for both to show improvement, but Murphy is basically writing them off.

Sports.title: Ashley Williams lands first coaching role six years after retirement from football
Sports.content:
Ashley Williams lands first coaching role six years after retirement from football

Former Wales international Ashley Williams will take on his first coaching position as an assistant with the national team.

Williams captained the Wales side that famously reached the semi-finals of Euro 2016, scoring the Dragons' equaliser in the memorable quarter-final win over Belgium.

2 Williams scored one of Wales' most iconic goals ever Credit: Getty

The 42-year-old will work alongside ex-Swansea City boss Alan Sheehan under Wales head coach Craig Bellamy.

The return of a Wales legend

Williams earned 86 caps in total, making him the Wales' joint sixth most-capped player of all time.

A centre-back, he started out at non-League Hednesford Town before going on to make over 350 appearances for Swansea, the majority of them in the Premier League.

Having won promotion with the club from League One and the Championship, Williams captained Swansea to their first major trophy as they lifted the League Cup in 2013.

The 2009 Welsh Footballer of the Year later spent two years with Everton.

His other clubs were Stockport County, Stoke City and Bristol City – for whom he made his final career appearance in 2020.

Since announcing his retirement in 2021 at the age of 36, Williams has turned to media work.

A pundit for the BBC and Sky Sports, he's also a regular on talkSPORT.

Wales back in action with quadruple-header

Williams will link up with Wales ahead of the next international break at the end of this month.

Bellamy's side play four Nations League fixtures in the space of 12 days, beginning with Portugal away on Thursday September 24.

2 Williams and Bellamy's international careers overlapped Credit: Getty

They then travel to and host Denmark either side of a home clash against Norway.

Bellamy took charge of the national team in July 2024, succeeding Rob Page, who was sacked from his post.

His current contract is due to expire after Euro 2028, where the Dragons will be hoping to be involved after missing out on qualification for this year's World Cup.

And there's even more riding on those Euros: the tournament is being co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

However, with spots in the finals only guaranteed for up to two host nations, all four co-hosts will go through the normal qualification route.

The draw for Euro 2028 qualifying is scheduled to take place in Belfast on December 6.

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid star to miss Liverpool clash due to red card suspension earned two years ago
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid are set to be without Arnau Ortiz for their Champions League opener against Liverpool.

The Spanish giants head to Merseyside once again in a repeat of one of the League Phase contests last year, but Ortiz can't play due to a red card from August 2024.



3 Liverpool came out on top the last time these sides met thanks to a Virgil van Dijk stoppage-time winner Credit: Getty

Ortiz was playing for Polish side Slask Wroclaw, and they were playing a Conference League tie against Swiss outfit St Gallen.

The 24-year-old came on in extra time after a great comeback from his team to make the match 3-3 on aggregate.

He was booked for diving before receiving a second yellow for protesting about the decision.



Since then, Ortiz hasn't played in any European competition or involved with a team in Europe as Slask Wroclaw were knocked out.

As a result, he serves his one match ban at Anfield.

Ortiz joined Atletico Madrid's second team in the summer of 2025 from Slask Wroclaw after initially heading to Poland from Girona in 2024.



But after a stunning year last season for the B team, he's been promoted to be part of Diego Simeone's squad.

Ortiz scored 23 goals and provided six assists, and has made three LaLiga appearances so far.



He actually started the 2-0 win over Malaga on the opening weekend before appearing as a substitute against Sevilla and Athletic Club.

Simeone has actually been deprived of someone who had a good chance of playing some role in the game.

3 Simeone has enjoyed a mixed bag at Anfield Credit: Getty

3 Ortiz will have to wait to make his Champions League debut Credit: Getty



Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid

Last season, this match ended in a 3-2 win for Liverpool as Virgil van Dijk scored a late winner.

But it has been the scene of heartbreak for the Reds as well.

Perhaps the most famous being the Champions League meeting just before the COVID pandemic in which Atletico ended the Reds' hopes of winning it again after success the year before.

New Liverpool signing Bradley Barcola, a two-time winner of the Champions League, could make his first start for the Reds.

The France international made his debut for Liverpool last Friday as he came on in the second half of a win at Ipswich Town.



Speaking after the 2-0 win over Ipswich, Andoni Iraola said: "Bradley hadn't played a single minute since the World Cup so we needed to be careful.

"He is training well, in a good place, and I think that he has helped us. Probably, we haven't found him in a couple of situations where I think he was going against the 'keeper, but we haven't really seen his movements.

"He has had a very good counter, very good passing side. He was always a threat.

"When he carries the ball, I think you can feel this threat and I'm happy because I think 30 minutes is going to be good for his fitness, for his build-up, and we will continue because now we play a lot of games, so he will have a chance to play more."



talkSPORT will have live commentary of the match with Andy Gray making his return to UK broadcasting as part of the team.

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea forward Bertrand Traore signs for EFL club a week after deadline day
Sports.content:
Wolves have announced the signing of former Chelsea forward Bertrand Traore.

The 31-year-old Burkina Faso captain joins the Championship club on a free transfer, six days after the transfer window closed, after leaving Sunderland at the end of his contract this summer.

2 Wolves are the ninth club of Traore's career Credit: Getty

Traore's next chapter

Traore made 12 Premier League appearances as Sunderland finished seventh last season to qualify for the Europa League.

A versatile attacking player, Traore arrives at Wolves as they aim to mount a promotion push following relegation from the top flight last term.

Now managed by Cesar Peixoto, Wolves sit ninth in the Championship table having won two and drawn two of their opening five games.

Wolves are in action away to Sheffield United on Sunday, though that game may come too soon for Traore to make his debut.

The club's executive chairman Nathan Shi confirmed that Traore will need to get back up to speed.

"He needs time to get fit because he’s been working alone, and he needs time to know our idea of the game, but he is another option to help us fight to get to the Premier League," Shi said.

"Like we saw on Sunday, the Championship is very tough, so we need two players in each position to manage the games."

Born in Burkina Faso, Traore spent time in the youth system of French club Auxerre before moving to Chelsea shortly after his 18th birthday.

After a goal-laden loan spell with Dutch side Vitesse, he played 16 first-team games for the Blues, mostly under Guus Hiddink in the 2015/16 campaign, scoring four goals – three of which came in back-to-back appearances, all of them ending in 5-1 wins for Chelsea.

Another fruitful loan stint in the Netherlands followed, this time with Ajax, before Traore left Stamford Bridge permanently to join Lyon in 2017.

2 Traore scored two Premier League goals for Chelsea Credit: AFP

After three seasons in Ligue 1, he returned to the Premier League to sign for Aston Villa, where he was a regular in 2020/21, netting seven times in 36 league outings.

However, opportunities were harder to come by in subsequent campaigns and, after spending time on loan with Turkish outfit Istanbul Basaksehir, Traore departed Villa Park for Villarreal in 2023.

A return to Ajax followed before he was snapped up by Sunderland last summer following their return to the top flight.

Captain of his country

At international level, Traore is one of Burkina Faso's most-capped players and leading scorers, representing them 91 times and bagging 22 goals.

Having made his senior international debut aged just 15 in 2011, he helped his country to third place at the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations.

Traore's is the cousin of Shakhtar Donetsk forward and fellow Burkina Faso international Lassina Traore.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League star delivers ambitious invite to Raheem Sterling, Jadon Sancho and other free agents to join second tier club
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League star delivers ambitious invite to Raheem Sterling, Jadon Sancho and other free agents to join second tier club

Jonjo Shelvey has offered a surprising career lifeline to Raheem Sterling, Jadon Sancho and other players still without a club.

The former Liverpool, Swansea and Newcastle midfielder is the manager of Dubai-based Arabian Falcons.

4 Shelvey is on a recruitment drive for his new club Credit: Arabian Falcons FC

The Falcons are a young club having only been founded in 2023, and they currently play in the UAE Second Division League, which is the second tier of UAE football.

The six-cap former England international has been joined by ex-Crystal Palace and Southampton forward Jason Puncheon as director of football.

And in his squad, he can call upon Premier League winner Danny Simpson and Ravel Morrison, who was once tipped to be a world-class player.

When asked if any of the high-profile free agents had expressed interest, Shelvey told Hawksbee and Jacobs: "There are a couple that have got in touch.

"I don't really deal with that side of it. I am trying to manage the team because I want to get promoted this year.

"But it is a fantastic opportunity for people if that is what they are looking for at this stage of their career, or if they are struggling to get a club.

"Once the UK window shuts, you are scrambling for clubs, so we put out a call to see if there was anyone who was interested.

"There are no strings attached to it. They can leave and go to bigger clubs whenever they are ready.

"But we can offer that Dubai lifestyle, and bigger names are coming out here.

"The window is open until the end of September, so the option is there for these players to join or even come and train with us."

4 Sterling is still waiting to find a new club after a short-term deal at Feyenoord came to an end Credit: Getty

4 Sancho is another English player who is looking for a new club and a chance to rebuild his career Credit: Getty

Shelvey's managerial leap

The 34-year-old became the Falcons' manager after initially joining the club from Burnley and playing for them until his retirement earlier this year.

And he's loving life in the Middle East, adding: "I've really enjoyed it.

"The football is growing and evolving, and I am grateful to come out here.

"We train at 7am for about an hour and a half before the humidity and heat picks up.

"But I've always had an interest in it throughout my career, and my legs were giving way, so it's come hand in hand.

"I am grateful for the opportunity, and it's a great club to be at."

4 Shelvey made 278 Premier League appearances for a variety of clubs across an 18-year senior career Credit: getty

Arabian Falcons issue call to all

As well as Shelvey appearing on talkSPORT, the Falcons released a statement as well.

They said: “Come and Train, live and play in Dubai, with no long-term commitment required.

“Don’t sit on the sidelines. Come and show what you’ve got over in Dubai."

And when you see the list of current free agents, Shelvey could build a hell of a side.

Sports.title: Edu officially leaves Nottingham Forest as club’s head of global football after being banished from premises by Evangelos Marinakis
Sports.content:
Edu officially leaves Nottingham Forest as club’s head of global football after being banished from premises by Evangelos Marinakis

Edu has left Nottingham Forest just over a year after joining as the club's global head of football.

talkSPORT reported in March that the two parties were negotiating the former Arsenal midfielder's departure.

2 Owner Evangelos Marinakis was underwhelmed by Edu's time at the club Credit: Getty

Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis had told Edu to stay away from club premises amid disappointment over his performance.

Edu, who was also tasked with overseeing Greek club Olympiacos and Portuguese outfit Rio Ave – both also owned by Marinakis – as part of the role, was involved in a turbulent season at Forest.

Forest's wild ride

The Reds went through four managers over the course of the campaign, with the last of them, Vitor Pereira, being replaced by Oliver Glasner this summer.

Nuno Espirito Santo guided began the season in charge before a dramatic falling out with Edu over summer transfers led to his sudden exit just three games in.

He was succeeded by Ange Postecoglou, but the former Tottenham boss lasted just eight winless matches before being dismissed.

Sean Dyche took over and won 10 of his 25 games in charge, but he too was given his marching orders in February, making way for Pereira.

Pereira ultimately steered Forest to Premier League safety, securing a fifth straight top-flight campaign.

But that wasn't enough for him to keep his job and he made way for Glasner following his departure from Crystal Palace.

Glasner has overseen two draws in his first three Premier League games at the helm.

He'll be looking for his first win as Forest head coach away to Aston Villa on Saturday.

Edu exits

2 Forest were the second Premier League club where Edu had worked in a technical capacity Credit: Getty

One of Arsene Wenger's 2003/04 Arsenal 'Invincibles', Edu also earned 16 caps for Brazil.

Finishing his playing career with Corinthians, he took over as the Brazilian giants' director of football in 2011.

After working as an assistant to Carlos Queiroz with the Iran national team and becoming Brazil's general coordinator, he returned to Arsenal in 2019.

Edu was appointed as the Gunners' first-ever technical director.

Three years later, in another club first, he was named sporting director.

The 48-year-old took the job at Forest in July last year, but it's fair to say things have not worked out.

Sports.title: Joey Barton to remain in custody ahead of 2027 trial
Sports.content:
Joey Barton to remain in custody ahead of 2027 trial

Former Premier League player Joey Barton will remain in custody until his trial next year.

An application for bail for the 44-year-old ex-Manchester City and Newcastle midfielder has been refused.



2 Barton was arrested and remanded in custody in March after the incident Credit: Getty

Barton's trial pushed back

Barton had been due to stand trial last week on a charge of inflicting grievous bodily harm (GBH) with intent.

But the case has since been pushed back to March next year.

Barton is accused of attacking former non-League manager Kevin Lynch at a Huyton and Prescot Golf Club in March this year.

Lynch was previously in charge of Merseyside football club Prescot Cables.



By the time the trial is due to take place, Barton will have been on remand for 12 months.

This isn't the first time Barton has been charged over a violent incident.



In May 2007, he was charged with assaulting Man City teammate Ousmane Dabo during a training session, leaving Dabo unconscious and hospitalised with a suspected detached retina.

Having initially pleaded not guilty, Barton changed his plea to guilty and received a suspended four-month prison sentence, as well as being ordered to pay £3,000 in compensation and undertake 200 hours of community service.



He was also banned for six matches by the FA with a further six matches suspended.

In December of the same year, by which time he had left City for Newcastle, Barton was arrested on suspicion of assaulting a man in Liverpool city centre.

2 Barton was no stranger to cards during his Premier League career, receiving 78 yellows and six reds Credit: Getty

He pleaded guilty to the offence and, in May 2008, was imprisoned for six months.



In July 2025, Barton was found guilty of assault by beating after pushing his wife Georgia Barton to the floor and kicking her in the head during an incident over which he was initially charged four years earlier.

He received a 12-week suspended prison sentence for that offence.

A familiar name in referees' notebooks

Barton retired in 2017 after a playing career that was beset by controversy on the pitch as well as off it.

He was sent off six times in the Premier League, among the most of any player in the history of the competition.

In May 2012, while playing QPR against former club City on the final day of the season, he was dismissed for violent conduct after elbowing Carlos Tevez.



While leaving the pitch, Barton kicked Sergio Aguero in the back of the knee and tried to headbutt Vincent Kompany.

As a result of his actions, the FA suspended him for 12 games and fined him £75,000.

Barton's most recent role in football was as manager of Bristol Rovers, where he was sacked in 2023.

He previously spent two-and-a-half years in charge of another EFL club, Fleetwood Town.

Sports.title: Where to watch Chelsea v Leeds and why Blues are playing Carabao Cup tie this week
Sports.content:
Where to watch Chelsea v Leeds and why Blues are playing Carabao Cup tie this week

Leeds United will be aiming to beat Chelsea in a League Cup tie for the first time on Wednesday.

The two sides meet at Stamford Bridge in the third round of this season's competition.



3 Leeds must pull off an historic club first to reach the last 16 of the Carabao Cup Credit: Getty

A place in the last 16 is up for grabs for the winner as the rivals face off in west London.

It will be the first League Cup tie between the two clubs for 14 years.

Their last meeting in the competition came in the quarter-finals back in December 2012, with Chelsea running out 5-1 winners at Elland Road.



This time around, the Blues play host to Leeds, who have not won this fixture away from home since 1999.

However, Leeds have made an impressive start to the season, with Daniel Farke's side unbeaten in all competitions.



As well as a win and two draws in the Premier League, they beat Nottingham Forest in the Carabao Cup second round last month.

Meanwhile, Chelsea suffered their first defeat under new boss Xabi Alonso away at Arsenal on Sunday.



Where to watch Chelsea vs Leeds

Chelsea host Leeds in the third round of this season's Carabao Cup at 8pm on Wednesday, September 9.

The match has been selected for live television broadcast on Sky Sports.

Coverage on Sky Sports Main Event is scheduled to get underway at 7.30pm.

3 Chelsea have never lost a League Cup tie to Leeds in the competition's 66-year history Credit: Getty



Alternatively, updates from Stamford Bridge will be available on both talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 



For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

3 Chelsea beat Luton to reach the third round as they eye their sixth League Cup triumph Credit: Getty

Chelsea vs Leeds team news

Alonso is set to be without Jordan Henderson and Marco Palestra against Leeds.

The pair have been ruled out through injury, but could return at home to Hull City this weekend.



Moises Caicedo is also a doubt, with the midfielder's fitness currently being assessed.

Leeds have injury absentees of their own, notably defender Joe Rodon.

The Wales international is sidelined with a hamstring issue, joining long-term absentee Mateo Joseph on the treatment table.

Ilia Gruev is being assessed ahead of a potential comeback, though, but Monday's league meeting with Newcastle United is seen as a more realistic return date.

Why are Chelsea playing this week?

Chelsea's clash with Leeds comes a week before the likes of Arsenal and Manchester United play their third round ties.



This is due to the Blues' absence from European competition this season.

Clubs in the Champions League begin their league phase campaign this week.

UEFA fixtures cannot be rescheduled to make way for domestic matches, meaning those clubs' cup ties have been delayed.

Arsenal, Liverpool, United, Manchester City and Aston Villa will all play their third round matches next week.



With the round split across two weeks, Chelsea's meeting with Leeds is one of six ties played across Tuesday, September 8 and Wednesday, September 9.

The remaining 10 matches are then to be played between September 15 and 17.

Sports.title: Naomi Osaka brutally trolled by fans after debuting latest 'ludicrous' look... only for star to crash out of US Open in straight-set defeat
Sports.content:
Naomi Osaka brutally trolled by fans after debuting latest 'ludicrous' look... only for star to crash out of US Open in straight-set defeat

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Naomi Osaka has been brutally trolled by tennis fans after debuting her latest bold walkout look, only to get blown off the court by world No. 2 Elena Rybakina in a straight-set US Open exit on Monday afternoon.

The four-time Grand Slam champion has dominated headlines at Flushing Meadows all week with a string of unconventional runway-inspired outfits.

However, her fashion statements came back to bite her during Monday's round of 16 clash, where Rybakina dismantled the Japanese star in a brutal 6-1, 6-4 defeat.

Osaka had initially turned heads before a ball was even hit, arriving on court in an eye-catching, oversized hooded coat lined with thick faux-fur.

While the streetwear look marked a shift from her earlier outfits, viewers quickly took to social media to mock the ensemble after Osaka fell flat on the court.

One critical viewer wrote on X: 'Osaka comes out in a ridiculous coat and gets absolutely smoked in 1st set. Maybe leave the ludicrous bling in the locker room.'

Naomi Osaka debuted yet another bold pre-match outfit at the US Open on Monday afternoon

However, the Japanese star's time in the competition came to an end after a straight-set defeat

Elena Rybakina secured a 6-1, 6-4 win over Osaka to punch her ticket to the quarterfinals

Another fan took aim at the pre-match theatrics, writing: 'Clothes are great, but let's see if she can back it up on the court. Style points don't win matches.'

'What is this, a modeling shoot? The outfits are garish!' another spectator blasted.

'Naomi Osaka latest outfit, looks like an oversized fur coat number? Meanwhile her opponent and fellow elite athlete Elena Rybakina entered in her playing outfit, not seeking any attention just here to play a match of tennis,' another wrote.

The online backlash proved swift as Rybakina wasted no time seizing complete control of the contest, ruthless on serve and blasting groundstrokes past Osaka to snatch the opening set 6-1 in a blistering 22 minutes.

Osaka offered stiffer resistance in the second set, however, Rybakina's relentless power proved decisive once again, breaking through in the crucial stages to seal the set 6-4 and punch her ticket to the quarterfinals in just over an hour.

More to follow...

Sports.title: Champions League supercomputer: PSG are FIFTH favourites for a third consecutive crown and Man United are given almost the same chance of winning as Real Madrid - but which of Arsenal and Man City top the list?
Sports.content:
Champions League supercomputer: PSG are FIFTH favourites for a third consecutive crown and Man United are given almost the same chance of winning as Real Madrid - but which of Arsenal and Man City top the list?

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain have been deemed fifth favourites to win this year's tournament, with a supercomputer viewing Arsenal as the team to beat.

PSG became just the second team after Real Madrid to go back-to-back in the tournament in the Champions League era when the French giants overcame Arsenal in May.

Luis Enrique's side overcame the Gunners in a penalty shoot-out in Budapest following a 1-1 draw.

Ahead of the league phase of this season's competition beginning on Tuesday, Opta's supercomputer has deemed PSG have just a 7.1 per cent chance of clinching a third successive title.

It follows PSG having endured their worst start to a season in 19 years after losing to Lens in the French Super Cup, as well as drawing against Rennes and Lille in Ligue 1 before a 2-1 loss to Monaco on the weekend.

PSG are ranked behind Arsenal, Bayern Munich, Man City and Barcelona in the supercomputers list of favourites.

Two-time reigning champions PSG are deemed by Opta to be the fifth favourites to win this season's Champions League

Arsenal are backed as favourites as they bid to bounce back from losing last season's final to win the tournament for the first time

The favourites have been devised after the supercomputer ran 10,000 simulations of the Champions League season.

Arsenal have come out on top following the simulations, with Mikel Arteta's side backed to win Europe's elite club competition for the first time.

The reigning Premier League champions finished as runners-up in the Champions League for the second time last season, having also made the final back in 2006.

Arsenal have been given a 20.9 per cent chance of glory.

The Gunners are seen as having a 50 per cent chance of reaching the semi-finals and are 34.8 per cent to make the final.

Bayern Munich are narrowly behind Arsenal, with the German champions given a 19.4 per cent chance to win the Champions League for the first time since 2020.

Man City follow at 12.3 per cent in their first season under Enzo Maresca, while Barcelona are fourth at 8.2 per cent.

The Spanish giants last reached the Champions League final back in 2015, when they were crowned winners for the fifth time.

Michael Carrick's Man United side are given just a 3.8 per cent chance of glory this season

Barcelona's best showings since have been two semi-finals, achieved in 2019 and 2025.

Liverpool are ranked as sixth favourites at 6.1 per cent, with Andoni Iraola set to experience his first Champions League campaign in charge of the Reds.

Record champions Real Madrid are ranked down in seventh place, with Jose Mourinho's side given just a 4.4 per cent chance.

Their prospects are only marginally better off than Manchester United, who are given an outsiders chance at 3.8 per cent on their return to the competition.

The top ten is completed by 2025 runners-up Inter Milan and Europa League winners Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Iga Swiatek leaves the court in floods of tears as former world No 1 crashes out of the US Open after throwing away 5-0 first-set lead against qualifier Zheng Qinwen
Sports.content:
Iga Swiatek went down the tunnel inside Arthur Ashe in floods of tears after being knocked out of the US Open - and suffering a staggering collapse during her first set against Zheng Qinwen.

The 2022 champion in New York had been in cruise control in the opening stages of the fourth-round match, playing confidently to a 5-0 lead.

But a thorny sixth game of the match saw the Chinese star break her serve, and go on a formidable seven-game run to clinch the opening set.

Remarkably, this is the second time at this tournament that Zheng has stared down the barrel of being 'bagelled' - losing a set to love - having roared back from the same scoreline in the third set against Madison Keys.

Defeating Keys booked Zheng her spot on Ashe on Monday, and she proved her staying power by chasing the consecutive comeback with a confident 6-3 winning of the second set.

Swiatek cut a defensive figure in the pressroom as she questioned why a reporter considered the collapse of her five-game lead to be extraordinary, firing back pointedly at him.

Iga Swiatek fell in straight sets despite leading 5-0 in the opening stages of her last-16 match

Zheng Qinwen is experiencing a dazzling return to form after time spent in the wilderness recovering from injury

The player had been asked what experiences in her career were 'comparable' to this match, and how she might have 'bounced back' before.

'Honestly, every US Open except 2022 has been like that,' Swiatek replied. 'We face many losses, so obviously it's not the best thing to say, but, like, in tennis, you're more used to losing than winning.

'So I don't feel like I need to bounce back from anything. Just need to focus on the work before next tournaments, and there are going to be other chances to play good tennis, and I will focus on growing and developing my game. That's it.'

But, the reporter queried, specifically he had meant that the 5-0 lost set, and how she planned to 'grow' from it.

This time, Swiatek had a more tense response, responding curtly 'It's just one match, like...'

What followed was a long and uncomfortable silence where she tried to understand the reporter's question, before continuing: 'I'll try to play the same way as usual.

'What do you mean, like, what? Do you think it's something crazy?

'You can lose a set from any score, so nothing special about that. Just that's what happened and that's it.'

Zheng will now look forward to a spot in the quarter-final, as she bids to become the first Grand Slam winner who featured in the qualifying rounds since Emma Raducanu's miracle run in 2021.

Raducanu's success five years ago marks the first and last time a qualifier has won a major, but Zheng's pedigree could see her continue to threaten higher-ranked players.

Currently sitting at world No121, former top-10 star Zheng saw her ranking tumble after a lengthy injury layoff.

But those she meets on-court are aware of how deceptive her current ranking will be, due to her status as a former Australian Open finalist, and the 2024 Olympic champion.

Zheng beat Swiatek in her semi-final in Paris before claiming Olympic gold two years ago, in her only previous defeat of the Polish star.

Sports.title: Graeme Souness rips into Declan Rice again - insisting he 'plays too deep' and 'might be a centre-half' - as legend claims Arsenal midfielder wouldn't get into any of Real Madrid, Barcelona or Man City's teams
Sports.content:
Graeme Souness has delivered another scathing assessment of Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice, suggesting he might be better suited to playing in defence because he operates 'too deep'.

Rice has established himself as a key figure for both Arsenal and England since his £105million move to the Emirates in 2023, but Souness remains unconvinced the 27-year-old has the qualities required of an elite central midfielder.

The Gunners star, who played a pivotal role in steering Arsenal to their first Premier League title in 22 years last campaign and helped guide his country to the World Cup semi-finals in the summer, was singled out for criticism and labelled 'limited' by Souness after England's heartbreaking defeat against Argentina.

Appearing on Piers Morgan's new Football Uncensored show on Monday after Arsenal's 2-1 victory over title rivals Chelsea at the weekend, Souness doubled down on his view of Rice.

'How many times do you see him as the last man with the ball,' Souness told Morgan. 'In the build-up, he's last man. He's sitting between two centre-halves or between the centre-half and the full-back. He's last man. A lot of the time, he doesn't play in midfield.

'In my second or third home game (of my career), I went into the back four like all midfield players do today. It's old man's football. It's cheating. An old man's way of playing midfield. You get the ball under no pressure and you play it out to the full-back.'

Graeme Souness has delivered another scathing assessment of Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice

He believes the England star is more of a 'centre-half' and ripped into him for playing 'too deep'

Souness went on to explain how he was eviscerated by team-mates at half-time after he dropped back to pass 10metres between the centre-back and full-back - and from then on was 'told to play in midfield' further up the pitch.

'He (Rice) plays too deep to affect the game,' Souness added. 'I don't think he's got enough football. Let me tell you what he can do. He's the best defensive midfielder in the country right now, he smells danger. But then again, he's back there all the time.

'He's not a midfield player then is he? I think he may be a centre-half. The ball travels faster than you do. I see him run with the ball 30 yards and pass it square. He's a lovely kicker of the ball and opens his body up well, there's nothing to dislike about him. But modern players are a bit precious. Criticism doesn't fall easily on these (players') shoulders. He isn't the complete midfield player.'

Morgan then responded with the claim that Rice is a world-class midfielder, to which Souness added: 'I'm not sure if he gets in Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Man City. If you want the best in that position, City had two of them - Fernandinho and Rodri. They played in midfield. Next time, please watch him. He goes in and gets it cheap under no pressure, a 10-yard pass off Gabriel, and passes it sideways.'

Souness also again blamed Rice for his role in England's World Cup semi-final collapse against Argentina in July.

'When England went one-nil up against Argentina, they s*** themselves. "Oh, what do we do now?" And I put that down to Declan Rice and (Elliot) Anderson as the central midfield players in the engine room,' he said.

'They didn't get them playing. They went back in held hands with the back four.'

So far this season, Rice has helped Arsenal claim three wins from their opening three matches against Coventry, Aston Villa and Chelsea, sitting second in the Premier League behind title rivals Manchester City on goals scored.

Arsenal have bolstered their ranks in midfield with the £75million acquisition of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United this summer, who started Sunday's 2-1 victory at the Emirates on the substitutes' bench.

Rice played a key role in helping Arsenal win the Premier League for the first time in 22 years

Rice, one of the most durable players in the Premier League, played 55 games for the Gunners last campaign in a crucial role for Mikel Arteta, who will now have the option of resting him more frequently after the arrival of Guimaraes.

Arsenal take on Napoli in the Champions League on Wednesday before travelling to the Stadium of Light to face Sunderland on Saturday.

Sports.title: Aston Villa handed major blow with new star Leon Goretzka out until after the international break
Sports.content:
Leon Goretzka will be out until at least after the international break in a fresh blow to Aston Villa's new-look team.

The former Bayern Munich midfielder, who joined Villa on a free transfer and has won 17 trophies in an impressive career, posted on his social media channels that his Villa debut will be delayed for at least a month.

Goretzka said: 'Unfortunately, my body has reacted to the increased workload after my time away from the pitch. It's frustrating, but I need this short break now to come back at full strength.

'I'll use the coming days, including the international break, to recover fully.'

Villa start their Champions League campaign against Club Brugge in Belgium on Tuesday without six of the stars who helped them to Europa League glory last season.

Emi Martinez, Lucas Digne, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins have all been sold since the 3-0 win over Freiburg in Istanbul last May.

Leon Goretzka will be out until at least after the international break in a fresh blow to Aston Villa's new-look team

Villa have yet to win or even score in the Premier League this season but boss Unai Emery hopes a return to European action will bring a change of luck.

He said: 'Goretzka's issue is a bit frustrating, but we have players who can replace him.

'When he's coming back, hopefully he can get the consistency in training and playing and we can add his experience. He is a player who will help us in different competitions with the level he has.'

Sports.title: Inside Man City's summer of streamlining: Enzo Maresca's new strategy for squad depth, where Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez fit in and how Hugo Viana quickly fixed the mistakes of 2025
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson had only been back in the country for 48 hours, still processing England's defeat by Argentina, when his day arrived. Going up to Manchester to officially sign the deal of a lifetime before enjoying deserved time off on two separate holidays with his brothers and girlfriend.

The interest had been heavily signposted, with Manchester City making relevant enquiries just before Christmas, and the 23-year-old was earmarked as the man to add much-needed punch into a midfield that felt light and yearned for the Rodri of old.

He had been anticipated to arrive, smiling with Hugo Viana and meeting Enzo Maresca, as the most expensive British footballer of all time - though that £116million fee paid to Nottingham Forest was eclipsed by Chelsea and Morgan Rogers within days of the agreement being reached during the World Cup.

And he didn't even end the transfer window as City's record signing either, Enzo Fernandez sourced from Chelsea for £125m in the nick of time on deadline day. So late – City threatened to pull out amid the posturing – that he was having a medical at almost 10pm and posing for photographs in complete darkness.

But irrespective of the finances and what ultimately transpired in City's hectic window, the conversation around the dinner table at the Ivy Asia on July 22 between Anderson, his family and representatives would have circled to how he was one of the faces of this rebuild. A pillar of Maresca's midfield, huge trust in somebody whose stock is rising rapidly yet will only taste the Champions League for the first time in Porto on Tuesday.

Midfield was clearly the area identified as the one requiring most surgery. Anderson's early displays, powerful and authoritative, suggest he is picking up from where he left off in taking more responsibility in an England shirt. Next to him stands the divisive character of Fernandez, a proven winner, a signing Maresca pushed for personally, and who offers a nastiness that City have probably missed in the past two years.

Elliot Anderson will be a pillar of Enzo Maresca's midfield - huge trust in somebody whose stock is rising rapidly yet will only taste the Champions League for the first time on Tuesday

Next to him stands the divisive Enzo Fernandez, a proven winner, a signing Maresca pushed for personally, and who offers a nastiness that City have probably missed in the past two years

Ironic, really, that City's new-look engine room is on show in Europe for the first time at the Estadio do Dragao – the scene of the 2021 final defeat by Chelsea, when Pep Guardiola went without a conventional holding midfielder. The decision is still debated in the bars of Manchester to this day.

When taking deep breaths at 11pm last Tuesday, City were satisfied with their work, totalling a net spend of £145m following heavy sales, and there is an insistence that the squad is now in a significantly more advantageous position than a year ago.

That is largely because the two windows of 2025 have aged poorly, with Tijjani Reijnders, Omar Marmoush and Nico Gonzalez all having been let go less than 18 months after landing.

City rectified those mistakes by earning their money back on all three, with Tottenham owning an obligation to purchase Marmoush for £60m once his loan finishes. And not forgetting the astonishing £85m for two-goal Savinho, bought a year earlier.

Another 2025 signing, Rayan Ait-Nouri, cannot buy a game at left back and Manchester United even asked whether the Algerian was available for transfer. In truth, allowing Ait-Nouri to leave as well would have left City too short and that throws up an intriguing subplot to their summer.

It feels deeper, this squad. It feels more complete. But there are fewer players. Twenty-two senior outfielders last year plays 20 this. In the Treble season, there were 18.

With ten first-teamers departing since May, six coming in, this has been a streamlining. Is the thinking clearer now than it was a year ago, when Txiki Begiristain was handing over and Guardiola's time began drawing to a close? The proof will be in the progression over the next three years and these past few months will likely define Viana's tenure at the Etihad.

The idea on the squad's make-up appears to have shifted slightly, with more emphasis placed upon individual players battling a team-mate in specific positions – much like how Thomas Tuchel ran the England team in the build-up to the World Cup – rather than demanding they are capable of performing in three or four different areas.

How that works or evolves will only become clear over time, as with much of this new era, and City's idea that Antoine Semenyo is the alternative No9 to Erling Haaland suggests they will still be leaning on some versatility.

Rayan Ait-Nouri cannot buy a game at left back and Manchester United even asked whether the Algerian was available for transfer

City's idea that Antoine Semenyo is the alternative No9 to Erling Haaland suggests they will still be leaning on some versatility

HAALAND FEARS MENTAL TOLL OF PLAYING AT WORLD CUP Erling Haaland has warned that a non-stop year could impact his season with Manchester City despite a flying start. The Norway international had three weeks off after his exploits at the World Cup but has claimed to be mental fatigued. Haaland has netted three Premier League goals from three starts, with manager Enzo Maresca mindful of over-playing the striker after featuring in more matches last season than in any other during his career. 'When I came back it was like "wow – it's good to be home" but it was weird because so much had happened and I hadn't digested it,' Haaland said. 'The new season started and I didn't even have a pre-season. I normally have a bit of pre-season but this time, just nothing. 'The physical side will come – if you manage to stay injury free. But you need to be sharp mentally as well – and that's not easy. 'We need to have that eager feeling to go back but we don't because there is no time to properly stay away from football because there are so many games and the season is longer.' Haaland added on his YouTube channel: 'I'm not complaining because it's still a positive thing that you get to play football throughout the whole year and live off it. 'I've never been in this situation before – I never played a World Cup so I don't know how it is.' Maresca will continue to monitor the stars who went into the final week of the World Cup, with Jeremy Doku having already suffered an injury on his return and unavailable for Tuesday's Champions League encounter at Porto. 'It's not easy for them,' Maresca said. 'I think it is correct in the moment that you see these kind of players that they start to be tired. It's correct to give them some rest. 'It can be one game out or one week away. It depends on which moment we are in. But the priority is to allow the players to be good and happy. In the moment you see them tired the risk is there. We need players at 100 per cent.' Jack Gaughan in Porto

What follows over the next ten days – Porto, United at Old Trafford on Sunday and then the Carabao Cup against Norwich City – should provide clues as to what sort of City manager Maresca sees himself as.

Settled side or heavy rotation? There will have to be some caution – Porto have won all six of their games this season, conceding only once, and Guardiola found out how troubling the Champions League league phase can be.

With the derby on the horizon, Maresca must decide whether to go same again or mix things up in Portugal. Given it certainly looks as if the quality gap between individuals fighting for the same position has narrowed with the recent business, there could be more confidence in tweaking with the sort of regularity that Guardiola was famed for.

Maresca has talked up the need for Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye to be offered minutes, while Phil Foden didn't start against Coventry City.

Before they flew out to Porto on Monday afternoon, Maresca had the music blaring during the early part of City's training session, as is customary under him. The Italian is quietly convinced he will get a tune out of City's reimagined squad.

Sports.title: Why tennis chiefs should fear the power of Carlos Alcaraz as the sport's most charismatic figure rails against an 'impossible' schedule - despite its significant riches
Sports.content:
Why tennis chiefs should fear the power of Carlos Alcaraz as the sport's most charismatic figure rails against an 'impossible' schedule - despite its significant riches

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Carlos Alcaraz does not play like someone who has been out for four months. Returning to the US Open after recovering from a wrist injury, the Spaniard has reached the quarter-finals hitting with the same on-court magic that saw him win the Australian Open at the start of the year, and showing the game just how much he was missed in his absence. He has also arrived with a message.

‘In the future, I’m going to take some breaks, some long breaks,’ he said after beating Jaime Faria in the second round. ‘Maybe not for four months, but one month, two months, missing some tournaments, because it's impossible to play them all.’

After knocking out Tommy Paul in the fourth round, he doubled down. No, he does not have an idea of his schedule next season, but what he is sure about is taking breaks. ‘I just really want to take care of my mental health and my body,’ he added, to have a career built to last.

This is not a recent issue. In 2024, Alcaraz pointed out that ‘this schedule is going to kill us’. But having now felt the benefit of an enforced break, Alcaraz has turned evangelist, and provided the ATP tour with an almighty headache.

Tennis never stops. The moment a player loses at one tournament, they can catch a plane to somewhere else and pick up their racquet if so inclined. This week, there are men’s matches ongoing in destinations as far-flung as Genoa, Shanghai, Cassis, and Phan Thiet, Vietnam. But at the very top of the game, recent years have seen the elongation of all but two of the Masters 1000 tournaments from one week to more than 12 days.

While one side of the argument is that more time is afforded to players between matches, with the format closer to the two-week Grand Slams, many players feel that the longer they stay in the draw, the longer they stay in tournament mode. Factor in the 250 and 500 events, and the all-important majors, and a top-30 player can find themselves booked-up from January to mid-November.

Carlos Alcaraz's plan to miss tournaments in the future to protect his body has raised a powerful point over the tour's cluttered schedule

With lengthened events have come significant riches. Increased revenue for the tournaments, and increased prize money for the players who feature in them. But there’s a catch - eight of the nine Masters are mandatory, as is playing four 500 events. The punishment is designed to hit where it hurts, with docked ranking points, and a reduction of the share they receive from the tour’s end-of-year bonus for top stars.

Frustration with the schedule is not exclusive to Alcaraz. Cincinnati Open winner Arthur Fils said in April during the expanded 12-day Madrid Open that he ‘always prefers week-long tournaments’, and claimed that the remaining - non-mandatory Monte-Carlo, and Paris - are the ones ‘everyone loves’.

22-year-old Fils is world No11 and has the explosive, watchable game style fans believe make him one of the few contenders to break the Jannik Sinner-Alcaraz duopoly - if only he can stay on-court. In the past year alone, he has struggled with stress fractures to his back and hip. The more cluttered the schedule, the more playing on is incentivised, the more injuries. It’s already telling - across the men’s and women’s singles events, there were 24 withdrawals on the eve of the US Open.

Alcaraz shares the as the sport’s reigning superstar with Sinner, but there’s not touching him as the tour’s most charismatic figure. Having broken with his fellow stars pursuing a greater prize money share ahead of the US Open, the ATP should now fear the power he might have as the figurehead of a movement to change tennis’ unendurable schedule.

‘I just want to step on the court, have joy, have fun on the court,’ Alcaraz said on Friday. ‘Sometimes playing such a long season or playing a lot of tournaments week after week, I feel like I'm not playing with joy, I don't have fun on the court.

‘I just want to miss tennis sometimes.’

Sports.title: Edu leaves Nottingham Forest: Transfer chief departs just over a year into the job after being told to 'stay away' from the club six months ago
Sports.content:
Edu Gaspar has officially left his role at Nottingham Forest having been told to stay away from the club six months ago. The Brazilian has not been seen at a match since February and reports emerged the following month that he had been told by the Premier League club not to visit either the training ground or stadium. Edu's departure from the club was expected following the request, with his contract having now been officially terminated. The 48-year-old had been appointed by Forest in July 2025 after leaving Arsenal, where he played a key role in helping transform the club under Mikel Arteta. Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis hired Edu to ‘oversee all football-related functions, including recruitment, performance, squad strategy and player development’. His role also encompassed other clubs owned by Marinakis, including Olympiacos in Greece and Portuguese club Rio Ave. Edu Gaspar has officially left Nottingham Forest, six months after being told to stay away from the club Edu was understood to have had a falling-out with Nuno Espirito Santo just weeks after his arrival at the City Ground. The breakdown in their relationship had been viewed as a key factor in Nuno's departure from the club. Nuno had publicly criticised Forest's transfer policy on the eve of last season, with the manager struggling to work under the new structure after Edu's arrival. The Portuguese coach was sacked just three games into the season, despite leading the club into the Europa League just months earlier. Nuno was the first of four Forest managers last season, with Ange Postecoglou, Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira also having short-lived spells during a chaotic campaign. Edu is not expected to be replaced at the City Ground, as Forest's chief football officer George Syrianos has assumed his responsibilities. Edu had previously served as Arsenal's sporting director for five-and-a-half years, before taking the surprise decision to leave in November 2024. The former midfielder, who had been part of Arsenal's 'Invincibles' squad, officially left in April 2025 after serving a period of gardening leave. Forest, now managed by Oliver Glasner, have begun the new season with two draws and a defeat in their opening three Premier League matches.

Sports.title: VAR row takes fresh twist as new image of Nottingham Forest disallowed goal released
Sports.content:
VAR row takes fresh twist as new image of Nottingham Forest disallowed goal released

Nottingham Forest's disallowed goal on Saturday has caused plenty of debate after Neco Williams was pinned for handball - but a new image has shed light on the saga

View 2 Images Nottingham Forest were left fuming after VAR ruled out their goal against Tottenham

A new picture shows the ball DID hit Neco Williams’ arm - but might not end the VAR row over Nottingham Forest ’s disallowed goal.

‌



Williams bundled the ball over the line but video assistant referee Peter Bankes disallowed the goal even though Forest boss Oliver Glasner insisted there was no proof.

‌



But a still picture does show the ball hitting Forest defender Williams’ arm which is why it was disallowed in Saturday’s goalless draw with Tottenham, denying the home side a precious win.

‌



However, the picture was not available to Bankes when he made his decision to intervene which then saw referee Craig Pawson disallow the goal.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Referees' body, Pro Ref, are comfortable that the correct decision was made and that Bankes is an experienced VAR who also knows tell-tale signs like a ripple of the shirt.

‌



Refs boss Howard Webb has overseen a “lighter touch” this season from VAR which should result in less interventions with the strict instructions that officials should not get involved unless they are sure. Pro Ref are backing the officials over this decision which has caused a backlash from Forest who have history on ref rows.

This time, Glasner said: “I think the VAR can't intervene when he is guessing. It was not clear and obvious. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high, which is why this is a wrong intervention.”

View 2 Images A new angle has shown that the ball did strike Neco Williams' arm

‌



The Forest boss also claimed: "I think it was a clear penalty when Neco Williams was fouled by Mo Kudus. We didn't feel that some decisions were in our favor today. If it's not 100% clear, stick to the on-field decisions. This is the inconsistency today. I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood."

The stats show that there have been just two subjective interventions this season which is a ratio of 0.06 after 30 games compared to 0.15 last season.

Arsenal had a goal ruled out by VAR in their win over Chelsea on Sunday. It came when they were trailing 1-0 but replays showed the officials were again right to step in.

Sports.title: Edu's venture after Arsenal exit 'not what he envisaged' as Nottingham Forest errors prove costly
Sports.content:
Edu's time at Nottingham Forest is officially over, with the Brazilian leaving his role as Global Head of Football.

Almost two years on from leaving his role at Arsenal with his stock at an all-time high, Edu's gamble to move elsewhere for a broader remit has not quite paid off. The former Gunner had worked impressively in tandem with Mikel Arteta as the duo combined to make the north Londoners a force in the Premier League once more. But, shortly after a second successive season where Arsenal finished as runners-up to Manchester City, Edu left the Emirates.

He headed to the City Ground to work under Evangelos Marinakis, with a desire to work in a multi-club model seen as a huge pull, with Edu also overseeing Olympiacos and Rio Ave.

However his work in Nottingham failed to produce the necessary results and he's been removed from his role. The news has been a long time coming - The 48-year-old had been sidelined for months and hasn't attended a match since February or set foot in the City Ground or training facility since early March.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The Telegraph reports that the work assigned to Edu was not what he envisaged when he took on the job. Edu himself accepts that he struggled to foster relationships with key members of Marinakis' staff, which ultimately made his job more challenging.

The decline in his relationship with Nuno Espirito Santo was also well documented, leading to the Portuguese leaving the City Ground. Last year's disaster campaign saw Forest go through four managers - Nuno, Ange Postecoglou, Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira as the club narrowly avoided the drop. Oliver Glasner is now at the helm.

The transfer decisions taken by Edu failed to push the club on, after they had finished seventh and qualified for Europe in 2025. The former Arsenal chief was responsible for several transfer calls that failed to pay dividends - he led the pursuit of Igor Jesus from Brazilian club Botafogo.

‌



View 3 Images Edu's difficult relationship with Nuno Espirito Santo was well documented (Image: Visionhaus, Visionhaus/Getty Images)

The £37.5million signing of Omari Hutchinson, plus loan deals for Douglas Luiz and Oleksandr Zinchenko, were all influenced by Edu, but only three of those four players remain at the club.

Adding James McAtee from Manchester City was seen as a real coup, but the young midfielder has struggled to push on, in part owing to the constant managerial upheaval that has impacted on a host of players. Being on the outer meant that the club's summer transfer business was conducted with other key figures.

When Edu quit Arsenal he claimed: "This was an incredibly hard decision to make. Now it is time to pursue a different challenge."

‌



View 3 Images Omari Hutchinson was one of several Nottingham Forest signings who have not delivered (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Whilst at the Emirates Edu, who was part of the Invincibles that won the title in 2004, helped assemble a huge bulk of the team that would go on to win the Premier League last season. He was responsible for signing Martin Odegaard, Ben White, Gabriel and the club-record capture Declan Rice.

But since leaving the Arsenal wheel has continued to turn and they've been able to add more star quality, which now leaves them with the best squad in the league by some distance. Andrea Berta, effectively Edu's replacement, has continued to conduct the club's business.

Edu's stint at the City Ground will leave him scarred and his upwardly mobile status was always going to be assessed after joining Forest, which in itself was by no means a step forward, if anything its set him back.
