One Reddit user asked what a group of eight can "absolutely not miss in Vancouver" as they planned to "enjoy the rest of the week and keep our flights home."

Serenade of the Seas welcomed passengers aboard again on Sept. 6 for its next seven-day, round-trip Alaska cruise, the "Royal Caribbean Blog" reported on Sept. 7.

World.title: Menendez brothers granted 2027 parole hearing a year earlier than expected
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Erik and Lyle Menendez have been granted a parole hearing for next year, a year earlier than previously expected.

The brothers, who were both convicted of the Aug. 20, 1989, shotgun slayings of their parents, Jose and Mary Louise "Kitty" Menendez, in their Beverly Hills home, are scheduled to have a parole suitability hearing in March 2027 instead of August 2028, Fox News confirms.

The change stems from two provisions included in Proposition 9, which allow a prison inmate's next parole hearing date to be moved up if there is a change in circumstances or new information indicating the person may be suitable for parole, The Orange County Register reported.

CALIFORNIA SUED OVER POLICY THAT COULD FREE SERIAL KILLERS AS LACI PETERSON'S FRIEND SOUNDS ALARM

"For almost 40 years, Erik and Lyle have worked to take responsibility for their actions, confront and heal from the unimaginable abuse and trauma they endured, grow as individuals, and dedicate themselves to serving others," a statement by family members reads.

"Through efforts such as helping to establish a hospice program and creating Green Space, they have sought to build an environment that reminds people serving life sentences that their lives still have meaning and that, regardless of their circumstances, they can choose each day to grow, heal, accept accountability, and contribute something of value to the world around them," they added.

NEW HAMPSHIRE RESENTENCING GIVES DARTMOUTH KILLER ROBERT TULLOCH A PAROLE PATH AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING

The brothers were handed life sentences without the possibility of parole for the murders, which drew widespread media attention. However, they were resentenced to life in May 2025, making them eligible for parole.

The new sentencing came amid a push by supporters following a Netflix series on the case that resurrected calls for their freedom. They were denied parole last year.

NEVADA PAROLE BOARD REJECTS HENRY RUGGS III'S BID FOR EARLY RELEASE AFTER DEADLY 156 MPH DUI CRASH

The brothers have said the murders were committed after years of sexual abuse by their father. However, prosecutors have contested the claims, arguing the pair killed their parents out of greed.

"Erik and Lyle were once sentenced to life without the possibility of parole," the family statement said. "We will always be profoundly grateful that they have been resentenced and that our family can now imagine a future in which they are once again part of our everyday lives… We are incredibly proud of the men they have become and deeply grateful to the Parole Board for recognizing their efforts and allowing them to advance their parole hearing."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Lyle Menendez, 58, and Erik Menendez, 55, are both incarcerated in the Richard J. Donovan Correctional Facility in San Diego.

World.title: Olivia Dunne pours beers like a patriot while her LSU tigers run up the score, Gator Bait & Lane's subtle shot
World.content:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

"The Week 1 college football schedule stinks, the NCAA needs to try a little harder next time!"

Idiot. Goodness, I was an IDIOT Friday. That was my big gripe going into this glorious first weekend of college football.

The schedule wasn't great. On paper, it wasn't.

CLOCK CONTROVERSY ALLOWS MICHIGAN WOLVERINES TO AVOID MASSIVE UPSET AGAINST WESTERN MICHIGAN

Of course, college football games are played on the field, and they never, ever disappoint. Simpletons like myself look at the paper and see "Western Michigan-Michigan" and think we're in for a snoozer.

And then the Big Ten refs slap you across the face and tell you to SNAP OUT OF IT. What a game! What a weekend. And how about the Ole Miss-Louisville shootout from last night?

How lucky are we? How great is college football. Welcome back, old friend. Let's have a season.

Welcome to a Labor Day Nightcaps — the one where Olivia Dunne serves up booze while Lane Kiffin serves up an a–kicking to Clemson and poor Dabo Swinney.

Lordy, what a mismatch.

What else? I've got the Florida Gators reviving a lib-triggering chant, the field for last night's game in Nashville was disgraceful, and how great is the ESPN broadcasting team of Sean McDonough and Greg McIlroy?

I said it last year, and I'll say it again today: If those two are on a call, expect fireworks. Every time. It never fails.

OK, grab you one final summer beer before the unofficial calendar tuns to fall at 12 a.m., and settle in for a special holiday 'Cap!

Olivia Dunne returned to LSU this weekend and served up some patriotism

Look, it's a holiday. You're all (hopefully) grilling/drinking/both right now, and paying very little attention to this class.

Trust me, I don't take it personally.

Because of that, we're gonna keep it short and simple. We all have things to do and more football to watch. Lord knows I do.

So, let's go ahead and get this Labor Day party started with Olivia Dunne returning to her roots and pouring some ice cold Miller Lites for the Tiger faithful before LSU absolutely annihilated Clemson on Saturday:

Lane claps back

OutKick pointed this out months ago, but it's worth repeating today: Miller Lite partnering with Livvy Dunne to promote their beer was the smartest move a beer company has made in quite some time.

Look at the Bud Light fiasco from a few years back. I'm pretty sure Bud is still trying to recover. I'm not sure they ever fully will.

Miller saw that, took some notes, used their brains, and decided to bring in Olivia Dunne this year instead. It worked out perfectly with Lane Kiffin going to LSU, too.

Talk about a 1-2 punch!

Speaking of Lane at LSU ... those with good hearing caught this little remark during his halftime interview of Saturday's blowout win against Clemson:

Gator Bait, McDonough & is this field a joke?

Amazing.

Look, I'm no longer the biggest Lane Kiffin fan. I used to be, but the way he left Ole Miss last fall really turned me away. At this point, the proof is sort of in the pudding.

He will, inevitably, leave things in terrible shape. Tennessee. USC. Oakland. Ole Miss. There will always be drama.

That being said, he's still a #content machine.

Fair is fair, and that was a funny little one-liner at the end. Sure, it's a little silly given he's the one choosing to create all this NFL-college drama, but if his team's gonna go into the locker room up 31-3 at the half, he's welcome to talk all the crap he'd like.

And I'll eat it up.

OK, let's rapid-fire this quick holiday class into a big Labor Day night. First?

You know who is also a #content machine in the world of college football? New Florida coach Jon Sumrall.

Look at what this DEMON brought back to Ben Hill Griffin Stadium on Saturday:

Goodness, did I miss that song! I grew up going to Gators games during the glory years ('98-2011), and that song was such a banger every time.

For those confused as to why the left deemed it racist ...

The former UF president canceled it back in 2020 because of what he deemed racist imagery and literature from way back in the early 1900s.

That imagery? Black children being used as bait to catch alligators. Yeah, disgusting. Not good.

Also, not at all associated with the Gator Bait chant. Literally no correlation!

"While I know of no evidence of racism associated with our ‘Gator Bait’ cheer at UF sporting events, there is horrific historic racist imagery associated with the phrase," former UF president Kent Fuchs wrote in a letter in June 2020.

Still, he bent the knee because the world went absolutely crazy during that horrible summer, and the Gator Bait chant had been locked away ever since.

Until this past weekend, when the fine folks in Gainesville dusted it off and unleashed it for the first time in six years.

Perfection. Sanity wins again!

Next? How great was Sean McDonough last night? I know Fowler and Herbie get all the shine, but I maintain that any time Sean McDonough is on the call for a college football game, it's destined to be electric:

Sean McDonough, by the way, is the only announcer I can think of who excels in not one, not two, but THREE sports.

He's a great baseball guy. I grew up listening to him call Red Sox games for WEEI, and he still does occasionally during the summer. Amazing.

He's also ESPN's hockey guy, and he nails it.

Obviously, he's done both college and the NFL. Don't forget, he took over for Tirico on Monday Night Football during a pretty down time for ESPN in terms of games. They used to get some pretty awful MNF games. That, of course, changed when Joe Buck and Troy Aikman came in a few years ago.

Weird!

My point? Sean McDonough probably deserves more praise than he gets. I'd put him up there with the best of the best. In terms of college football, there is no one better at the moment.

Frankly, it's not close.

OK, that's it for today. Good start to the week. Let's enjoy some football tonight. And Wednesday. And Thursday. And Friday. And Saturday. And Sunday.

And again, next Monday!

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

I just hope the fields don't look like this abomination from Tennessee last night:

Where does McDonough rank for you? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

World.title: King Charles confirms Harry and Meghan will not be working royals after U.K. return
World.content:
LONDON — Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, will remain nonworking members of Britain’s royal family after their return to the U.K., a letter sent on behalf of King Charles III said Monday.

The couple who last month moved from California back to Britain for an “extended” stay with their children Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, will still not be able to use the titles of His and Her Royal Highness, according to the letter signed by the Lord Chamberlain, the most senior officer of the royal household.

“It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of The Sovereign, and are no longer working Members of The Royal Family,” the letter read.

“This position, distinct from the State and Royal duties undertaken by the working Royal Family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be fully respected,” it added.

A Buckingham Palace source confirmed to NBC News that the letter had been shared with Harry’s team on Monday. It was put into the public domain because it would likely have leaked anyway and they wanted to avoid claims of secrecy around what it contained, they said.

NBC News has reached out to the Sussexes for comment.

The letter from Lord Chamberlain went on to say that “their styles as His and Her Royal Highness remain in abeyance and are not used.”

It added that their charitable work was “a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity” and “in short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests.”

The letter was released “to help avoid doubt or confusion,” after “a number of requests for guidance.”

Harry and Meghan rattled the royal family when they opted to step down as working royals six years ago, eventually choosing a quieter life in Montecito, an affluent coastal enclave in Santa Barbara.

Relations with the royal family have been strained since then, worsened in part by explosive allegations of racism and bullying made by the couple in their Netflix documentary “Harry & Meghan” and in Harry’s memoir, “Spare.”

Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, stepped down as working royals six years ago. AFP via Getty Images file

After few signs of a royal rapprochement, Britain was shocked last month when it emerged they were planning a return and reports in British media indicated that Archie and Lilibet had been enrolled in schools in the country.

A source close to the couple told NBC News at the time that they were moving back for an “extended period” of time.

The location of their new home has not been disclosed and questions remain over what security arrangements will be in place for the couple, after a protracted legal battle between Harry and the British government over the removal of their security protection.

Harry’s return to Britain also comes after he and several other claimants were ordered to pay a combined 34.5 million pounds ($46 million) to Associated Newspapers, the publisher of The Daily Mail and Mail on Sunday, after losing a High Court battle over alleged breaches of privacy.

It was one of several salvos between Harry and the British press, which went into overdrive after they announced their return, with front pages dominated by unconfirmed reports that Meghan could return to acting for the first time since she departed the television show “Suits” ahead of her 2018 wedding to Harry.

World.content:
Labor Day is officially here, and so are the sales — but not all of them are great (and most of them end tonight). The best ones center around a few key categories, according to experts I talked to: summer-related products, mattresses, furniture, major appliances and warm-weather fashion.

If you’re browsing online or heading into stores today — which 73% of shoppers plan to do, according to a recent survey by RetailMeNot — that’s what you should focus on. To help you get started, I curated a list of the best Labor Day deals up to 75% off across retailers like Amazon, Target, Old Navy, Brooks, Home Depot, REI and Ulta. I also consulted experts to answer all your saving and spending questions, including why you should avoid buying tech right now.

Want more from NBC Selected? 

Best Labor Day deals 2026

Land’s End’s Canvas Tote is one of my go-to everyday bags because it’s durable, fits all my essentials and has a zipper closure to keep everything inside. The bag is structured and has a flat base, so it stays upright when I’m filling it or taking items out. The base and trim are also treated with a water-resistant coating, so I never worry about putting my bag down when I’m outside. Internal and external pockets, plus a built-in key strap, help keep you organized.

The Little Green Max spot-cleans stains and removes dirt from your furniture and carpets. Add the included cleaning solution to the tank, spray it on problem areas with the nozzle, then suction up the liquid into the appliance’s dirty water tank. It has a long hose and cord to reach any area in your home, and you get two interchangeable attachments: a self-cleaning tough stain tool and a pet hair removal tool.

The Brooks Ghost Max is one of my favorite walking shoes for women and men due to its thick layer of soft cushioning that keeps my feet comfortable for hours whether I’m exercising, commuting or running errands around town. It’s also ideal to wear for casual runs and when you’re standing for long periods of time. The Ghost Max, which earned the American Podiatric Medical Association’s Seal of Acceptance, has a curved outsole that makes your heel-to-toe transitions as smooth as possible, as well as a wide, stabilizing base.

Toast, bake, broil, and warm up food with this countertop appliance, which helps you feed a crowd — it fits up to six slices of bread, an 11-inch pizza or a family-sized casserole. You can adjust its mode, temperature and toast shade using the dials, and the toaster oven automatically shuts off when the timer goes off. In toast mode, the oven monitors its temperature and automatically adjusts cooking time to ensure consistent results.

Labor Day is typically known for its deals on major home appliances, but there are plenty of strong discounts on smaller ones, especially those that revolve around cleaning. Shark makes some of the best cordless vacuums, including this model, which has a 4.2-star average rating from more than 16,000 Amazon customers (at the time of publishing).

The vacuum has LED headlights to help you spot dirt and pet hair, and powerful suction to get rid of it. It also senses the type of floor you’re cleaning to automatically adjust its settings accordingly. You get 40 minutes of runtime on a full battery, according to the brand. You can convert the appliance to a handheld vacuum, letting you attach the included crevice and pet-multi tools when you want to clean stairs, windowsills or between couch cushions.

Retailers drop prices on summer clothing during their Labor Day sales to get rid of warm weather apparel and make room for fall styles, says Vipin Porwal, CEO and consumer savings expert at Smarty, a shopping and rewards platform. I use this as an opportunity to stock up on basics like this Old Navy T-shirt, which I add to my cart every time it’s on sale. I wear it while temperatures are still high and layer under sweaters once it’s chilly out. The shirt has a relaxed fix that’s not too tight or baggy, gets softer with every wash and hits right below my hips, so I can tuck it in if I want to. It fits true-to-size, too.

The internet-famous Stanley Quencher is the ideal water bottle to keep on your desk at work, school or home. It has a 40-ounce capacity, is made from durable stainless steel and is insulated to keep drinks cold for up to 48 hours, according to the brand. The tumbler has a large, easy-to-hold handle and comes with a lid that rotates into three positions: one is a straw opening, one is a chug opening and one fully covers the openings to prevent leaks.

My Samsonite luggage is still in great condition after I’ve taken it on numerous trips, overstuffed it and beat it up in transit. This set comes with a carry-on suitcase and medium checked bag, both of which have hard, scratch-resistant exteriors, smooth spinner wheels, multiple handles and interior organization pockets. There’s also a TSA-approved luggage lock built into the checked bag.

In addition to summer apparel, retailers are putting outdoor gear on clearance, like this chair. It’ll serve you well at the beach next year, but for now, take it tailgating, camping and to kids’ sports games, or set it up on the patio or in the backyard at home. The cushioned chair has a four-can cooler, a mesh cup holder and a side pocket, as well as adjustable arms. It holds up to 325 pounds and folds up into an included bag for transport.

Waterpik’s Cordless Advanced Portable Water Flosser is one of the best options on the market — it earned a NBC Selected Wellness Award and the American Dental Association’s Seal of Acceptance. The reservoir built into the handle holds enough water for a 45-second clean, and a full charge gives you enough battery for about four weeks, according to the brand. You can choose from three pressure settings and four included interchangeable tips, all of which rotate 360 degrees to reach all parts of your mouth.

You get 10-inch and a 12-inch pans in this set, which are compatible with all stovetops, oven-safe up to 350 degrees Fahrenheit and dishwasher-safe, according to the brand. They have a nonstick ceramic cooking surface that releases food quickly, as well as chip-resistant rims to help them last long.

According to RetailMeNot data, groceries is the number one category that shoppers are planning to spend on during Labor Day weekend, which is indicative of the economic pressure many are still facing as the cost of living continues to rise. Retailers are more focused on discounting summer clearance, mattresses, furniture and major appliances (which we have deals for below), but you can find grocery deals here and there, especially on bulk nonperishables, like these Kind bars. You get 12 gluten-free bars in the pack, which you can throw in the kids’ lunchboxes or keep in your car, desk drawer or everyday bag.

Similar to groceries, if household essentials like these batteries are on sale for Labor Day, I highly recommend adding them to your cart — you know you’ll use them, so you may as well save on them while they’re discounted. This pack comes with 20 AA batteries that last up to 10 years in storage, according to the brand.

You’ll find some of the best bedding deals during three-day holiday weekends like Labor Day, so if you’re in the market for a new quilt, now is the time to buy. Lands’ Ends’s machine-washable Seed Stitch Quilt is made from 100 percent cotton that feels already broken-in when you use it for the first time. It has a seed-stitched design, cotton batting and a smooth poplin backing. You can buy the quilt in twin, full/queen and king sizes, and buy matching shams separately (they’re also on sale right now).

With a 4.5-star average rating from more than 46,000 customers on Amazon, these are some of Levi’s most beloved men’s jeans. They have a relaxed fit that’s loose through the seat and thigh areas, but more tapered underneath. They’re also low stretch, which means there’s some give, and they sit right below the waist with a higher back for more coverage. You can buy the jeans in a range of standard and tall sizes, and numerous washes are currently on sale.

This insulated cooler keeps food and drinks cold for hours when you add an ice pack, and it has a 15-liter capacity — to give you an idea of how big that is, it fits about 24 12-ounce cans. The cooler comes with two shoulder straps and a longer crossbody strap, all of which you can remove if needed. It also has a leak-proof liner you can wipe clean, and a clamshell lid that makes it easy to access what’s inside.

Comfrt’s Dreamer Blanket comes highly recommended by NBC Selected commerce editor Cory Fernandez, who says it’s just as soft and cozy as you’d hope (the brand sent him one to try). It’s covered in velvety fabric on both sides, and is semi-stretchy and machine-washable. The throw blanket is available in four sizes from medium, which covers one person, to XL Dreamer, which covers a king bed.

Frequently asked questions When do Labor Day sales end? Most Labor Day sales end on the holiday, which is today, Monday, Sept. 7. Some may extend longer into the week, but don’t plan on it — aim to get all your shopping done by tonight. What are the best Labor Day sales to shop? The best Labor Day sales to shop this year are: Summer-related products: Summer is officially coming to an end, and retailers are desperate to get rid of related products to make room for fall inventory, says Porwal. Because of this, you’ll see huge clearance sales on grills, patio furniture, pool and beach accessories and outdoor sports equipment.

Warm-weather clothing, footwear and accessories: Summer fashion usually makes up the biggest portion of retailers’ summer clearance sections, says Porwal. Use it as your chance to stock up on basics and buy discounted pieces you’ve had your eye on to save for next year. If you see something you’re interested in, be sure to jump on it — the most popular brands, styles, colors and sizes sell out very quickly.

Mattresses, furniture and major appliances: Deals on these categories are the bread and butter of all three-day holiday weekend sales. Shoppers tend to wait on purchasing mattresses, furniture and major appliances because they’re pricey, says Stephanie Carls, a retail insights expert at RetailMeNot. By offering deep discounts across a few days, retailers give customers time to compare prices and weigh options, plus, on top of deals, they offer add-ons like free delivery and installation, which could be the thing that finally makes someone take the leap. Porwal says using Labor Day to buy mattresses, furniture and major appliances is especially important this year — he expects prices to increase by the end of 2026 due to ongoing economic issues, so this may be the last time you see deals this low. What Labor Day sales should you skip? The Labor Day sales you should skip this year are: Tech : Retailers offer the lowest prices of the year on items like TVs, gaming consoles, smart home devices, earbuds and Bluetooth speakers during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, says Carls. Unless you need something immediately, don’t add tech to your cart just yet. The only exception is laptops. “Higher memory costs are putting pressure on notebook pricing, so if you find a strong Labor Day deal on the exact laptop you want, I’d take it seriously,” says Carls. “I wouldn’t assume November automatically gets you a lower final price.”

Wait until sales in October and November to save on denim, boots, coats and sweaters, for example, says Porwal. How can you save the most money during Labor Day sales? All the experts I talked to agree that the best way to save the most money during Labor Day sales is to stack your savings. That means looking at the deal price as the starting point and combining it with additional offers to save even more, says Gerstley. For example, search for promo codes to lower prices further, shop through cash back apps and browsers to put money back in your pocket, and pay with credit cards that let you earn rewards as you spend. Additionally, make sure you’re comparing prices across retailers before buying anything, says Porwal. Since so many retailers are hosting sales right now, they’re all competing for your attention, and you never know when one might lower prices just a little bit more to give themselves an edge, or throw in extras that make a purchase more worthwhile, like free shipping, delivery, install or haul-away. Don’t be afraid to ask about price matching, too, says Carls. If a retailer really wants your business, they’ll be open to negotiating with you. Last but not least, don’t feel like you absolutely have to buy something if deals aren’t compelling, says Gerstley. As we enter the final quarter of the year, sales are plentiful with early Black Friday and Cyber Monday offers starting in October, and Amazon Prime Big Deal Days might be around the corner (it hasn’t been confirmed yet, however). There will be more promotional moments in the near future, and waiting might be key to maximizing your savings. Are there better Labor Day sales online or in stores? There are comparable Labor Day sales online and in stores, especially at big box retailers, so you’re guaranteed to find strong deals wherever you shop. A few things to keep in mind while deciding whether to leave your couch: Shopping online makes comparing prices and stacking savings easier , letting you consider the total value of a deal, not just the sale price, says Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, a shopping and savings expert at Rakuten. Open a few tabs and search for the exact same product at a handful of retailers to weigh which one offers the lowest price and lowest shipping fee. You can also shop through cash back apps and browser extensions online, which help you find additional promo codes and rewards, she says.

Why are these Labor Day sales worth it?

Labor Day sales historically offer strong deals across key categories like summer clothing and shoes, outdoor goods, furniture, mattresses and bedding, and appliances. Shoppers can save online and in stores throughout the holiday weekend at almost every major retailer. Labor Day sales are typically the last summer clearance events, causing brands to drop prices extra low to get rid of inventory before the fall.

World.title: Ohio Democrat Amy Acton reflects on a ‘rough day’ as witnesses recall ‘frightening’ confrontation
World.content:
Democrat Amy Acton vowed to continue on as a “fierce warrior” in her campaign for Ohio governor Monday, a day after law enforcement officials said an armed man aggressively attempted to confront her at a county fair.

“Yes, we had a rough day yesterday,” Acton told the crowd at a Labor Day parade and festival in Cleveland, NBC affiliate WKYC reported. “I am a fierce warrior in this fight. That’s exactly why I’m running. I refuse to look the other way like people didn’t look the other way when I was a struggling kid in Youngstown, Ohio. I won’t look the other way, and you are refusing to look the other way.”

Acton was not injured during the Sunday incident at Mahoning County’s Canfield Fair, near Youngstown, but several others in the crowd were, officials and witnesses said. A suspect, Patrick Havas, was arrested on charges of disorderly conduct and assault.

Havas, 38, could be formally charged as soon as Tuesday, said Gerry Ricciutti, a spokesperson for the Mahoning County sheriff and prosecutor.

Amy Acton was back on the campaign trail Monday after the Sunday incident. Jeff Swensen / Getty Images

On Sunday, Havas approached the local Democratic Party’s tent, where Acton was speaking, and began pushing his way through the crowd, according to accounts from the Mahoning County Sheriff’s Office and the Ohio State Highway Patrol. Havas “knocked multiple fairgoers over” while advancing toward Acton, according to the Highway Patrol, which provides a security detail to Acton because of her candidacy for governor. A statement from Acton’s campaign spokesperson, Addie Bullock, said the suspect “lunged” at her.

Law enforcement officials reported finding two handguns, a set of brass knuckles and a Taser on Havas after arresting him. He did not brandish the weapons during the incident, according to the Sheriff’s Office. Officials have not yet offered their thoughts on what motivated the confrontation.

Acton faces Republican Vivek Ramaswamy in the November election. Polls have shown a close race in a state that has become redder since the political rise of President Donald Trump, an early backer of Ramaswamy’s campaign.

On Monday, three witnesses to the incident told NBC News that they saw the suspect knock two older attendees to the ground. They also said they watched as Acton, a physician and former state health director, administered care to them.

“Amy immediately went into action and gave care … while emts made it to the scene,” Lindsay Yaggi, referring to emergency medical technicians, wrote in a Facebook message. “She apologized that this happened to them and made sure they were ok before they had her leave.”

In an interview, former Rep. John Boccieri, D-Ohio, said he was standing “within arm’s length” of Acton and that the suspect made it “within feet” of her. The suspect entered the tent and appeared to be attempting to ask Acton questions while filming the confrontation on his cellphone, he said.

“He was yelling, ‘Dr. Acton! Dr. Acton!’ And when the State Highway Patrol and the security detail grabbed him, he said, ‘I was just trying to ask a question,’” said Boccieri, who described the incident as “an aggressive move from a very large man.” The suspect “started rushing and barreling towards Dr. Acton.”

Boccieri added: “He was not coming in the tent to give Dr. Action a hug. He was coming in more aggressively, and that’s what I saw.”

An older male attendee who was knocked down in the pursuit fell face down in the mud “right in front of Dr. Acton,” Boccieri recalled observing. “She immediately began rendering aid and care to the man.”

Acton, 60, served as Ohio’s health director under term-limited Gov. Mike DeWine, a Republican, during the early days of the Covid pandemic. Her role issuing stay-at-home orders made her a target for conservative activists and protesters, some of whom reportedly wielded guns and signs bearing antisemitic messages outside the Statehouse in Columbus and outside her home.

Acton, who is Jewish, downplayed those incidents as a factor in her resignation in June 2020.

Ramaswamy, 41, has emphasized Acton’s work during the pandemic in the general election contest. His campaign and his allies also are attacking Acton’s character — attempting to frame her as a quitter and calling attention to a 2019 incident at Acton’s home that police described as a “domestic dispute.” No charges were filed.

“Candidates should be able to meet with voters without having to worry about threats or violence,” Connie Luck, a Ramaswamy campaign spokesperson, said in a statement Sunday. “What happened today is completely unacceptable and has no place in politics, and we hope that no one was hurt.”

The Canfield Fair, which is celebrating its 180th year, is an annual destination for politicians in the Youngstown area, which like Ohio has moved more to the right in recent years. Trump and then-Vice President Joe Biden both visited in 2016.

“This is the largest county fair in Ohio,” Boccieri said. “Thousands of people come here, and to know and understand that someone’s walking around with a gun and brass knuckles and rushing towards a gubernatorial candidate is just frightening and scary. Luckily, the security detail was able to prevent something more tragic.”

World.title: Family of 14-year-old found dead in singer D4vd’s Tesla seeks the death penalty
World.content:
The family of Celeste Rivas Hernandez is calling for the singer D4vd to face the death penalty after a Los Angeles judge ordered him to stand trial in the killing of the 14-year-old, whose dismembered remains were found in the trunk of his Tesla last year.

“If the death penalty were activated, it would be perfect for this kind of human being, devoid of feelings and emptiness inside, and without conscience, who only caused pain to our daughter, our family, and the world that supports our precious daughter,” the teen’s parents said in a statement Monday via their attorney.

They released the statement on what would have been her 16th birthday. An attorney for the singer, whose real name is David Anthony Burke, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In a separate statement, the family said they were “experiencing so many emotions” and “reliving unforgettable moments even though she is no longer here.”

“These are feelings that only a father and mother and her siblings can share, with a heavy heart. We will always remember every moment and every good time we spent with Celestita,” the family said.

Celeste Rivas Hernandez's remains were found in September 2025. Frederic J. Brown / AFP via Getty Images

The teen’s body was found in the front trunk of Burke’s Tesla at a Los Angeles impound lot in September 2025. Prosecutors said the car had been left on a street near Burke’s home and impounded at Hollywood Tow after someone reported an abandoned vehicle.

A decomposed head and torso were found in a black cadaver bag, according to court documents, and a second bag contained additional dismembered body parts.

Burke, 21, was arrested in April at a house on Marmont Avenue in the Hollywood Hills, Los Angeles police said. He has pleaded not guilty to charges of murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under the age of 14 and unlawful mutilation of human remains.

At an evidentiary hearing in July, prosecutors said Burke began a relationship with Rivas Hernandez when she was 13 and ended it after she threatened to expose him. Text messages revealed in court showed that the teen had gotten pregnant by Burke and had an abortion.

Last month, Burke abruptly parted ways with his legal team and asked to be represented by public defenders. An attorney for Rivas Hernandez’s family said in a statement that he does not deserve a public defender given his status and fame on social media.

“The residents of Los Angeles County should be outraged because it will be the taxpayers that are picking up the tab to defend this millionaire,” attorney Patrick Steinfeld said. “David Anthony Burke is not indigent.”

World.title: Ross Fire still burning, with over 90,000 acres scorched
World.content:
A wildfire that sparked near Ross in Palo Pinto County on Aug. 24 has burned at least 90,400 acres and is about 57% contained. It has destroyed more than 150 structures in the area, including homes, forced evacuations in neighboring Jack County and affected local schools, North Texas officials said.

The National Weather Service said the Ross Fire is now the second-largest wildfire in North Texas.

How big is the Ross Fire and where is it burning?

The Ross Fire has burned at least 90,400 acres in Palo Pinto and Jack counties, with the fire burning near U.S. 180 and FM 919.

According to the Texas A&M Forest Service, the fire was 57% contained as of Monday, Sept. 7; 157 structures have been destroyed, 140 structures are damaged, and 453 structures have been saved.

Residents in Jack County along County Road 2210 toward Highway 281 were instructed to evacuate on Tuesday, Aug. 25; however, those mandatory evacuations were lifted a day later as conditions improved. Jack County Emergency Management warns returning residents to stay vigilant as the fire is still burning in neighboring Palo Pinto County.

The fire began near Ross in Palo Pinto County just before 1:30 p.m. Monday, Aug. 24, and was initially estimated at 25 acres, according to the Palo Pinto County Emergency Service District. It rapidly expanded to thousands of acres.

The Longhorn Council of Scouting America said many buildings at Worth Ranch in Palo Pinto were among the structures that suffered catastrophic damage, but no scouts, campers, or guests were at the property when the fire moved into the area, and the camp ranger, Pat Adams, was safely evacuated.

What areas are under evacuation orders because of the Ross Fire?

As of Monday, Aug. 31, all school districts in the area have resumed normal operations.

The wildfire and evacuations affected schools in the area. Jacksboro ISD delayed the start of school by two hours on Tuesday, Aug. 25, but normal operations resumed the next day.

Perrin CISD canceled classes for Tuesday, Aug. 25, and delayed the start of school to 10 a.m. Wednesday, Aug. 26.

Jack County Emergency Management instructed Bryson ISD and Graford ISD to cancel classes that same Wednesday.

A Molson Coors spokesperson said the company had temporarily paused some canning lines at the Fort Worth facility out of an abundance of caution over the smoky skies.

"But beer lovers will see absolutely no impact," the spokesperson said.

The Texas Intrastate Fire Mutual Aid System (TIFMAS) Strike Team, along with the Texas A&M Forest Service, is supporting firefighting efforts with dozers and aircraft.

What roads are closed because of the Ross Fire?

U.S. Highway 180 has reopened after being closed to all traffic between South FM 4 and FM 919 because of the wildfire on Tuesday.

A Temporary Flight Restriction is also in place over the fire area.

Where can livestock be taken during the Ross Fire?

CBS News Texas

The Graham Livestock Commission said that it was offering space for livestock displaced by the wildfire at the Old Mineral Wells Sale Barn at 2805 North Oak Ave.

The holding station is available to people who need a temporary place for livestock until other arrangements can be made.

The Humane Society of North Texas said it is helping the Mineral Wells Animal Shelter clear out its current shelter population to make room for pets displaced by the Ross Fire. Twelve dogs and 26 cats were expected to arrive at the shelter in Fort Worth on Wednesday.

Why is the wildfire risk high in North Texas?

Dry vegetation, a lack of measurable rainfall and gusty winds are creating elevated wildfire conditions across parts of North Texas.

The National Weather Service is monitoring several wildfires west of Interstate 35, with the Ross Fire among the largest.

After more than a month without measurable rainfall, fine surface fuels have become critically to extremely dry, making vegetation easier to ignite and allowing fires to spread quickly.

Residents are urged to avoid outdoor activities that could produce sparks or flames.

World.title: Hurricane warning issued for western Hawaii as Lowell approaches
World.content:
Hurricane Lowell, now a Category 2 storm, battered western Hawaii on Monday with powerful winds, triggering a hurricane warning for the islands of Kauai and Niihau. The National Hurricane Center also issued a tropical storm warning for the island of Oahu as Lowell approached close to land.

The hurricane warning extends to parts of the vast Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument, which covers almost 583,000 square miles of ocean and 10 of Hawaii's islands. Lowell is expected to pass over portions of the national monument as it travels past the island chain.

Maps show Lowell's forecast path

The Miami-based hurricane center forecasts that Lowell's center will move just west of the main Hawaiian Islands, near Niihau, on Monday night, then slow down by early Wednesday after passing them.

Earlier Monday, Lowell had been a major Category 3 storm, but "gradual weakening is expected through Tuesday. However, Lowell is forecast to remain a hurricane as it passes near the Hawaiian Islands," the center said.

Lowell is expected to pass just west of the Hawaiian Islands Monday night. CBS News

Hurricane-force winds extended outward up to 60 miles from the storm's center.

Lowell could bring huge amounts of rain to various islands, the hurricane center said, with forecasters estimating between 6 and 10 inches of rainfall for Kauai and, potentially, up to 16 inches in some areas. The Big Island could see 4 to 8 inches of rainfall, with up to 12 inches possible, while Oahu and Maui County could see 4 to 8 inches, with up to 10 inches possible depending on the location.

Lowell's maximum sustained winds remained at 115 mph, with higher gusts, early Monday. CBS News

That rain could bring "significant" flash flooding and mudslides, especially in Kauai County and parts of Hawaii's Big Island, the center stressed.

In addition, Lowell could hit Kauai County with a storm surge of up to 4 feet, according to the center, and bring "life-threatening surf and rip current conditions across many of the Hawaiian islands." Up to a foot of storm surge could materialize on Oahu.

What's more, several tornadoes could be spawned near Kauai and Niihau Monday afternoon through Monday night, the center said, and a few twisters are possible across the rest of Hawaii, the center pointed out.

World.title: NTSB arrives at MIA to begin investigation into deadly plane crash
World.content:
Members of the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) arrived at Miami International Airport on Monday to begin their investigation into what caused an Amazon cargo plane to overshoot a runway and slam into several vehicles before coming to a stop and bursting into flames on Sunday.

That crash, which left at least five people dead and five others injured, led to a roughly three-hour ground stop and forced officials to close all four runways at the South Florida airport.

Two of MIA's four runways have since been reopened, and the ground stop was lifted, but impacts for travelers remain and are likely going to continue for the next day or two.

That led Miami International Airport officials to urge passengers traveling to or from the facility to get in touch with their airline directly regarding a flight status before heading to the airport in case of a delay or cancellation.

MIAMI, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 07: Investigators continue work to determine what caused the crash of an Amazon cargo plane at Miami International Airport on September 07, 2026 in Miami, Florida. Joe Raedle / Getty Images

Because of the ongoing situation at the airport, American Airlines said it was waiving change fees for travelers with flights to, from, or through MIA.

The airline posted more details on its website.

Many passengers who spoke with CBS News Miami said the situation had left them wondering what to do next as flight delays and cancellations mount, but said that they're keeping things in perspective given the fatal plane crash.

"It's sad what happened," Juana Paz said. "We just think of ourselves, but we don't think about other people who died, which is sad."

The NTSB held a news conference on Monday afternoon to provide more information about the fatal incident.

21 Air says it's "devastated" by crash at MIA

The Prime Air plane, which was being operated by North Carolina-based 21 Air, overran one of the airport's runways and came to a rest in an adjacent field, officials said at a Sunday news conference.

Miami-Dade Fire Rescue said the plane hit several vehicles near the 2100 block of Northwest 42nd Avenue, and more than 60 of its units responded to the crash. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office said it also responded.

An Amazon cargo plane after it crashed at Miami International Airport on Sept. 6, 2026, in Miami, Florida. Joe Raedle/Getty Images

21 Air CEO Keith Winters said in a statement on Sunday that he was "devastated by the accident involving one of our aircraft."

"Our deepest condolences are with the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives," he said. "Our immediate priorities are supporting those affected, assisting the authorities, and ensuring that accurate information is communicated as it becomes available."

"We are cooperating fully with the National Transportation Safety Board, the Federal Aviation Administration, and local authorities," he said, adding that, "The circumstances of the accident are under investigation."

Miami-Dade Fire Rescue battles fire after plane crash, rescues victims

Of the five people who were injured, three were taken to a local trauma center in critical condition. Two others were assessed and taken to local hospitals. The names of the victims have not been released.

MDFR said when crews arrived, the plane was on fire and spewing out heavy smoke.

"What we found was a very complex situation," MDFR Chief Ray Jadallah said.

An Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767 crashes off the runway and crushes a vehicle west of Miami International Airport in Miami onSept. 6, 2026. Al Diaz/Miami Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images

Crews used foam and specialized airport firefighting units to combat the flames, MDFR said. Crews also conducted search and rescue operations, including for the pilot and co-pilot inside the cockpit, while also locating and assessing patients throughout the scene, MDFR said.

Officials did not provide further information on the condition of the plane's crew. Officials have said it was too early to tell if the people killed were aboard the plane or on the ground.

Several people were trapped inside their vehicles and had to be removed using specialized MDFR technical rescue personnel, officials said.

Fuel leak reported at Amazon plane crash site

MDFR said there was an active fuel leak "occurring off of the aircraft that is being mitigated." Residents and motorists were urged to avoid the area of 67th Avenue and 25th Street, Commissioner Natalie Milian Orbis said.

Officials said there was no ongoing threat to public safety.

An Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami International Airport on Sept. 6, 2026, causing a full ground stop that halted all flights. Al Diaz/Miami Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images

Amazon responds to cargo plane crash

Amazon confirmed one of its planes was involved in the crash.

"We're working closely with local authorities and officials to understand exactly what happened. Right now, our absolute priority is the safety, well-being, and care of everyone involved. We're doing everything we can to support those affected," Kelly Nantel, an Amazon spokesperson, said.

Nantel said the company was "heartbroken to learn that five people lost their lives" and that their "deepest sympathies go out to the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating loss."

Amazon will "cooperate fully with any investigation," Nantel added.

Is Miami International Airport still under a ground stop?

The Air Traffic Control System Command Center, part of the Federal Aviation Administration, issued the ground stop around 2:30 p.m. ET. Two of the airport's runways have since been reopened, according to Greg Chin, the communications director for the Miami-Dade Aviation Department. The ground stop was canceled after about three hours, and on Sunday night the average delay for a flight into the airport was more than six hours.

The FAA confirmed that a Boeing 767-300 that departed from San Juan, Puerto Rico, was involved in the crash. The 767 is 32 years old and had originally flown as a passenger plane for several airlines before it was converted into a cargo plane in 2015, according to Flightradar24.

Sean Duffy, secretary of the U.S. Department of Transportation, shared a brief statement on X, advising travelers of possible delays and cancellations.

World.content: Hurricane Lowell expected to impact Hawaii overnight Hurricane Lowell has turned northward and is expected to pass close to Hawaii overnight Monday into Tuesday, bringing hurricane-force winds and heavy rainfall. CBS News correspondent Carter Evans reports from Kauai.

World.title: NTSB gives update on deadly Amazon cargo plane crash
World.content: NTSB gives update on deadly Amazon cargo plane crash The National Transportation Safety Board held a news conference on Monday, one day after an Amazon cargo plane overran a runway and crashed at Miami International Airport. Officials said they recovered the flight data and cockpit voice recorders, but the cause remains unknown.

World.title: As Nepal identifies those killed in the floods, questions grow over China's reporting
World.content:
As Nepal identifies those killed in the floods, questions grow over China's reporting

toggle caption Dar Yasin/AP

BEIJING — Shortly after the deadly flash floods hit the border of Nepal and China on Aug. 26, Nepalese authorities released a list of names, ages and nationalities of hundreds of missing foreigners. In contrast, Chinese authorities took five days to disclose that the 261 foreigners missing in Tibet come from 23 countries.

Twelve days on, very little is known about the victims in Tibet as Chinese authorities have restricted reporting on the floods.

To date, Nepal has reported over 1,300 dead and nearly 5,000 missing, while China is reporting over 40 dead and more than 500 missing.

"Xinhua (state-run news agency) and (state broadcaster) CCTV have total information dominance," said David Bandurski in Taipei with the China Media Project, which monitors news censorship in China.

These outlets are expected to "guide public opinion," he said.

While China has always censored information, controls have tightened steadily over the last decade, he said to levels that are "unprecedented."

Sponsor Message

No independent access

Rights groups that have been closely following the disaster relief say the lack of independent access to the area of the flooding in Gyirong County in Tibet is striking.

"This is in contrast to the Nepal side of the border where there was immediate access given for journalists, for other observers, for international humanitarian relief organizations," said Ryan Fioresi of the DC-based International Campaign for Tibet.

To report on the rescue efforts in Nepal, NPR was able to check in with international aid agencies on the ground and speak with a rescue pilot . Nepal's police, disaster management authority and the tourism board have also been providing regular updates on their social media feeds.

Whereas in China, the government restricts foreign journalists from entering the politically sensitive region.

It took more than a week of repeated requests from multiple international media outlets before the Chinese government allowed foreign journalists in Tibet.

toggle caption Dar Yasin/AP

However, it was limited to a small number of foreign outlets in a carefully arranged visit. NPR was not granted access.

The International Campaign for Tibet claims at least 300 homes were destroyed in Gyirong County, and Fioresi said the casualty count could be "much higher" than the dozens reported by Chinese officials so far.

Sponsor Message

He also said Tibetans in the worst affected areas were relocated to "tightly controlled holding areas."

"Their communications with the outside world have been extremely limited and curtailed," Fioresi said, adding that it hampers local rescue efforts.

China's foreign ministry has not responded to NPR's request for comment.

However, in an earlier briefing with reporters in Beijing, foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun denied China was understating the number of missing and dead, saying China has been "open, transparent and timely in information release."

"Smear and disinformation is most unwelcome at a time of disaster response," Guo said.

How different Chinese media are covering the tragedy

China's commercial media, which were still subject to censorship but had more leeway, would have sent journalists to a disaster site quickly in the past, according to Rose Luqiu, an associate professor of journalism at Hong Kong Baptist University who studies Chinese propaganda and censorship.

She said she saw the Beijing News and Southern Weekly had tried to do some of their own reporting.

toggle caption ARUN SANKAR/AFP

"For example they tried to interview tourists. Not victims or those directly impacted in the local villages but they're trying to … provide some more information," she said.

In the 2008 Sichuan earthquake, various Chinese media outlets sent hundreds of journalists to the scene "in direct violation of an explicit ban from the central propaganda department of the Communist Party," Bandurski said.

This time, he said, the Southern Metropolis Daily, known for its journalistic investigations, ran only one front page cover on the floods in the days after the disaster, and it was an article reprinted from the official Xinhua news agency.

"They didn't do additional reporting," Bandurski said, adding that it was unusual for the paper.

Bandurski said his team saw the same pattern in other commercial Chinese media outlets.

"Xi Jinping has reined in the [commercial] press, such as it was developing in the 2000s," he said. "We see a total control of the narrative and basic news and information."

Sponsor Message

Foreign ministry spokesperson Guo has denied China deletes videos and first-hand accounts online.

toggle caption Niranjan Shrestha/AP

But many of the videos that were circulating widely after the floods were being actively deleted, according to Bandurski.

Recently the Chinese police penalized 10 people for spreading what they called misinformation about the floods.

Chinese state media, such as Xinhua, CCTV and Tibet Daily, have sent journalists with rescue teams, sometimes hiking overnight with them at high altitudes, sleeping openly under the rain, to reach the worst affected area at the Gyirong-Rasuwa border crossing.

The focus of their coverage is on the rescue teams, logistics of the operations and how government leaders are reacting quickly to the disaster, according Luqiu.

She said there are state media reports on people affected by the floods, but compared with the reports on the rescue operations, "the situation about the victims and the village members is relatively very small."

NPR's Diaa Hadid in Mumbai, and Mamita Bhandari in Kathmandu contributed to this report.

World.title: 5 dead after crash at Miami Airport. And, Germany's far-right wins state election
World.content:
5 dead after crash at Miami Airport. And, Germany's far-right wins state election

Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day.

Today's top stories

The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating after a cargo plane crashed at Miami International Airport yesterday, killing five people and injuring five others. The Amazon Prime plane was landing at the airport around 2 p.m. ET when it overran the runway and crashed into vehicles on the ground. It remains unclear if the people who were hurt or killed were on the plane or on the ground at the time of the collision.

toggle caption Joe Raedle/Getty Images

🎧 These investigations are often extensive and time-consuming, because a series of cascading factors can contribute to any crash, NPR's Arezou Rezvani tells Up First. Investigators will look into possible mechanical failures, flight crew performance and weather conditions. Rezvani says that airports, particularly those with shorter runways, have been concerned about incidents like these for the last couple of decades. Many have installed Engineered Materials Arresting Systems — essentially, crushable materials at the ends of runways designed to help stop planes that overrun the runway. Miami International Airport doesn't have this system in place because its runways are pretty long, which makes this crash more unusual, Rezvani says.

Sponsor Message

Trump administration envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner said their meetings with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv yesterday were "substantive." The envoys held extensive conversations with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow the day before. Witkoff and Kushner want peace talks to resume, but the visit did not yield a breakthrough.



🎧 This is the two men's first-ever wartime visit to Ukraine, and that held significant symbolism for Zelenskyy, NPR's Joanna Kakissis says. White House-sponsored peace talks between Ukraine and Russia stalled after the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in February. Ukraine's negotiating team maintained communication with Trump's team and even occasionally with Russian representatives, but the two sides remain far apart on key issues, according to Kakissis. Russia demands that Ukraine relinquish controlled land for a peace deal, but public opinion polls indicate that most Ukrainians strongly oppose this.

The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party has claimed a landslide victory in the German state of Saxony-Anhalt, narrowly missing an absolute majority to form the regional government. It is unclear whether AfD will govern the state yet, but this outcome is shaking Germany's political landscape. If the AfD forms a governing coalition, it would establish the first far-right regional government since Nazi Germany.



Sponsor Message

🎧 NPR's Esme Nicholson says that politically, these election results are "a disaster" for German Chanceller Freidrich Merz, who vowed to halve the number of AfD voters when he came into power. AfD can thank its candidate, 35-year-old Ulrich Siegmund, for pulling off this win, Nicholson says. He is a former marketing executive who shared feel-good videos on social media, vowing to "bring back the good old Germany." Despite his upbeat demeanor, he is not moderate, Nicholson says. Germany's domestic intelligence labels the AfD as "extremist" in Saxony-Anhalt. At the top of the party's agenda is "remigration," which promises mass deportations that will include those deemed to be unproductive, including Ukrainian refugees without jobs. The AfD also aims to segregate refugees and disabled children in schools and rework the curriculum to portray a more positive view of Germany's history.

Living better

Hanna Barczyk for NPR

Living Better is a special series about what it takes to stay healthy in America.

Research suggests that about 50% of women going through the menopausal transition experience dry eye symptoms, including red, watery or gritty-feeling eyes. Hormonal changes play a significant role, but they aren't the only culprits — many other factors can contribute to this discomfort as well. Here's some of what you should know about the chronic condition:

👁️ Dry eyes can affect work performance, reading, driving and other aspects of everyday life.

👁️ A dry eye disease researcher warns that ignoring symptoms can worsen the condition and could eventually damage corneal surface cells.

👁️ People can find relief through various treatments, such as warm compresses, over-the-counter eye drops and prescription medications. Reducing screen time can also help.

Picture show

toggle caption Claire Harbage/NPR

The bridge-building nonprofit Fika is connecting communities in Rwanda separated by rivers and gorges. Since 2020, the charity has built 96 bridges, and a new study shows that life in those areas looks very different now. People are able to access assets that were once hard to reach. Before the bridges, crossing options could be costly and dangerous. But now, people have better access to healthcare, schools and even post offices that were previously only on the other side of the crossing. See photos of some of the towns changed by these bridges and read more about their impact.

Sponsor Message

3 things to know before you go

toggle caption Fiona André/Religion News Service

Muslim pitmasters in Texas are gaining recognition for their unique halal takes on the state's iconic barbecue, as Republican leaders target the growing Muslim communities. Authorities have arrested an armed man who allegedly lunged at Democratic candidate for Ohio governor Amy Acton at the Canfield Fair, injuring several bystanders in the process. (via Statehouse News Bureau) Researchers have published findings that reveal key biological insights into profound autism and offer new targets for drug development.
