World.title: Investigators seek answers after Amazon cargo plane crash kills five at Miami airport
World.content:
Investigators seek answers after Amazon cargo plane crash kills five at Miami airport

toggle caption Joe Raedle/Getty Images

Authorities in Florida are investigating a plane crash at Miami International Airport that killed five people and injured at least five others on Sunday.

It was not immediately clear how many of those killed or hurt were on board the plane or on the ground.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said the Amazon Prime cargo plane overran the runway while landing around 2 p.m. Sunday.

Rosie Cordero-Stutz, the Miami-Dade County sheriff, said that the plane came to rest in a field adjacent to the airport.

Amazon said the plane was operated by 21 Air, a contract cargo carrier.

Sponsor Message

Photos showed the plane off the runway in a parking lot, with its wings charred. The FAA said that Flight 7598 originally took off from Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico.

The Miami-Dade Aviation Department said in a statement that the plane overran the diagonal runway and is disabled at the northwest end of the airport.

"What we found was a very complex situation here," Miami-Dade County Fire Chief Ray Jadallah told reporters on Sunday, adding that the airplane struck several vehicles and trapped victims who had to be extricated. He also said emergency teams were able to rescue the pilot and co-pilot.

National Transportation Safety Board investigators said they were looking into all factors, from potential mechanical failure to environmental variables or flight crew performance.

Videos posted on social media of the touchdown show the cargo plane landing hard and fast midway down the runway. There were also thunderstorms and winds in the area at the time, but it wasn't immediately clear if bad weather played a role in the crash.

Officials at Miami International Airport said on Monday morning that two of the four runways were back open following a temporary groundstop, but cautioned that it was still dealing with the "impacts of this incident."

Sponsor Message

"Because of aircraft and flight crews not arriving at MIA due to the cancellations yesterday, we will continue to see impacts to operations throughout the day," the airport said in a notice on its website. "Passengers with flights scheduled today should check directly with their airline for flight status updates before heading to the airport."

More than 230 flights into and out of Miami International Airport have been delayed as of Monday afternoon, according to FlightAware.com . More than 70 flights have been cancelled as of Monday afternoon.

Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel said in a statement on Sunday the company's priority is "the safety, well-being, and care of everyone involved."

"Our deepest sympathies go out to the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating loss," Nantel said. "We're working closely with local authorities and officials to learn more and will cooperate fully with any investigation."

World.title: Germany's far-right achieves an electoral breakthrough in key state election
World.content:
Germany's far-right achieves an electoral breakthrough in key state election

toggle caption Matthias Schrader/AP

BERLIN — Germany's populist, far-right Alternative for Germany party has declared victory in the state of Saxony-Anhalt after more than doubling its share of the vote in the first of several regional elections this fall.

Falling just shy of an absolute majority, it's not yet clear whether the AfD will be able to govern the state of Saxony-Anhalt. But the outcome is already causing a political earthquake.

According to preliminary final results, the AfD won 43.8% of the vote — its strongest performance in any German state election, which puts the far-right party within reach of power for the first time since the time of Nazi Germany.

Sponsor Message

The center-right Christian Democratic Union more than halved its share of the vote, falling to a historic low of 17.2%. The centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) received 9.3%, the Greens 8.9%, and the Left party 8.6%.

All of these parties refuse to form a coalition with the AfD. But the AfD can come to power with the help of BSW, a small, anti-immigration, left-wing populist party. BSW got 5.3% of the vote on Sunday, potentially giving it enough seats to form a parliamentary majority with the AfD — something the party has not ruled out.

AfD's candidate for state governor, Ulrich Siegmund, said the result "sends a very clear signal to Berlin: this is the end of the line; people don't want to go on like this."

"They want their good, old, secure Germany back," Siegmund told German public broadcaster, ARD.

Christian Democrat candidate Sven Schulze took to the stage on Sunday evening to congratulate the AfD on its win. While polls had shown the AfD with a comfortable lead for weeks, the CDU fared worse than predicted.

Whether Schulze will attempt to cobble together a "firewall" coalition — a platform by Germany's main political parties to keep the AfD out of government — is unclear. Such a strategy would require the Christian Democrats and others to work with the far-left party, Die Linke — something the conservatives refuse to do.

Sponsor Message

Addressing supporters, Schulze sounded resigned.

"Some say this is a dark day for Saxony-Anhalt. I say this is democracy," he said.

Alice Weidel, co-chair of AfD at the federal level, told public broadcaster ZDF that the CDU will never win another election. She said the AfD is seeing "explosive growth" across the country.

In Saxony-Anhalt, that growth is down to 35-year-old Siegmund, a former marketing executive and a salesman who, observers say, showed a knack for packaging his party's policies in positive slogans and pop-star-like appearances at campaign events and on TikTok.

His personable and amiable style is uncharacteristically upbeat for the AfD and he distinguishes himself from others in the party for being more happy-go-lucky than angry.

Germany's domestic intelligence classifies the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt as extremist. Its regional platform is the party's most radical and is seen by the AfD as a blueprint for the rest of Germany.

If Siegmund ends up as state governor, he will be privy to foreign and domestic intelligence, which is a major concern for the other parties considering the AfD's push to revive relations with Russia. Several state interior ministers from Germany's other 15 states say they are already preparing to meet separately.

At the top of their platform agenda is what the AfD calls its "remigration" policy, which promises mass deportations. Speaking to public broadcaster ARD on Sunday night, Siegmund spelled out the policy in more detail.

"Remigration is far more than just deportation," he said, adding that "remigration applies to anyone who does not contribute to society." He included Ukrainian refugees without jobs.

The AfD also wants to segregate refugees and disabled children in schools and revamp the curriculum to focus on what it refers to as a "more positive" teaching of Germany's history.

After the results, Siegmund declared: "We have made history in this country."

Sponsor Message

"This isn't just about Saxony-Anhalt," he told supporters, "It's a signal for the whole of Germany - a self-confident signal."

On Sunday evening, President Trump posted a screenshot of the projected election results on Truth Social . Trump's post was shared by Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev, who described the result as a "historic win."

The AfD has called for an end to support for Ukraine and seeking to revoke the refugee protections currently granted to Ukrainians.

Also among those hailing AfD's success was Tesla CEO Elon Musk. In response, Siegmund thanked Musk for his "support" and "clear and highly important perspective on the political developments of our time."

But neighboring Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk took a very different view, posting on X that "in Poland, only idiots or traitors can rejoice at the triumph of the AfD in Germany."

World.title: Trump to Bombardier: You can't sell in U.S. unless you build in U.S.
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday that Montreal-based airplane maker Bombardier would no longer be allowed to sell in the United States unless ​it starts manufacturing in the states.

"NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER ​IN THE UNITED STATES! Their products aren’t good enough!" Trump said in Truth Social post.

"If they want our Market, they must ​build here, and stop treating America like a 'piggybank.'"

Trump's post, ⁠which comes amid a ⁠growing trade dispute between Washington and Ottawa, ‌was the latest salvo in his campaign to pressure foreign and domestic companies to manufacture more products in the U.S.

That objective has driven many economic policies in his second term, especially a near global tariff wall that ⁠has drawn complaints from many U.S. trading partners.

Canada is set to introduce a wave of counter-tariffs against the United States early Tuesday.

Bombardier 'a source of pride,' premier says

Quebec Premier Christine Fréchette said on social media on Monday that she won't respond to Trump's provocations with more provocations.

"Bombardier is a source of pride for Quebec, a flagship of our economy, and a major player in our aerospace industry. Behind this company are thousands of Quebec workers who showcase our expertise around the world," she wrote in French.

"I have reached out to Eric Martel, CEO of Bombardier, to offer him our full support."

WATCH | Trump blasted Canada on trade last week: Trump says not doing business with Canada is an option | Duration 1:50 U.S. President Donald Trump blasted Canada over trade Wednesday, saying the country has been ‘ripping off’ the United States for years. He mentioned upping tariffs to as much as 100 per cent on imported vehicles or not doing business with Canada at all as possible options.

The White House didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on how Trump would enforce the action targeting Bombardier or the steps ‌he would take to bar deliveries of Bombardier jets that have been approved by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

The company's jets also comply with the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) trade deal that Trump helped implement.

Company already building in U.S.

U.S. aerospace analyst Richard Aboulafia said he didn't believe any business jet customers ⁠would cancel Bombardier orders and didn't see how Trump could stop them from being sold.

Aboulafia said most Bombardier private jets use U.S. engines, which are produced by Honeywell Aerospace and GE Aerospace.

Aerospace has largely emerged unscathed from the tariff war, with ‌the flow of parts and planes not currently impacted by duties.

Like the U.S. auto sector, which depends on Canadian parts production, aerospace is ​highly integrated on a global scale.

Bombardier, the rival of U.S. business jet manufacturer Gulfstream Aerospace, has an American workforce of 3,500 and a U.S. footprint of 2,800 suppliers, along ⁠with factories and service centres in the country. The company is now adding its sixth U.S. service centre and ⁠produces wings for its flagship Global 8000 jet in Texas.

Bombardier also has a defence division with a U.S.-based factory, in Kansas, where it prepares planes for special mission purposes. About half of the fleet of 5,100 aircraft operated by Bombardier customers are located in the U.S.

The ​company did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

WATCH | Unifor leader says vehicle sales aren't 'a one-sided thing': Trump trying to destroy Canada’s manufacturing base: Unifor president | Duration 1:30 Amid the aftermath of last-minute trade talks breaking down, Unifor national president Lana Payne says the Trump administration is purposely targeting Canada’s manufacturing sector.

In January, Trump said the U.S. was decertifying Bombardier Global Express ⁠business jets and threatened 50 per cent import tariffs on all aircraft made in Canada ⁠until the country's regulator certified a number of planes produced by U.S. rival Gulfstream. Neither ⁠occurred, ⁠but the following month, Canada ​certified several Gulfstream planes.

Bombardier announced on Sept. 1 that it would acquire a Canadian factory ​from supplier Mitsubishi Heavy ⁠Industries, which manufactures wings for the private jet maker's Global 5500 and 6500 aircraft.

In July, Bombardier reported that its quarterly revenue grew six per cent compared with the same three months a year ago to $2.15 billion U.S., helped by strong demand for aftermarket services.

World.title: Investigators have recovered voice and data recorders from Amazon plane crash at Miami airport
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The five people killed when an Amazon cargo jet ran off a runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday were inside a van carrying seven people from a cleaning company and an SUV hit outside of airport property, the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board's (NTSB) chairperson said on Monday.

Jennifer Homendy didn't detail how many people were in the SUV or where the dead were found, but she called the scene of Sunday's crash "utter devastation."

U.S. federal investigators examining why an Amazon cargo jet barrelled off the runway have already been able to recover both the voice and data recorders from the aircraft, she said.

Video of Sunday's landing appears to show the Boeing 767 remaining airborne well down the runway before touching down. Homendy called on anyone with relevant video or photos from the crash to send their footage to the NTSB via its website.

Investigators will examine the plane's speed and braking, weather and wind conditions, the aircraft's mechanical condition and other factors that could have contributed to the deadly overrun.

The aircraft overran the runway just before 2 p.m. ET on Sunday after arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico, and plowed across a road used by warehouse workers and other businesses that surround the airport.

Investigators say they will focus on the moment of touchdown and why the pilots didn't abandon the landing if they had overshot the runway. (David Fischer/The Associated Press)

Pilots, people in cars trapped

The crash, which sent thick black smoke billowing into the sky, trapped the pilot and co-pilot in the cockpit and some occupants in cars, said Miami-Dade Fire Rescue Chief Ray Jadallah. The agency said crews also had to extricate a person who was trapped under a vehicle.

The typical landing zone for a plane is within the first 914 metres of a runway, experts said. If the cargo jet was beyond that area, it should have aborted the landing and gone around for another try, aviation safety expert Steve Arroyo said.

Mary Schiavo, a pilot and former inspector general of the Transportation Department, said video posted online shows the Amazon plane floating above the runway for an extended period without flaring the nose upward to force the main landing gear onto the ground.

It wasn't raining at the time, but dark storm clouds loomed and strong winds were reported. Schiavo said that if the plane had a tail wind, that could have contributed to it floating further down the runway.

"A tail wind would certainly add to your troubles if you've already given up a good chunk of the runway by not touching down and landing right away."

WATCH | Investigating the Amazon cargo plane crash: 5 dead after Amazon cargo plane leaves runway, smashes into cars | Duration 2:21 An Amazon cargo plane overran the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday, slamming into cars, killing five people and injuring several others. An investigation into what caused the crash is underway.

No safety system on Miami runways

The Miami airport is not equipped with engineered material arresting systems (EMAS) that the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says have been installed at more than 120 airports countrywide to safely stop planes that do go past the end of a runway.

Those beds of lightweight, crushable material at the end of a runway have been credited by the FAA with helping save at least 497 lives aboard planes that overran runways.

Miami's airport appears to be in compliance and wasn't required to have an arresting system because it has a 304-metre safety buffer at the end of its runways, said Mike O'Donnell, the FAA's former director of airport safety and accident investigations.

The NTSB's Homendy told reporters on Monday that the question of whether EMAS should be required at every airport and might have prevented Sunday's tragedy in Miami will be a key part of the NTSB investigation.

The requirement was prompted by American Airlines Flight 1420 overrunning a runway at Little Rock National Airport in Arkansas in 1999, killing nine.

The Prime Air plane came to rest beside a roadway near two semi-trucks, images showed. The aircraft appeared to be resting on its belly and was largely intact despite the fire.

History of aircraft

The flight had been operated by 21 Air, a cargo carrier based in North Carolina. The 32-year-old Boeing 767 was originally built to carry passengers and flew for several airlines for more than two decades before being converted to a cargo plane in 2015, according to flight-tracking site Flightradar24.

Schiavo said the NTSB will also closely examine the maintenance history of this plane — particularly since it has a history of foreign ownership, including by a Russian company.

The crash halted flights at the busy travel hub for much of the afternoon and continued into Monday.

The crash halted flights at the busy travel hub for much of Sunday afternoon and continued to hamper air travel into Monday.

Miami International Airport said two of its four runways remained closed in the morning and operations would be affected throughout the day because of aircraft and flight crews not arriving there due to Sunday's cancellations.

Amazon said in a statement that it would co-operate with any investigation.

"We're heartbroken to learn that five people lost their lives in today's incident at Miami International Airport," the company said. "Our deepest sympathies go out to the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating loss."

Last year, a UPS plane crashed after losing its engine while accelerating down the runway at Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport. The crash killed all three pilots and 12 people on the ground. Twenty-three people were injured.

World.title: Far-right victory in German state expected to send shockwaves throughout the world
World.content: The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results. Voters in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt have overwhelmingly chosen the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) to run their government. It's a historic victory for a once-fringe populist party that's designated as right-wing extremist by local domestic intelligence agencies in numerous states, including in Saxony-Anhalt, and whose members have come under fire for using Nazi slogans. Some experts say the win Sunday signifies a deep crisis of established politics in Germany and sends a message to right-wing populists around the world, ahead of numerous regional and federal elections in the European Union, that the political tides are in their favour. "I'm feeling so excited and I'm so proud of our team here in Saxony-Anhalt," Alice Weidel, federal co-leader of the AfD, told CBC News at the election media centre in Magdeburg, the state's capital. "We have a huge responsibility, not only in Saxony-Anhalt, but in overall Germany." WATCH | Far-right AfD wins state election in Germany: Far-right party wins German state election, falls short of a majority | Duration 4:03 AfD, or Alternative for Germany, a far-right political party surged to a victory Sunday evening, but fell short of holding a majority. It could become the country’s first far-right state government since the Second World War. The AfD in Saxony-Anhalt promises to improve relations with Russia, ban Pride flags in schools and create separate classrooms for refugee children. It calls for "remigration," a term often used in far-right circles to refer to mass deportations of people who come from a migration background. "No one who is honest, and no one who is accepting our laws and no one who is not illegal in Germany has to be scared because of our party," said AfD Saxony-Anhalt chairman Martin Reichardt. Elon Musk, Trump react to election results AfD politicians in Saxony-Anhalt have praised U.S. President Donald Trump as a source of inspiration, even using the catchphrase "Make Saxony-Anhalt Great Again" on the campaign trail, an echo of Trump's MAGA movement. Some in the United States are already responding to Sunday's win with their congratulations. Elon Musk wrote "Gut gemacht!" (which translates to "well done") in response to Weidel's post on X congratulating Ulrich Siegmund, the AfD candidate to lead Saxony-Anhalt, on his win. Musk previously endorsed the party at a rally in Saxony-Anhalt in 2025. Trump also posted a screenshot of the preliminary election results to his Truth Social page on Sunday evening. Gut gemacht! —elonmusk Siegmund said Germany's success hinges on having more “sensible diplomacy” with other countries such as the U.S. and Russia. "Momentum is still on the side of the right-wing populists," said Oliver Schmidtke, former director of the Centre for Global Studies at the University of Victoria in B.C. "I think right-wing populists around the western world, they see it as a sign that the frustration with old parties is very profound." Federal AfD co-leader Alice Weidel in Magdeburg, Germany, on Sunday. (Mona Schulze/CBC) The win is also an unprecedented blow to the established political system in Germany, according to Marcus Böick, a University of Cambridge professor who studies modern German history. Voters in rural areas, of which there are many in Saxony-Anhalt, feel neglected by so-called elites in Berlin, he said. This regional vote is a form of protest. "At the moment it’s quite desperate, the situation," said Böick, who is from Saxony-Anhalt. He said many people living in the former East Germany have grappled with ongoing inequality, unemployment and a lower quality of life compared to states in the west, more than three decades after the fall of the Berlin Wall. "How should you get out of the mess?" German chancellor faces widespread unpopularity Voter turnout in Sunday's election was around 78 per cent, according to the state election commissioner, reportedly the highest turnout in Saxony-Anhalt since German reunification in 1990. The AfD more than doubled its support from Saxony-Anhalt's last election in 2021, but it fell just three seats short of securing an absolute majority. That means the party could still face challenges in forming government or electing Siegmund to head the state, since the German political system is usually governed by a coalition of more than one party. At a news conference in Berlin on Monday, Siegmund said the AfD will speak with individual parliamentary groups and lawmakers to see if they would support the party in governing Saxony-Anhalt. "We will, of course, hold discussions to see whether there are — and this is a crucial message today — individual parliamentary groups or individual MPs willing to join us in tackling this historic task," said Siegmund in German. Weidel, Siegmund and Chrupalla celebrate as the preliminary results came in on Sunday for the state election in Saxony-Anhalt. (Fabrizio Bensch/Reuters) The win is also already leading to questions for the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), which after 24 years of governing in Saxony-Anhalt suffered major losses on Sunday. The CDU received just 17.2 per cent of the vote, compared to 37.1 per cent last election. The centre-right party also leads Germany federally under Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who faces widespread unpopularity. "I predict that the CDU will never again win a federal election," Weidel told reporters in German on Sunday. Merz said at a news conference in Berlin on Monday that the results of Saxony-Anhalt's election have shaken him personally. He said Germany has a special responsibility to protect its constitution because of its past, and he pledged introducing reforms to improve the country's sluggish economy. "We are all deeply shocked," said Merz, standing beside the lead candidate for the CDU in Saxony-Anhalt, Sven Schulze. "We did not expect it to turn out like this. We must, of course, accept it. Those are the rules of our democracy. "But yesterday marked a turning point not only in Saxony-Anhalt, but throughout Germany. And this election result will have consequences." The CDU and other mainstream political parties previously kept the AfD out of state power by forming coalition governments by refusing to work with them. The strategy is known as "the firewall" and is meant to safeguard German democracy against threats to the country's postwar liberal values and constitution. LISTEN | Is Germany's 'firewall' against the far right crumbling?: Front Burner 30:48 Is Germany's firewall against the far right crumbling? But experts say options for the mainstream political parties to form a coalition that will keep the AfD out of power in Saxony-Anhalt are limited, especially with the party's level of public support. The AfD also leads national opinion polls at 27 per cent, according to German election research company Infratest-Dimap, and secured the second-highest number of seats in the 2025 federal election. Siegmund arrives for a news conference in Berlin on Monday, a day after the eastern state's election results. (Liesa Johannssen/Reuters) A feather in Russia's cap The AfD is also pitching major overhauls to Germany's current policy toward Russia. There are also reported concerns about the party's ties to the country, because if the AfD holds state power, it could control state-level domestic intelligence services. Weidel told reporters on Sunday that the AfD party wants to help facilitate peace negotiations amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, but experts say the party takes a clear pro-Russia stance. Party lawmakers have reportedly praised and visited the country, and called for an end to support for Ukraine; in the Saxony-Anhalt AfD's government manifesto, it states it has a strong interest in good relations with Russia both "economically and culturally." Kirill Dmitriev, CEO of Russia's sovereign wealth fund who is considered a longtime ally of Russian President Vladimir Putin, took to X to offer his praise for the AfD party. "AfD will restore Germany and Europe by leading the common-sense approach that migrant-friendly, warmongering Biden-think EU politicians tried to eradicate," wrote Dmitriev, who ended his message depicting shaking hand emojis between the flags for Russia, Germany and the United States. AfD will restore Germany and Europe by leading the common-sense approach that migrant-friendly, warmongering Biden-think EU politicians tried to eradicate. 🇷🇺🤝🇩🇪🤝🇺🇸 https://t.co/CohkKRSxYI —kadmitriev Schmidtke said Putin supports right-wing populist movements throughout the world to sow division and weaken support for democracy. "I'm sure the champagne was opened at the Kremlin to see a party that has very strong pro-Russian links and doesn't want to support Ukraine anymore," said Schmidtke of Sunday’s election results in Saxony-Anhalt. "This is a sign that, in a way, the unified front in Europe in support of Ukraine becomes more difficult to sustain." Merz said the election results wouldn't change the country's continued support for Ukraine, and said there are threats to Germany's internal security. "I want to make this very clear: 2,500 kilometres east of here, people are especially delighted with this election result," said Merz, in reference to Russia. It's unclear when a possible coalition government could be announced for Saxony-Anhalt or whether Siegmund will be able to lead the state. The AfD is also leading the opinion polls in nearby Mecklenburg-West Pomerania, which is having its state election on Sept. 20 alongside Berlin.

World.title: Charles confirms Harry and Meghan to remain non-working royals after their return to U.K.
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

King Charles authorized a letter to senior British officials on Monday confirming that his youngest son, Prince Harry, and Harry's ‌wife, Meghan, remain non-working royals following their return to the U.K.

The letter, which was shared with Harry's team and sent as guidance to senior officials ​in the government and military, said that after ​Harry and Meghan stepped down from official royal duties in 2020, they "are no longer working Members ​of The Royal Family."

"This position, distinct from the State ⁠and Royal duties undertaken ⁠by the working Royal ‌Family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be ⁠fully respected," the letter said.

"It follows that there is no change to the current status of the Duke and Duchess of ‌Sussex.... The charitable work of the Duke and Duchess is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity.

"In short, their position is akin to ​private citizens with commercial and charitable interests."

Prince Harry and his family arrived ⁠back in Britain late last month, six years after quitting royal ⁠duties and moving to the United States.

The couple had left ⁠for ⁠the U.S. in 2020, ​stepping down from official royal duties to chart independent careers, but ​they never left the ⁠headlines as Harry accused the royals of neglect, the tabloid press of ruining his life and the government of failing to provide enough security for him to ever return home.

World.title: Grindr to pay $48-million settlement over sale of users' info — including HIV status
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The hookup app Grindr is on the hook for a huge payout after settling a U.K. lawsuit that alleged sensitive information about its users — including their HIV status — was sold to advertisers.

The California-based company agreed last week to pay £26 million (approximately $48.6 million Cdn) to some 12,000 people who signed up to the claim filed by London law firm Austen Hays in 2024.

The claim alleges Grindr violated U.K. privacy protection laws for a period prior to April 2020, when Grindr updated its consent guidelines, by sharing data with other companies in exchange for payment or commercial benefits.

That data included users' HIV status, most recent HIV testing dates and result and whether or not they were using PrEP, an HIV prevention regimen.

Such information is provided voluntarily by users and they can choose whether or not to display it publicly on their profiles.

Such information, the lawsuit claims, was shared with third parties, including the advertising companies Localytics and Apptimize, which would then allow ads to be targeted or customized based on the users' info. That data may have also been sold to fourth parties, the lawsuit claims.

"Grindr users may have assumed that the information submitted to the app was only available to other app users," Austen Hays says on its website.

The firm says Grindr "plays an important role" in the 2SLGBTQ+ community, facilitating dates and sexual encounters for gay, bisexual, trans and queer adults, and that it must "be held accountable and reinstate confidence in the way it treats user data."

Eligible claimants who used the free version of the app between 2016 and 2020 will be entitled to £2,167, or $4,050 Cdn each, if paid equally.

According to a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filing post ed Thursday, the publicly traded company will pay out the first half of the settlement by the end of this year, and the remainder by March 31, 2027.

WATCH | Why dating apps may be on the decline: CBC's Aarti Pole speaks to anthropologist Treena Orchard about a decline in dating apps | Duration 5:12 Mass layoffs at dating app provider Bumble are the latest sign that more people are splitting from the high-tech way of making connections.

A 'loss of trust' for Grindr users

Per the SEC filing, Grindr says that "the settlement includes no findings or admission of liability."

"While Grindr disputes the allegations, it recognizes and acknowledges the distress and loss of trust expressed by some of its U.K. users regarding that pre-2020 period," the company said.

The British lawsuit followed Norway's government fining Grindr 100 million Norwegian kroner in 2021 — nearly $15 million Cdn at the time — for illegally sharing the data of users of the free version of the app.

Grindr challenged Norway's decision but lost its appeal in 2024.

Grindr, which bills itself as the world's largest social networking app for 2SLGBTQ+ people, was solely owned by Chinese gaming company Beijing Kunlun Tech Co. Ltd. between 2018 and 2020. That company also held a majority stake since 2016.

The U.S. government ordered Kunlun to divest from the company over concerns about its handling of sensitive data like HIV status, as well as the contents of users' private messages.

A group of private investors known as San Vicente Acquisition LLC purchased Grindr for $620 million US, which the government approved in 2020.

Reuters later reported that investors involved in the San Vicente Acquisition group's purchase had ties to Kunlun.

Grindr was first launched in 2009 and claims to have more than 15 million monthly active users worldwide.

In its latest investor report, Grindr state it brought in $138 million US ($190 million CAD) in revenue in the second quarter of 2026.

World.title: 'It's incredible,' Winnipeg man says after car blows over onto someone else's lawn in storm
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A Winnipeg man says the damage left by Sunday night's thunderstorm was "overwhelming" after his vehicle rolled into the front yard of a nearby home.

High winds and heavy rains led to downed power lines and trees, particularly in Winnipeg's Westwood and River Heights areas, Hydro spokesperson Peter Chura told CBC News on Monday morning.

Sometime during the storm, Darryl Gervais says the wind pushed his Pontiac Vibe, which rolled over into a nearby lawn on Lindsay Street in the River Heights area.

Gervais said he had just finished repairs on the vehicle and left it for his son to use right before the storm hit.

"It looked wonderful, and now it doesn't," he told CBC News on Monday. "The windows are smashed, the roof is crumpled, and there's a trail of parts along the lawn."

If the vehicle had rolled another three metres, Gervais said it would have struck a house. (Prabhjot Singh Lotey/CBC)

But Gervais is glad no one was hurt, saying if the vehicle had rolled another three metres, it would have hit a house.

"It's incredible, the force of the wind that can pick up a 3,000 pound vehicle," he said.

"Y esterday, I was working on it, figuring it would last another two years."

Preliminary numbers from Environment Canada show winds in the city reached 83 kilometres per hour on Sunday night, while 35 millimetres of rain hit Winnipeg's airport and The Forks got about 63 millimetres.

'Pretty scary'

Robyn Can icula, who lives nearby on Lindsay Street, says her family may be staying in a hotel for the next few days after the storm damaged her home just before her children head back to school.

"We can't go in the backyard because there's a power line down," Canicula told CBC News on Monday. "Our trampoline's gone, our pergola's up in a tree down the road."

The storm left destruction all over the neighbourhood, including downed power lines and trees, as well as power lines that were cut in half, she said.

"It feels like we're in a movie. It's pretty scary."

Workers seen near a felled tree in Winnipeg on Sunday morning. Preliminary numbers from Environment Canada show winds in the city reached 83 kilometres per hour on Sunday night. (Prabhjot Singh Lotey/CBC)

Canicula is thankful the community has come together in light of the damage, she said.

"We've had a lot of neighbors reach out," she said. "Actually, somebody's been helping my husband put a tarp on our roof and our neighbour's roof, so it's been really nice, all the support we've been getting from the community."

About 4,000 customers in Winnipeg were without power on Monday morning, Hydro's Chura said.

Although crews worked through the night to repair damage and restore power to some, people in areas that suffered severe damage should expect "extended outages today and likely into tomorrow," Chura said.

"We'll assess the damage and concentrate on the damage that's going to restore the most customers to power at once, and then work our way down from there," he said.

"There's more severe weather in the forecast, so that could complicate repairs and cause further hazards for people."

Hydro is urging the public to stay away from downed power lines and to report them to 911, said Chura.

"And remember, a downed tree can also be hiding other hazards, so stay away from those as well."

The storms began near Moose Jaw, Sask., on Sunday morning and moved eastward over southern Manitoba, resulting in "quite an interesting dinner hour" for Winnipeg, Environment Canada meteorologist Dan Fulton said.

"It was a lot of precipitation, but it pretty much all fell within an hour or two," he told CBC News on Monday.

Storm damage reported near the community of Elie, which is just west of Winnipeg, points to a potential tornado, Fulton said.

"If it was [a tornado], it would be probably a pretty brief tornado, but I mean, it can't be ruled out."

More rain is expected to hit southern Manitoba on Monday night, including Winnipeg, but Fulton said he doesn't expect "we'll see anything in Winnipeg other than that rain."

The only potential complication would be if severe weather develops in the province's southwest and clips Winnipeg on Monday evening, he said.

Rainfall warning in southwestern Manitoba

A yellow rainfall warning has also been issued for parts of southwestern Manitoba as heavy rain and thunderstorms are expected to bring upwards of 50 millimetres of rain in some places on Monday.

The cities of Brandon and Dauphin, as well as the towns of Swan River, Virden and Melita, are included in the weather agency's advisory issued shortly after 4 a.m.

Rainfall amounts are expected to be highly variable, but widespread amounts are predicted to be between 30 to 50 millimetres, while local amounts could be higher than 50 millimetres, Environment Canada said.

Water is likely to pool on roads and low-lying areas. Visibility is also likely to suddenly reduce at times.

The weather agency is warning people not to drive through flooded roadways, to allow extra time for travel and to avoid low-lying areas.

World.title: Quebec overhauled its bottle deposit-refund system. Is it working?
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

In less than three years, Consignaction changed how Quebecers return empty beverage containers and get paid for it.

With the help of the province, the company has centralized Quebec’s bottle deposit-refund system by removing thousands of return points from retailers.

Instead of using the bottle deposit machines usually found in grocery and convenience stores across the province, people can now go to two types of sorting centres: Consignaction, for single-unit returns, and Consignaction+ for bulk deposits.

Since the rollout of its first phase in 2023, Consignaction’s new system has received mixed reviews; some users love it, others, not so much.

CBC spoke with some users, waste management experts and the company behind the new system. Here’s a breakdown of what’s working and what needs improvements.

WATCH | New system receives mixed reviews: Quebec tried to modernize its bottle recycling system. Did it work? | Duration 2:35 Two years after the creation of Consignaction sorting centres, users and experts agree that some aspects are working well, but that other issues still need to be resolved.

Long lines, limited access

Before Consignaction took over the network, empty containers could be returned to thousands of businesses participating in Quebec’s deposit-refund system.

Many of these return points, often located within walking distance to users, are now gone, and only 172 Consignaction sorting centres have opened in their place.

Karel Ménard, executive director of the Quebec Common Front for Ecological Waste Management, says that’s not nearly enough to meet the needs of Quebecers.

“We used to have around seven to eight thousand depot centres: confectionery, retail stores and so on. It wasn’t perfect, but we had a lot,” he said. “We have billions more containers but thousands less deposit centres.”

Ménard says this creates two outcomes: long lineups at centrally located return points or “access deserts” for people living in areas where a Consignaction isn’t easily accessible.

The waste management expert believes Quebec needs at least 2,000 deposit-refund centres for the system to run smoothly.

Some users like Marie Claude agree. She frequents the Consignaction location on Beaubien Street in Montreal’s Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough.

“The wait times are very long, some days it can take two to three hours. Only having two machines to collect containers for the entire neighbourhood is not nearly enough,” she said.

Long lines are usually caused by one of the two machines being out of service or not handing out cash. Users say both occurrences are common. Some also say it can take days or weeks to receive electronic refunds for a return.

Hiccups to be expected, Consignaction says

Consignaction says it’s listening to feedback from retailers and users, attributing most issues to hiccups with any new launch.

“This network did not exist just a bit over two years ago,” argues Jean-François Lefort, the company’s vice-president of strategy.

“Whatever happens, we address it quickly, but we just have to be aware this is a transition phase.”

Lefort points out that employees work at Consignaction + locations to facilitate the deposit process or help with broken machines.

He adds opening more locations will reduce long lines.

Waste management expert Karel Ménard says Quebec needs at least 2,000 bottle deposit points for the system to run smoothly. There are currently 172 Consignaction sorting centres across the province. (Djeneba Dosso/CBC)

'It's out of money'

It might not be that simple for "binners" — people who collect cans and bottles from waste bins to earn money.

Les Valoristes Co-op, an organization supporting unhoused people who rely on the system for extra income, have noticed the new model creates barriers.

“The biggest one that always comes about is that the machine that gives money is not working, it’s out of money,” explains co-founder Marica Vazquez Tagliero, who argues supermarkets were more efficient.

“Yes, there were machines that would break here and there but they always had money. This is very important for those who collect every day and need that cash every day.”

Consignaction created dedicated bottle drop-off centres to replace standalone machines inside businesses like grocery stores. (Djeneba Dosso/CBC)

When asked about this, Consignaction said users can either be reimbursed through their app or by receiving a redeemable coupon.

If the machine is down at one location, that coupon is still valid at other points to ensure users get their money, even if they don’t have a bank account or phone.

But Tagliero argues this extra step can be discouraging for binners who spent their night collecting cans and bottles.

“We need more machines and we need a diversity of collection systems,” she said.

Her organization created their own bottle depot made for and by binners. They’ve noticed more turnout since some return points were removed from retailers.

Out with the old, in with the new

Meanwhile, others don’t just like the new system — they prefer it.

Joseph Gonzalez and his partner made the move from returning cans at their local grocer to making deposits at the nearest Consignaction + location.

So far, the transition has been smooth.

“It’s great, it’s a lot easier than it is at the stores,” he said. “Usually at the shops, the machines would break down and there would be no staff, so it’s much nicer to have dedicated service versus rolling your luck.”

Gonzalez’s Consignaction + centre in Saint-Laurent is the latest to open, joining 171 other sites across the province.

Quebec has given Consignaction until March 2027 to open at least 400 dedicated bottle deposit facilities and 800 modernized return points inside retailers.

March 2027 is also the deadline for the final phase of the system. Consignaction will extend bottle deposits to all glass containers, including wine and spirit bottles, as well as milk and juice cartons.

World.title: Stephen Fuhr was mocked for opposing the purchase of F-35s. Now he's in charge of Canada's defence procurement
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Stephen Fuhr got his "Picasso" nickname back in his days as a fighter pilot in the Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF).

He'd been ordered to produce detailed attack maps, but his abstract scribbles earned him a call sign inspired by the cubist master, according to former military officials.

Today, the 57-year-old holds a more serious title: Canada's secretary of state for defence procurement.

In this role, he leads the Defence Investment Agency, an organization created last year by Prime Minister Mark Carney's government to speed up the procurement of tens of billions of dollars worth of military acquisitions.

It's been a quick rise for the former CF-18 pilot who, after retiring from the Armed Forces in 2009, drew mockery from members of the military community by vigorously opposing the purchase of American F-35 aircraft.

Multiple sources indicate that relations remain strained to this day between Fuhr and the RCAF, whether over fighter jets, radar planes or helicopter replacements.

Several sources told CBC News that Fuhr's RCAF career had its share of ups and downs, and that he's seen as an outsider by many prominent members of the fighter pilot community. Fuhr retired from the Armed Forces in 2009 with the rank of major. (Stephen Fuhr/Submitted)

In an interview with CBC News, Fuhr said he is always ready to fight for his convictions.

"I'm not afraid to stand out on the hill by myself," he said. "It's just a principled place to be. And sometimes it's lonely, but that's just the way it is."

CBC News spoke with a dozen people who have interacted closely with Fuhr over the years. Some requested confidentiality to avoid harming commercial relations with the government, or were not authorized to speak publicly.

Fuhr — who is from Edmonton but now lives in B.C.'s Okanagan Valley and is MP for Kelowna — first became interested in aviation when his grandfather took him to model airplane competitions. He never lost his taste for speed and flight.

In addition to his pickup truck, he enjoys getting behind the wheel of his sporty Porsche 911 or flying his own aircraft, a two-seater Van's RV-8 featuring a shark mouth on the nose.

Stephen Fuhr flies in his RV-8 plane. (Stephen Fuhr/Submitted)

Sitting in the cockpit in a hangar at the Kelowna airport, he tells CBC News this plane is his "happy place."

But he rarely gets time to fly over the nearby mountains. After travelling the world in recent months, his summer schedule was once again disrupted by wildfires in the area. Fuhr's house in West Kelowna was burned to the ground by a wildfire in 2023 and was only recently rebuilt.

Now, his political career is set to become even more demanding. Under the Liberal government's Bill C-31, he could soon inherit new powers as head of the Defence Investment Agency to award sole-sourced contracts in order to protect Canada's "economic security."

The measures proposed in Bill C-31 would create a "super minister" in charge of military procurement, said Justin Massie, a defence expert at Université du Québec à Montréal.

"He would have more power than Mélanie Joly at industry or [David] McGuinty at national defence, because he would combine many of the powers that were usually or historically delegated across several departments," Massie said.

Fuhr is in line to oversee a dramatic increase in Canada's defence budget, amid a promise to reshape the military relationship between Canada and the U.S.

He says he's aiming for a sweeping transformation of the military procurement system, either by producing more equipment in Canada or by finding new global partners.

"We are going to become less reliant and more resilient," he said.

"The good news is we have friends in every time zone. And everybody wants to work with Canada."

Fuhr gets an obvious political boost from being a former CF-18 pilot. Being a member of Canada's select "top gun" club is an enviable calling card.

Still, sources said Fuhr is seen as an outsider by many prominent members of Canada's fighter pilot community.

Fuhr receiving the chief of the air staff commendation. (Stephen Fuhr/Instagram)

During his four years in a CF-18 squadron at CFB Cold Lake in Alberta, from 1999 to 2003, he was known for standing up to his commanding officer and his career had its share of ups and downs, according to several sources.

Fuhr did not wish to comment on personal issues during the interview.

Some former pilots argue Fuhr lacks "operational credibility" within their community, having never been part of deployments in conflict zones.

He counters by pointing to a defining moment of his piloting career after the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, in which airliners were turned into missiles. He said he had trained for war, but not the scenario in which he took to the skies to protect North American airspace as commercial planes were redirected to Canada.

"When you've got hundreds of civilian airliners full of people coming your way, and that is now a threat you have to work through, that's a different mind space," he said.

After leaving CFB Cold Lake, he worked in Winnipeg managing Canada's fighter fleet and then training pilots and instructors. He retired from the RCAF after 20 years with the rank of major.

Fuhr made more of a name for himself after returning to civilian life in the early 2010s.

WATCH | What Canada's fighter jet decision could mean for NORAD: What Canada’s fighter jet decision could mean for NORAD | Duration 5:13 As Canada weighs a choice between American F-35s and Swedish Gripens for its fighter jet fleet, CBC’s David Common goes to NORAD headquarters to ask top generals about the implications of operating a mixed generation fleet for North American airspace defence.

While many in the fighter pilot community were tireless supporters of the F-35, he became a fierce critic.

"It may be a great airplane, it's not the right plane for Canada," he said on CBC's Power & Politics in 2011.

Friends and former colleagues speak of his fixation against the Lockheed Martin aircraft, which had been chosen by the Stephen Harper government to replace the CF-18s.

F-35 proponents say the aircraft is superior to any other Western fighter jet due to its stealth capabilities and the extraordinary amount of data it can process.

Still, Fuhr objected to the purchase for Canada, citing the project's staggering costs, numerous delays and some of the technical difficulties faced by some air forces. His opinion was based on a thorough review of every major study on the aircraft, including various public reports from the U.S. and Canadian governments on the program's failures.

He knew by publicly attacking the F-35, he was taking on many of his former air force colleagues.

"From the fighter pilot community, the F-35 has basically been considered the be-all and end-all," said Mike Reyno, a military magazine publisher and friend of Fuhr.

"What Stephen has done, and this is all with publicly available documentation, is [point out] the F-35 has actually failed to meet almost every critical point along its development."

Stephen Fuhr first ran with the Liberals in 2015. (Stephen Fuhr/Submitted)

A former supporter of the Conservative Party of Canada, Fuhr ran as a Liberal Party candidate in the 2015 federal election alongside Justin Trudeau, drawn in part by the Liberal promise to cancel the F-35 purchase.

He won the Kelowna-Lake Country seat but lost it to the Conservatives in 2019. He then became a consultant for Boeing, among other roles, and continued to criticize the F-35, describing the aircraft as "unaffordable" in 2021.

Two years later the Trudeau government announced the purchase of 88 F-35s, signing a firm contract for 16 aircraft.

Fuhr returned to politics last year, this time alongside Carney, who responded to growing tensions with the U.S. by subjecting the F-35 purchase to a review.

There is no doubt Canada will integrate F-35s into its air force, but the real question is how many aircraft the government will ultimately buy, and whether it will decide to add Swedish Gripen fighters to its military arsenal.

WATCH | Canada quietly makes payments related to 14 more F-35 jets: Canada quietly makes payments related to 14 more F-35 jets | Duration 3:57 The federal government has started to make payments for key components for 14 additional U.S.-built F-35 fighter jets, sources have told CBC News. The Department of National Defence says it is reviewing future fighter jet purchases in the context of trade tensions with Washington.

Easygoing and approachable, Fuhr is a fixture at defence trade shows, announcements, business trips and media interviews.

He is a prime target for lobbyists and executives hoping for a share of the new defence investments.

"He talks to everyone," said a lobbyist whose clients find it easier to get meetings with Fuhr than the defence minister.

Numerous procurement files are moving ahead much faster than expected under his leadership, including Swedish GlobalEye radar planes, German-Norwegian submarines and the purchase of over 60,000 assault rifles from Colt Canada.

But Fuhr has ongoing tensions with the RCAF regarding the diversification of equipment supply sources.

"The Canadian Army and the Royal Canadian Navy have welcomed the change," said Reyno. "I would say that the air force hasn't been as welcoming to that because the Royal Canadian Air Force basically wants to operate everything the Americans operate."

A Swedish Gripen fighter jet is fitted with air-to-air missiles as part of a training exercise during a NATO air policing mission in Iceland. (Murray Brewster/CBC)

Fuhr is not closing the door to new mixed fleets of aircraft or helicopters, while the RCAF has stated its objections to the purchase of Gripens.

"Many of our allies … run a mixed fleet with fighters," says Fuhr. "I don't necessarily subscribe to the fact that we can't do it. We certainly can and we've done it and our allies do it now. So it's a function of 'do we want to do this or not?'"

Despite disagreements on the matter, a former pilot says he wishes Fuhr the greatest success in his bid to modernize Canada's sclerotic military acquisition process.

"Stephen Fuhr has to succeed. Whether anyone likes him personally or not, it is crucial for Canada to procure the right equipment to do the right job in a timely manner," they said.

Fuhr is aware he carries the reputation of an unyielding politician who holds firm views on various procurement projects. He says he is always ready to change his mind — but only if he is given compelling evidence.

"That evidence better actually bring something to the table and be credible. And if it doesn't do those two things, then I don't see a reason anyone should change their position," he said.

Throughout the interview, Fuhr made an effort not to speak directly about the F-35, a particularly sensitive topic given the trade and diplomatic tensions with the U.S.

Still, he smiled as he was asked about recent comments by U.S. Gen. Gregory Guillot, the commander of NORAD, who said F-35s weren't necessarily the best aircraft to protect the Canadian and American borders.

"He is the commander of NORAD. So I think what he says, I take him at his word," Fuhr said, breaking into a laugh.

World.title: Colombia’s government clashes with human rights office over De la Espriella walking among corpses
World.content:
Colombia’s chief ombudsman, Iris Marin, clashed with the national government after she criticized President Abelardo de la Espriella for walking among the corpses of people killed by the military.

In a public statement, Marin reiterated that “in recent days, we saw the president of the Republic walking among the bodies—in white body bags—of people who were killed during Operation “Azarías” in Guaviare.”

“I don’t recall ever seeing a president walking among the dead and taking pride in those deaths,” said the ombudsman, whose office is independent from the government.

The state and the government cannot allow themselves to be drawn into a competition to see who can be the cruelest. They cannot compete with armed groups over who instills the most fear, who humiliates the adversary the most, or who turns death into a display of power. Ombudsman Iris Marin

According to Marin, the military has the right to kill citizens, but must do so with respect for the Constitution and International Humanitarian Law, and is responsible for “the way that the State exercizes power and communicates its results.”

In a response, Interior Minister Rodrigo Lara said that the Ombudman falsely equated the State with “narcoterrorist groups as if it wer competing with them in cruelty.”

“Such an equivalence is inappropriate,” said Lara and called on the Ombudsman’s Office to be “an ally of the victims and of our mission to protect them and to liberate them from the terror regime of crime.”

Marin told Lara that she trusted that “the President and the Government will reflect on the way they communicate operational results, as I requested in my statement.”

De la Espriella’s stroll through the 23 body bags, including those of two minors, was also fiercely criticized in independent and foreign media.

World.title: Far-right political marketing in Colombia
World.content:
A deep dive into the murky world of far-right propaganda and political marketing in Colombia and Latin America.

The surge of the peso, which went up roughly 25% over the past year, put Colombia Reports in acute financial trouble. If you can, please donate or become a patron.

World.title: Judge orders Colombia’s military to suspend air strikes on illegal armed groups
World.content:
A court ordered the government and the military to suspend air strikes on suspected members of illegal armed groups while studying the risk of harm to child forced recruitment victims.

In a preliminary sentence, the Bogota family court in response to a lawsuit that was filed by a civilian who claimed the State ignored its obligation to protect children when carrying out air strikes on illegal armed groups.

TO ORDER the PRESIDENCY OF THE REPUBLIC, the MINISTRY OF NATIONAL DEFENSE, the GENERAL COMMAND OF THE MILITARY FORCES, the NATIONAL ARMY, the COLOMBIAN AEROSPACE FORCE, and the NATIONAL NAVY, through the appropriate channels and within the scope of their respective authorities, that, pending a decision on the merits in this constitutional protection action, they refrain from conducting offensive air operations against targets regarding which there is certain, objective, or reasonably verifiable information regarding the presence of children or adolescents recruited or used by armed groups, until the necessary precautionary and protective measures have been adopted and verified, and it has been determined, based on the available information and applicable operational protocols, that there is no less harmful operational alternative that would allow the legitimate military objective being pursued to be achieved Bogota family court

According to Radio Caracol, at least 107 minors were killed in air strikes on illegal armed groups since they were resumed by former President Ivan Duque in 2018.

The sentence comes a day after President Abelardo de la Espriella announced the military killed 23 “narcoterrorists” in the deadliest air strike during the peace process that started in 2016.

The president vowed to resume bombing campaigns that were all but suspended by former President Gustavo Petro as he sought peace and demobilization talks with multiple illegal armed groups, a strategy rejected by the new far-right government.

Following the killing of at least three children in an air strike carried out in August, Defense Minister Jorge Eduardo Mora blamed guerrilla organizations for the deaths, claiming they were recruiting children for human shields and combatants.

World.title: Colombia’s education minister resigns after less than a month
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella replaced his education minister after she resigned, claiming “an unexpected family situation.”

De la Espriella announced on social media platform X that he had accepted the resignation of the evangelical Education Minister Viviane Morales, who took office on August 7, the first day of the administration.

I bid a nostalgic farewell to my dear friend Viviane Morales. God’s designs are inscrutable, and she must leave us early to take charge of a personal situation that I sincerely hope she can resolve very soon. President Viviana Morales

In the same post, De la Espriella said he had appointed Ilva Myriam Hoyos, stressing that “I am confident that she will be an outstanding minister and that she will serve Colombia with dedication, character, and conviction.”

While in office, Morales lead the government’s Culture War in education and vowed to remove “gender ideology” from Colombia’s classrooms, and proposed a law that would allow churches to provide public education services.

Hoyos, a catholic, warned in 2016 that a peace deal between the government of President Juan Manuel Santos and the now-defunct guerrilla group FARC promoted gender ideology.

The new education minister used to work with Alejandro Ordoñez, Colombia’s notoriously far-right former Inspector General and the country’s current ambassador to the Organization of American States.

World.title: De la Espriella claims Colombia’s military killed 23, arrested 6 EMC guerrillas
World.content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella claimed Wednesday that Colombia’s armed forces killed at least 23 members of FARC dissident group EMC and captured another six.

In a video, De la Espriella said that “Operation Azarias,” targeted the EMC’s Carolina Ramirez Front and killed one of its commanders, a man called “Tigre” or “Pintado,” in the south of the Guaviare province.

A second guerrilla commander, “Victor,” was among the six alleged EMC members who were arrested during the operation, which included air strikes.

The president claimed that Victor carried out attacks against the military “during the elections, as part of the ‘gunpoint vote’ strategy launched by the previous regime to skew the popular verdict.”

That narcoterrorist, whom we have now taken out of circulation, carried out attacks against members of the National Army and the Navy. During the elections, as part of the “gunpoint vote” strategy launched by the previous regime to skew the popular verdict, this criminal ambushed a unit that was on the move precisely to protect citizens’ right to vote freely. President Abelardo de la Espriella

There is no evidence to suggest that De la Espriella’s predecessor, former President Gustavo Petro, employed illegal armed groups to coerce voters into voting against his would-be successor.

One minor allegedly survived the attack and was surrendered to family welfare agency ICBF. The Medical Examiner’s Office is expected to investigate how many minors were among the alleged “narcoterrorists.”

At least three minors were killed in a previous operation in Guaviare that killed at least nine alleged members of the EMC’s main rival, FARC dissident group EMBF, the Medical Examiner’s Office said earlier this week.

Air strikes against illegal armed groups are controversial as they could imply the blanket killing of victims of child recruitment, a war crime according to international humanitarian law.

The government has long insisted that those recruiting children and minors are responsible for the deaths of their victims.

World.title: 1 killed, 15 injured in northeast Colombia car bomb attack on police station
World.content:
At least one person was killed and another 15 injured in a car bomb attack on a police station on the outskirts of Cucuta, the capital of Norte de Santander.

According to the National Police, the bomb exploded on Monday evening outside of the police station in Los Patios, a municipality that is part of Cucuta’s metropolitan area.

Apart from the casualties, the blast also damaged buildings and vehicles that were parked near the police station, police told local media.

In an initial response, President Abelardo de la Espriella said on social media platform X that he had convened a security council meeting “with the entire top brass of the security forces.”

“Wherever the terrorists try to sow fear, that is where the State will be with all is might,” said De la Espriella.

We will pursue with an iron fist those who threaten Colombians, until we capture them, dismantle their networks, and restore peace to our communities. Abelardo de la Espriella

In the region around Cucuta, guerrilla organizations ELN and EMBF have been fighting each other. Organized crime groups operate mainly inside the urban area of the capital of the Norte de Santander province.

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack.

World.title: Vote to move Uribe’s massacre probe to Congress triggers infighting among Colombia’s left
World.content:
Internal fractures within Colombia’s leftist opposition burst into the open following a vote by five representatives of the Historic Pact (PH) party to transfer a criminal investigation against former President Alvaro Uribe to Congress’ Accusations Commission.

The controversy erupted after the five PH members of the committee backed a motion of Uribe’s Democratic Center (CD) party to assert legislative jurisdiction over long-standing criminal cases against Uribe, including investigations into the massacres of El Aro (1997) and La Granja (1996), and the 1998 assassination of human rights defender Jesus Maria Valle.

PH members

David Alejandro Toro

María del Mar Pizarro

Heráclito Landínez

Jorge Bastidas

Gabriel Becerra

As the former governor of Antioquia, Uribe would have been in on the massacres carried out by the Bloque Metro and AUC paramilitary groups, according to the Prosecutor General’s Office, which refused to turn over the investigations.

The commission claimed jurisdiction over the Uribe file because the paramilitaries didn’t demobilize until after 2002, when he became president.

Critics of the decision, including the prosecution and PH Senate chief Ivan Cepeda, argued that Uribe’s alleged involvement in the crimes happened years before he was granted presidential immunity.

Cepeda spent much of his career fighting Uribe in court over his alleged ties to the AUC.

Because of the committee vote, the Constitutional Court will have to rule on who gets to investigate Uribe’s alleged crimes against humanity, which could delay the investigation.

Journalists who reported on the PH support for the fabricated conflict suggested that this may be part of a political deal between congressmen political deal between Uribistas and Petristas, supporters of former President Gustavo Petro.

Becerra, who is close to Cepeda, said in a statement that there “existed nor will there exist any political deal that would compromise justice, truth or the rights of victims.

According to the house representative, the PH lawmakers “initially considered it reasonable and legally appropriate to clarify the jurisdiction of the authority responsible for conducting the investigation,” but changed their mind in response to the controversy and calls for their resignation.

Lawyer Miguel Angel del Rio, the victims representative in the Uribe case, told Tercer Canal that “the ethic committee of the Historic Pact should investigate these five congressman,” adding that “what we have here is solidarity with impunity and this cannot be allowed.”

The Historic Pact became Colombia’s largest political party after congressional elections in March, but has seen an increase in internal tensions after Cepeda’s failure to win the presidential election in June.

World.title: Finance minister presents Colombia’s $203B budget proposal
World.content:
Colombia’s Finance Minister Miguel Gomez presented a budget proposal of COP634.9 trillion ($203 billion) for the coming year, a 14% increase compared to last year.

Much of the increase is due to the government’s debt obligations, which went up 55% to 155.4 trillion ($49.8 billion), almost a quarter of the entire budget.

At a presentation, Gomez told press that an earthquake that left tens of thousands homeless in western Colombia earlier this month also forced the administration of Abelardo de la Espriella to increase spending.

In a video, the finance minister also said that the government “has taken deci

The budget bill, a revision of the one that was presented by the former government of former President Gustavo Petro, will have to be approved by Congress before October 20 or be issued as a decree.

The government will also present a Finance Bill, which determines how the government plans to pay for its spending, before December.

World.title: Evacuations ordered in Chile as wildfires run amok
World.content:
Chile’s National Service for Disaster Prevention and Response (Senapred) Wednesday ordered the evacuation of 14 communes in the regions of Ñuble, Biobío, and La Araucanía, including Nacimiento, Purén, and Contulmo, which have all been particularly affected by the forest fires.

In messages broadcast through the Emergency Alert System (SAE), the authorities also called on residents to leave their homes to avoid further damage to their health.

It has already been a week since the first wildfires ran amok in south-central Chile despite efforts to contain them. High temperatures, dryness, and strong winds add to the plight of local people and some 5,600 firefighters deployed in the area while helping flocks in from abroad.

”We are entering this part of the week which is the most complex. Today, tomorrow, and the day after we have an alert for high temperatures in several regions of the country that has mobilized a very large effort (…) to prevent the fires from spreading,“ Interior Minister Carolina Tohá said regarding the 311 active fires, of which 89 are being fought. The Senapred also said 180 fires were under control, and 309,747 hectares have been affected.

”If the temperature rises and the wind increases we can indeed have more problems, and we already have many fires,” Spanish Lieutenant Colonel Carlos Javier Martín Traverso told AFP. Traverso’s Air Operations Section of the Military Emergency Unit (UME) arrived in Chile on Sunday to join the firefighting efforts.

Over 309,000 hectares have been consumed in the regions of Maule, Ñuble, Biobío, and La Araucanía with the death toll standing at 24, plus 2,180 people injured as 1,180 houses were destroyed, leaving 5,560 people homeless.

There seems to be a seamless scientific consensus that fires are the result of human actions, either by intentionality or carelessness, although the drought that has hit Chile for 13 years adds to the aggressiveness of the fires.

In this scenario, President Gabriel Boric Font has announced a curfew in the areas of Ñuble, Biobío, and La Araucanía where a state of catastrophe is in force, in order to guarantee the security and tranquility of

the families affected by the crisis. Defense authorities working on the sites will determine the restriction’s schedule.

“We have 24 people dead nationwide, three are from Santa Juana and we do not want there to be even one more,” Boric told reporters after visiting the area.

The number of fatalities was updated to 24 after two bodies were determined to belong to people who had died before the fires broke out.

Meanwhile, Biobío Governor Rodrigo Díaz said he was certain about “people criminally setting fires.”

“I have reports from police, firefighters, of people who have been setting fires. I do not have indications, but certainties, we need more patrols,” he insisted in a radio interview.

“We have fire outbreaks at the southern exit of Contulmo, different places where fires were set 300 meters away from each other, I could see it, nobody told me about it. The mayor of Mulchén told me how fires were lit in the four cardinal points, I have reports from the police, the Fire Department, from people who have been setting fires. I do not have indications, but certainties, we need more patrols in the area,” he explained.

President Boric’s Regional Delegate Daniela Dresdner said eight people had been arrested for “irresponsible and suspicious attitudes with respect to the setting of fires. This was due to citizen complaints and patrols by the Navy.”

“We are asking that all these conducts be denounced and we are filing a lawsuit for all these denunciations to [be] prosecute[d],” she added.

The Biobío Regional Prosecutor’s Office called on the citizenry to e-mail all data regarding criminal behavior to fiscaliaincendios@gmail.com, including pictures, videos, audios, or written information as to the probable causes of the fires, which will be handled confidentially. (Merco Press)

World.title: Chile’s wildfires death toll reaches 24
World.content:
Chilean authorities spoke Sunday of 24 fatalities, nearly 1,000 people injured, and some 800 houses destroyed in the past five days by wildfires spreading fast in amid a highly-irregular heat wave with strong winds and temperatures above 40°C in areas 500 km south of Santiago.

The death toll reached 24 after the death of one of the injured people who had been hospitalized in Angol, Undersecretary of the Interior Manuel Monsalve explained. “The risk situation in the country remains” in the regions of Ñuble, Biobío, and La Araucanía, and in certain localities of the central region of Maule, he said. A red alert was also decreed Sunday in communes of the southern regions of Los Ríos and Los Lagos due to the appearance of new fire outbreaks. He also pointed out that 26 of the 997 people injured were in serious condition.

“I came home from work and I was already without anything, without a house. I was left on the street, with my arms crossed, now with my son, and my wife, in a tent. I have no fodder for my animals,” a resident of the town of Purén, in the Araucanía region, told Televisión Nacional de Chile (TVN).

Meanwhile, President Gabriel Boric Font attended the wake of a firefighter in the town of Coronel. ”Chile is crying with you. I am here to tell you that you are not alone, that the family of Yesenia (Muñoz, the deceased firefighter) will not be alone,” he said.

According to Chile’s National Service for Disaster Prevention and Response (Senapred), the number of fires being fought went down from 87 to 51. “We are experiencing a small window of improving weather conditions during Sunday and Monday. That means that we are not with extremely high temperatures,” Monsalve said.

Undersecretary Monsalve also told reporters that 10 people have been arrested for their responsibility in starting some of the fires for which the red alert was still maintained. Of the total number of fires, 22 occurred Sunday for a total of 283 active fires, of which 151 were under control and 71 are being fought.

Given the magnitude of the fires in size and number, international help has been summoned. “We have just sent a plane to Chile with a contingent of the Military Emergency Unit to collaborate in extinguishing and controlling the fires that are raging in the country. All our support to the Chilean people,” tweeted Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

Chile’s Foreign Ministry also said assistance was being coordinated with Argentina, Brazil, Ecuador, the United States, and Mexico, while Boric’s administration has declared a constitutional state of catastrophe in the regions of Ñuble, Biobío and La Araucanía, to speed up additional resources while restricting free transit and involving military forces to contain the disaster.

In 2017, another chain of fires destroyed some 460,000 hectares, left 11 people dead, nearly 6,000 injured, and more than 1,500 homes burned.

Monsalve also warned that this week high temperatures will continue, as well as the risk of low humidity and strong gusts of wind, which will make it difficult to extinguish the flames. – MercoPress

World.title: Parts of Chile under red alert for major forest fires in central region
World.content:
The Government of Chile has declared a “red alert” in the central part of the country due to the heat wave stemming from 39 major forest fires as the wave keeps spreading throughout the country, most of them in Araucania (17) but also in Bío Bío (7), Ñuble (7), Maule (4), Los Lagos (3), and one in the Santiago Metropolitan Region.

The National Service for Disaster Prevention and Response reported that in addition to the 39 fires currently being fought, there were four others under observation, while 141 were already under control, and 20 had already been extinguished.

Authorities ordered a series of preventive evacuations in several towns, as well as the interruption of highway traffic in the most affected areas where 181 hectares of scrubland and pastureland were burned out, threatening nearby homes.

The main cause for the fires is said to be the summer high temperatures which reached 41 degrees Celsius in the Chillán area.

Meteorologists forecast that the heat wave will last until Sunday. The last major fires to affect Chile were recorded in the summer of 2017 when the flames swept through entire villages, causing 11 deaths and more than 580 thousand hectares affected.
